CHAPTER II 
Imposition and assessment of water rate 


4. (1) Whenever the State Government is of opinion that 
lands in any area are benefited or are likely tobe benefited by 
irrigation during kKharif season, rabi season or summer .season 
by water supplied from any irrigation work, the State 00৬০1 
ment may, by notification, declare its intention to impose in 
such area a water rate for every Ahurif season, rahi geagon ون‎ 
summer seasén, as the case may be. 


(2) Such notification shall contain as full a description of 
the irrigation work as, in the opinion of the State Government, 
may be practicable and the boundaries of the area within 
which the State Government intends to impose the water rate. 


5. (1) On the publication of a notification under section 
4, any person interested in any land likely to be ‘affected by 
the imposition of the water rate may, within a .period of 
thirty days irom the date 01 publication of the said notifica- 
tion, prefer objection to the State Government against the 


intended imposition of the water rate or the inclusion of such’ 


land in ‘the area in respect of which the declaration has, beem 
made under section 4. 


(2) On the expiry of the period referred tp in sub-secsion 
(1), the State Government may, after considering the objec- 
tions, if any, declare its intention either wholly to refrain 
from imposing the water rete or to impose the same in the 
area in respect of which the declaration under section 4 was 
made or in a specified part thereof, whereupon the said area 
or the specified part thervof shall be deemed and shall 
continue to he deemed for the purposes of this Ordinance, to 
be a notified area for every Ahurif season, rabi season or 
auinmer season, as the case may he: ‘ 


Provided that the State Government may, so far as may 
be in the manner hereinbefore provided, from time to time, 
include in or exclude from any notified area any area which 
was benefited or was not benefited, as the case may be, by 
water supplied from the irrigation work. 


6. In respect of any notified area, the State Government 
may issue a notification ,proposing to umpofe water rate at 
such rates net exceeding,— 


(a) rupees thirty-two for an area of .4047 hectares for 
kKhari{f season, 

(b) rupees forty-eight for an area of .4047 hectares for 72 
season, 

(c) rupees one hundred and sixty for an area of* .4047 
hectares for summer season, 


ax may be specified in the notification and the water rate so 
imposed shall remain effective until revised by the State 
Government by a similar notification issued under this section. 

7, Notwithstanding anything to the contrary coitained 
in any other for the time being in force or in any custom, 
usage or contract, the liability for payment of water rate 
shall be on the accupiers of*lands included in the notified 
area in which the water rate is imposed:

11, All arrears of water rate together with interest, if 
any, shall be recoverable as public demand. 


12. (Z) The owners or occupiers of all lands in a notified 
area shall be bound to afford free passage to water from the 
outlet of a canal through or over lands in their possession or 
under their contro] and for that purpose to allow, when soa 
required by the Collector by order made in this behalf, the 
construction and maintenance of such field channels as may; 
be necessary. 


(2) If any person refuses to comply with an order made 
under sub-section (£) the Collector may cause the 8 
channels to be constructed or maintained and may recover the 
cost thereof from such person as public demand. 


(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law 
for the time being in force, no person shall be entitled to 
claim any compensation for any damage or loss which may ba 
caused as a result of the construction or maintenance of 
any field channel over his land under this section. 


13. (1) If any obstruction is caused in any field channel 
or canal or any cut is made on the bank thereof as a result 
of which the normal flow of water through such field channel 
or canal is diverted for the purpose of irrigating any 
particular land, the Collector may— 


(৫) take such measures as he considers necessary to 
remove such obstruction or close such cut, and 


(b) without prejudice to the provisions of section §8, 
impose a penalty, which may extend to ten times, 
the water rate assessed for the kharif season, 
rabi season or summer season, as the case may be, 
having regard to the time when the obstruction is 
put or the cut is made, on the person who is the 
owner or occupier of the land sought to be irri- 
gated by the water so diverted, after giving him 
an opportunity of showing cauSe against the im- 
position of such penalty: 


Provided that no such penalty shall be imposed on any 
person who proves to the satisfaction of the Collector that 
such obstruction was put or such cut was made without his 
knowledge or consent. 


(2) Any penalty imposed under this section shall ০০ re- 
coverable as public demand. 


(3) Any person aggrieved by an order imposing a penalty 
on him under this section may, within thirty days from the 
date of the order, appeal to such appellate authority as may 
be prescribed and the decision of the appellate authority in 
such appeal shall be final. 


14, No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall 
lie against any person for anything in good faith done or in- 
tended to be done under this Ordinance or any rule or order 
made thereunder. 


15. (7) The State Government may make rules for carry- 
ing out the purposes of this Ordinance. 


(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality , 
of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any 
of the following matters, namely: — 


(a) the manner of publication of notifications issued 
under this Ordinance;

No. 3237/MIM-117/73.—2nd July 1974,-- 
Whereas the term of four ‘years provided by clause 
(a) of sub-section (1) of section 56 of the Bengal 
Municipal Act, 1932 (Bengal Act XV of 1932), 
for which the Commissioners of the Titagarh 
Municipality, in the district of 24-Parganas, as at 
present constituted were to hold office expired on 
the 18th November 1973; 


And whereas, by Notification No. 5066/MI1M- 
117/73, dated the 14th November 1973, the said 
term was extended upto the 15th July [4 


And whereas the Governor thinks fit to extend 
the said term of office of the Commissioners of the 
said Municipality for the purpose of holding the 
general election; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by sub-section (5) of section 56 of the Bengal 
Municipal Act, 1932 (Bengal Act XV of 1932), the 
Governor is pleased hereby to extend the term of 
office of the Commissioners of the Titagarh 
Municipality for a period from the 16th July 1974 
to the 3lst March 1975 both the days inclusive.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 


ORDER 


No. 16306/F.S./FS/6P-7/74.—5th July 1974.— 
In exercise of the power conferred by section 3 of 
the West Bengal Anti-profiteering Act, 1958 (West 
Ben. Act-XXIV of 1958), the Governor is pleased 
hereby make the following order, namely:— 


1N/Short Title, Extent and Commencement.— 
(1) This order may be called the West Benyal 
Wheat Price Fixation Order, 1974. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal 
except the areas in which the West Bengal 
Rationing Order, 1964, is in force. 


(3) It shall come in to force at once. 


2. Maximum prices of wheat chargeable by 
Wholesalers and Retailers.—(1) The price at which 
wheat may be sold by a wholesaler or a retailer 
shall not exceed the rate specified below against 
each. 


Class of dealer Rate 


Wholesaler 


Retailer 


Rs. 17.00 per quintal. 
Rs. 1.78 per kilogram. 


(2) The rate specified in sub-paragraph (1) 
against wholesaler is inclusive of the cost of gunny 
bags and of all charges for bagging, sewing, 
weighing and handling for delivery at the whole- 
saler’s godown. 


(3) The rates specified in sub-paragraph (1) are 
for stocks of fair average quality, in sound 
merchantable condition, sweet, dry, clean, whole- 
some, of good food value, uniform in colour and 
size of grain, free from moulds, weevils, obnoxious 
smell, discolouration, and admixture of deleterious 
substances and conferming to the standards laid 
down in the prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 
1954 (Act 37 of 1954), and the rules made 
thereunder. 


3. Savings.—Nothing in this order shall apply 
to stocks of wheat imported by, or on behalf of, 
or on account of, or on the authority of, the Central 
Government, the State Government of West Bengal 
and the Food Corporation of India established under 
the Food Corporations Act, 1964 (Act 37 of 1964), 
and supplied by them to any person appointed for 
sale thereof. 


By order of the Governor, 
5. B. RAY, 
Sccy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

CLOSED AND SICK INDUSTRIES DEPARTMENT 
NOTIFICATIONS 


No. 2452-CSlL—5th July 1974.—Whereas by 
this department notification No. 2448-C.S.I., dated 
the 5th July 1974, issued under section 3 of the 
West Bengal Relief | Undertakings ر07(‎ 
Provisions) Act, 1972 (West Ben. Act 111 of 
1972), the unit known as Messrs. Automative 
Enterprise Limited, having registered office at No. 
34/A, Lenin Sarani in the town of Calcutta, has 
been declared to be a relief undertaking (herein- 
after referred to as the said relief undertaking); 


And whereas the State Government is satisfied 
that it is necessary and expedient so to do in the 
public interest, with a view to enabling the 
continued running of the said relief undertaking as 
a measure of preventing unemployment; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power 
conferred by section 4 of the said Act, the 
Governor is pleased hereby to direct that in relation 
to the said relief undertaking, all the enactments 
specified in the schedule to the said Act shall not 
apply and that operation of all contracts, assurances 
of property, agreements, settlements, awards, 
Standing orders or other instruments in force (to 
which the said relief undertaking is a party or which 
may be applicable to the said relief undertaking) 
immediately before the date on which the said 
relief undertaking was declared as such, together 
with all the rights, privileges, obligations and 
liabilities accruing or arising thereunder before the 
said date, but excluding contracts, assurances of 
property and agreements entered into immediately 
before the date on which the said relief undertak- 
ing was declared as such, by the said relief undertak- 
ing with the Government, the Industrial Reconstruc- 
tion Corporation of India Limited or any Bank shall 
remain suspended. 


By order of the Governor, 
N. RAY, 
Dy. Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

No. 2448-CSI.—5th July 1974—Whereas the 
unit known as Messrs Automative Enterprise 
Limited having its registered office at No. 34/A Lenin 
Sarani in the town of Calcutta is an_ industrial 
undertaking (hereinafter referred to as the said 
industrial undertaking) in respect of whose loan of 
Rs. 3,500 (Rupees three thousand and five hundred) 
from the industrial Reconstruction Corporation of 
India, a guarantee has been given by the State 
Government; 


And whereas by virtue of the provisions of sub- 
clause (b) of clause (5) of section 2 of the West 
Bengal Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) 
Act, 1972 (West Ben. Act XIII of 1972), the said 
industrial undertaking is a State industrial under- 
taking (hereinafter referred to as the said State 
industrial undertaking); 


And whereas the State Government is satisfied 
that it is necessary and expedient so to do in the 
public interest, with a view to enabling the continued 
running of the said State industrial undertaking as 
& measure of preventing unemployment; 


Now, therefore in exercise of the power conferred 
by section 3 of the said Act, the Governor is pleased 
hereby to declare that the said State industrial 
undertaking shall, on and from the 5th day of July 
1974 and for the period up to the 4th day of July 
1975 be a relief undertaking. 


By order of the Governor, 
N. RAY, 
Dy Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

“(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section 
(7), where the Central Government is satisfied

exceeding the standard rate. or decreasing the pre- 
ferential rate, in respect of an article specified in 
the First Schedule, the Central Government may, 
by notification in the Official Gazette, direct an 
amendment of the said Schedule to be made so as 
to provide for such discontinuance of, or increase 
or decrease, as the case may be, in, the preferen- 
tial rate.

(3) The auxiliary duties of customs referred to in sub-section 
(7) shall be in addition to any duties of customs chargeable on 
such goods under the Customs Act, or any other law for the 
time being in force. :

regulations made thereunder, including those relating to refunds

regulations, as the case may be.

RULES FOR COMPUTATION OF NET AGRICULTURAL INCOME 


_ Rule 1.—Agricultural income of the nature referred ta 
in sub-clause (a) of clause (1) of section 2 of the Income-tax

Act shall be computed as if it were income chargeable to 
income-tax under that Act under the head “Income fr 
other sources” and the provisions of sections 57 to 59 of that 
Act shall, so far as may be, apply accordingly: 


Provided that sub-section (2) of section 58 shall apply 
subject to the modification that the reference to section 40A, 
therein shall be construed as not including a reference to sub- 
sections (3) and (4) of section 40A. 


_ Rule 2.—Agricultural income of the nature referred to 
in sub-clause (5) or sub-clause (c) of clause (1) of section 2 of 
the Income-tax Act [other than income derived from any build- 
ing required as a dwelling house by the receiver of the rent 
or revenue or the cultivator or the receiver of rent-in-kind 
referred to in the said sub-clause (c)] shall be computed as 
if it were income chargeable to income-tax under that Act 
under the head ‘‘Profits and gains of business or profession” 
and the provisions of sections 30, 31, 32, 34, 36, 37, 38, 40, 
40A [other than sub-sections (3) and (4) thereof], 41, 43 and 
43A of the Income-tax Act shall, so far as may be, apply 
accordingly. 


Rule 3.—Agricultural income of the nature referred to 
in sub-clause (c) of clause (/) of section 2 of the Income-tax 
Act, being income derived from any building required as a 
dwelling house by the receiver of the rent or revenue or the 
cultivator or the receiver of rent-in-kind referred to in the 
said sub-clause (c) shall be computed as if it were income 
chargeable to income-tax under that Act under the head 
‘Income from house property” and the provisions of sections 
23 to 27 of that Act shall, so far as may be, apply accordingly :1 


Provided that sub-section (2) of the said section 23 shall 
apply subject to the modifications that the references to “total 
income” therein shall be construed as references to net agri- 
cultural income and that the words, figures and letter ‘and 
রা making any deduction under Chapter VIA” shall be 
omitted. 


Rule 4.—Notwithstanding anything contained in any other 
provisions of these rules, in a case where the assessee derives 
income from sale of tea grown and manufactured by him in 
India, such income shall be computed in accordance’ with 
rule 8 of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, and sixty per cent. of 
such income shall be regarded as the agricultural income of 
the assessee. 


Rule 5.—Where the assessee is a partner of a registered 
firm or an unregistered firm assessed as a registered firm under 
clause (b) of section 183 of the Income-tax Act, which in the 
previous year has any agricultural income, or is a partner of 
an unregistered firm which has not been aSsessed as a 16515" 
tered firm under clause (b) of the said section 183 and which 
in the previous year has either no income chargeable to tax 
under the TIncome-tax Act or has total income not exceeding 
the maximum amount not chargeable to tax in the case of 
an unregistered firm but has any agricultural income, then, the 
agricultural income or loss of the firm shall be computed i 
accordance with these rules and his share in the agricultural 
income or loss of the firm shall be computed in the manner 
laid down in sub-section (7), sub-section (2) and sub-section 
(3) of section 67 of the Income-tax Act and the share so 
computed shall be regarded as the agricultural income or loss 
of the assessec. 


Rule -6.—Where the assessee is a member of an associa- 
tion of persons or a body of individuals (other than a Hindu 
undivided family, a company or a firm) which in the previous 
year has either no income chargeable to tax under the Income- 
tax Act or has total income not exceeding the maximum

then, the agricultural income or loss of the association or

the share of the assessee in the agricultural income or loss 
so computed shall be regarded as the agricultural income or 
loss of the assessee. 


Rule 7.—Where the result of the computation for the 
previous year in respect of any source of agricultural income 
is a loss, such loss shall be set off against the income of the 
assessee, if any, for that previous year from any other source 
of agricultural income: 


Provided that where the assessee is a partner of an unregis- 
tered firm which has not been assessed as a registered firm 
under clause (b) of section 183 of the Income-tax Act or is a 
member of an association of persons or body of individuals 
and the share of the assessee in the agricultural income of the 
firm, association or body, as the case may be, is a loss, such 
loss shall not be set off against any income of the assessee 
from any other source of agricultural income. 


Rule 8—Any sum payable by the assessee on account of 
any tax levied by the State Government on the agricultural 
income shall be deducted in computing the agricultural income. 


Rule 9.—{(1) Where the assessee has, in the previous year 
relevant to the assessment year Commencing on the Ist day 
of April, 1975 or, if by virtue of any provision of the Income- 
tax Act, income-tax is to be charged in respect of the income 
of a period other than that previous year, in such other period, 
any agricultural income and the net result of the computation 
of the agricultural income of the assessee for the previous 
year relevant to the assessment year commencing on the Ist 
day of April, 1974 is a loss, then, for the purposes of sub- 
section (7) of section 2 of this Act, the loss so computed shall 
be set off against the agricultural income of the assessee for 
the previous year first mentioned or the period aforesaid. 


(2) Where a change has occurred in the constitution of a 
firm, nothing in sub-rule (J) shall entitle the firm to set off 
so much of the loss proportionate to the share of a retired 
or deceased partner computed in the manner laid down in 
sub-section (1), sub-section (2) and sub-section (3) of section 
67 as exceeds his share of profits, if any, of the previous year 
in the firm, or entitle any partner to the benefit of any portion 
of the said loss (computed in the manner aforesaid) which is 
not apportionable to him. 


(3) Where any person deriving any agricultural income 
from any source has been succeeded in such capacity by an- 
other person, otherwise than by inheritance, nothing in sub- 
rule (7) shall entitle any person other than the person incurr- 
ing the loss to have it set off under that sub-rule. 


(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in this rule, no 
loss which has not been determined by the Income-tax Officer 
টি provisions of these rules shall be set off under sub- 

৪ (1). 


Rule 10.—Where the net result of the computation made 
in accordance with these rules is a loss, the loss so computed 
shall be ignored and the net agricultural income shall be 
deemed to be nil. 


Rule 11.—The provisions of the Income-tax Act relating 
fo procedure for assessment (including the provisions of sec- 
tion 288A relating to rounding off of income) shall, with the

No. 6550-Cot. /1R-11(II)/72.—31st May 1974. — 


The Governor is pleased to constitute a Committae 
with the following members to go into the ques- 
tion of transfer of the Wood Industries Centres 
ut Durgapur and Kalyani under the Integrated 
Scheme for Training-cum-Production Centres fo 
Wood Industries from the Directorate of Cotta 
aud Small Seale Industries, West, Bengal, to tha 
West Bengal Housing Board: — 


(1) Shri S. K. Banerjee, Cost Accounts Officer, 
Cottage and Small Scale Industries Depart- 
ment— Member. 


(2) Shri S. Chakrabarty, Assistant Commissioner, 
West Bengal Housing Board—Member. 


(3) A representative of the Finance Department 


—Member. 

(4) A representative of the Labour Department 
—Member. 

(5) Shri P. K. Mukherjee, Joint Director of 


Industries (Rural Industries Project), West 
Bengal—Member-Secretary. 


2. The terms of reference of the Committee will 
J.C 


(a) To work out the mechanics of absorption of 
the officers, staff and workers of the Wood 
Industries Centres at Durgapur and Kalyani 
and the proportionate headquarters staff 
attached to the Integrated Scheme for 
Training-cum-Production Centres for Wood 
Industries in the West Bengal Housing 
Boanl consequent on the transfer of the 
two Centres thereto, and 


(b) To suggest ways and means for disposal of 
the accumulated stocks of the Wood Indus- 
tries Centres at Durgapur and Kalyani. 

3. The Committee shall submit its findings to 
Government by the 2]st June, 1974. 

4. Secretarial work of the Committee will be done 
by the Wood Industries Section of the Directorate of 
Cottage and Small Scale Industries, West Bengal, 
under the guidance of the Joint Director of Indus- 
tries (Rural Industries Project), West Bengal. 


Order

extraordinary issue of the Calcutta Gazette and be 
circulated to all the members of the Committee, the 


-, Housing Commissioner, Government of West Bengal, 


the Director of Cottage and Small Scale Industries, 
West Bengal, the Finance Department, the Housing 
Department, the Labour Department, the West 
Bengal Housing Board.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF PANCHAYATS 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 11058AZP.—10th July 1974.—The following regulations made, with 
the previous approval of the State Government, by the Cooch Behar Zilla 
Parishad under sub-clause (b) of clause (1) of section 113 of the West Bengal 
Zilla Parishads Act, 1963 (West Bengal Act XXXV of 1963) and after previous 
publication as required by sub-clause (a) of clause (1) of rule 135 of the West 
Bengal Zilla Parishads (Election, Constitution and Administration) Rules, 1964, 
is hereby published as required by sub-clause &*) of clause (7) of the said rule. 


1. Short title: These regulations may be called the Cooch Behar Zilla 
Parishad (Management of Provident Fund) Regulations, 1974. 


2. Definitiona: In these regulations,— 


(a) “Depositor” means a servant on whose behalf a deposit is made under 
these rules; 


(b) “Due notice of resignation of appointment” means— 
(i) in the case of servants drawing Rs. 200 a month and over, three 
months, and 
(ii) in the case of all other servants, one month; 


(c) “Interest” means the interest which is paid on a deposit at a Government 
Savings Bank under the rules in force for such institution and 
includes that allowed on Government and other securitics; 


(d) “Salary” comprises monthly substantive pay, special pay or any 
allowance drawn during leave of any kind and includes acting, 
charge, personal, deputation or duty allowance, if any, but shall not 
include 190৪8] or travelling allowance or any other allowance;

1346(2) 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, eXTRAORDINARY, JULY 15, 1974 


¥ 


سے ہے শিল্ী পিপি‏ جو NS RE Ny 2 ২৮ পপ‏ ےہ ہے ہے شر a a PI কপির (আপ ng ae ae A‏ شس و 
ee‏ 


(ec) “Servant” includes every non-pensionable employee holding a 
substantive appointment under the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad but 
excludes those who are or may in future be treated by Government 
as non-pensionable if in Government service: 


Provided that the persons to whom the existing pension and gratuity rules 
issued under Government circular No. 16L.S.G., dated 19th March, 
1903, are applicable, may in lieu of enjoying the benefits of these 
rules elect to come under the Provident Fund rules at their option 
and the option once exercised shall be final : 


Provided further that all officers in temporary service are, with the consent 
of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad embodied in a formal resolution 
at a meeting, eligible to subscribe to the fund, if they have been 
employed or, in the opinion of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad, arc 
likely to be employed for at least three years : 


Provided also that persons appointed on probation to substantive appoint- 
ments or appointed to officiate in an office which is vacant, or the 
permanent incumbent of which does not draw any part of the pay 
or count service may, if they are confirmed without interrupption 
be allowed to join the Provident Fund with retrospective effect from 
the date of their joining the service. The monthly subscriptions to 
the Fund shall not in such a case be less than 10 per cent. on the 
salary of the officer till all arrear subscriptions are paid up: 


Provided also that a servant, while on temporary transfer to service under 
some other local fund or Government, may also subscribe to the 
Provident Fnnd. 


3. Rate and realization of subscriptions: Every setvant after completion 
of one year’s service to Zilla Parishad shall be required to subscribe at the rate 
of 8.5 per cent. on his salary to a Provident Fund of which an account will be 
opend at the Post-office Savings Bank. This deduction shall be made by the 
Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad upon every salary bill presented, and the net salary 
only shall be paid to the servant. In making this deduction fractions of a rupee 
of salary may be omitted. The subscription of a servant, while on temporary 
transfer to service under some other Local Fund or Government, shall be 
calculated_on his assumed pay [articles 767 and 768, Civil Service Regulations, 
Fifth Edition (Reprint)], and it will be the duty of the servant on transfer to remit 
the subscription to his original employer for credit to the Provident Fund. 


A servant who desires to subscribe during leave must notify his intention 
beforehand, in oredr to allow for the deductions from his leave allowance being 
noted in his leave and pay certificate. He will not be permitted to discontinue 
subscriptions during leave. 


A servant who fails to notify his intention to continue to subscribe, when 
proceeding on leave, can subsequently pay his subscription in cash. : 


4. Prohibition of voluntary deposits: No voluntary deposits from servants 
will be credited to the Provident Fund. 


5. Subscription during leave and suspension: Subscription on 199৮০ of any 
kind will be optional. They will be calculated on the allowances admissible 
during leave. 


A servant on reinstatement, after a period passed under suspension, may be 
allowed the option of subscribing for that period. In the case of a servant who 
exercises the option of subscribing to the Fund during د16‎ ٥٥ without allowances, 
or on reinstatement after a period passed under suspension without allowances, 
it is left to the discretion of the Finance and Establishment Standing Committee 
to determine in each case the amount of which subscription should be paid, 
the general principle to be observed being that the subscription should be 
calculated on half the salary last drawn by the servant before he proceeded on 
leave without allowances, or was placed under suspension without allowances. 


6. Cortribution by the Zilla Parishad to deposit account of each servant : 
It shall be competent to the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad to make contribution

to the deposit account of each servant equal to, but not exceeding the deduction 
made from his salary under regulation 3. Provided that, if the total of the 
contributions shown in the bill on which remittance is made to the Savings 
Bank contains a fraction of a rupee, it may be increased to the next highest 
rupee by an addition to the bill of the difference between this fraction and 
unity. These provisional increases in the contribution will be shown in the 
abstract of balance until adjusted at the close of the year (see rules 20 and 21 
below), but they will not appear in the depositor’s ledger accounts. 


No contribution shall be made by the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad on the 
subscription paid by the depositor for any period during which he had been 
On suspension as a penalty for misconduct or other offences. 


It will be optional with Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad to contribute for an 
employee while on temporary transfer to service under some other Local Fund 
or Government. 


7. Additional contribution: (1) When any servant retires or dies who has 
subscribed to the Provident Fund and has rendered continuous good service for 
not less than ten ycars, the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad may grant to him or to 
his estate from the Zilla Parishad Fund an additional contribution which should, 
if the finances of the Zilla Parishad permit, be calculated at the rate of half 
a month’s pay for cach completed year of service rendered by him, subject to 
a maximum of fifteen month’s pay. 


(2) If such servant has died before retirement or after retirement but before 
receiving the contribution, the contribution shall be paid in the manner laid 
down in regulation 15. 


(3) For the purpose of this rule— 


(a) “retirement” means retirement— 
(i) on attaining the age of 58 years, 


(ii) at a later age if an extension of service has been duly sanctioned, 
and 


(iii) at an earlier age, on account of physical unfitness, illness, abolition 
of an appointment or any other reason considered adequate by 
the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad, provided that if the retirement 
be voluntary retirement or resignation, it must be with the consent 
and approval of the authority empowered to appoint the servant; 


(b) “continuous service” includes any authorised lcave of absence whether 
with or without allowances and any overstayal of leave that was 
condoned at the time by the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad; 


(০) “Pay” means substantive Pay (i.e., the pay other than special pay, 
personal pay or other emoluments classcd as pay) to which an 
employee is entitled on account of a post to which he has becn 
appointed substantively, or by reason of his substantive position in 
a cadre. 


(d) when the completed years of service rendered are being calculated, 
period spent on leave other than privilege leave or leave on full 
average pay shall be excluded. 


(4) An additional contribution cannot be claimed by any subscriber to the 
Provident Fund as a matter of right. It should be granted at the discretion of 
the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad only to those subscribers whom they consider 
deserving. 


8. Investment: The deductions under regulation 3 and the contributions 
under regulation 6 shall be paid to the postmaster for credit to the account of 
the Provident Fund in the Savings Bank. The payment of the deduction shall 
be debited in the accounts to the same head as the salary, and the contributions 
shall be charged to the service head “Superannuation Allowances and Pensions”, 
sub-head “Provident Fund Contribution”. The remittances to the Savings Bank 
should whenever possible be made between the first and fourth of each month 
in order that interest may accrue for the month of deposit.

9. (1) Deposits on account of the Provident Fund or the Local Fund of 
employees may be made under rule 44(c) of the Savings Bank Rules (see Indian 
Postal Guide, April, 1971); the usual limitation of the total amount at credit 
of each account do not apply to such deposits [rule 44(g)]. When the invest- 
ment of any portion of the amount of the balance at credit of the account is 
found desirable, the amount shall, on application by the Chairman, be with- 
drawn, and the investment shall be made either through the Postal authorities or 
through other agencies, as may be deemed convenient by the Chairman, in 
Government loans, Municipal Debentures or Port Trust Bonds of Calcutta, 
Bombay or Madras or in the fixed deposit in the State Bank of India or in a 
Co-operative Bank specially approved for the purpose of the Registrar of 
Co-operative Societies, provided that in case of investment in a Co-operative 
Bank at least three-fourths of the subscribers are in favour of such investment. 


(2) The interest will be drawn by the post-office in the case of investment 
through Postal authorities, or by the Chairman in case of investment through 
other agencies, and credited in the Savings Bank account. 


(3) The actual cost of purchases of such securities or the amount of such 
fixed deposits shall be added to the balance in the Savings Bank to obtain in 
total balance of the Provident Fund ledger. When any such securities are sold 
or any loss of such fixed deposits is caused by the failure of the Bank in which 
such deposits are made, the net gain or loss shall be added to or deducted from 
the net excess interest calculated for that year [see regulation 2201)] before 
apportioning such interest among the depositors as set forth in that rule. 


10. Advances for special purposes: (1) No final withdrawal will be 
allowed until the depositor quits the service or dies, but when the pecuniary 
circumstances of a depositor are such that the indulgence is absolutely necessary, 
a temporary advance may be allowed from the sum at his credit with the 
sanction of the Chairman of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad when the depositor 
draws a salary below Rs. 76 and that of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad at a 
meeting wlien his salary is Rs. 76 or over. Such an advance shall not exceed 
the amount subscribed by the depositor, except in special cases, e.g. when the 
necessity for the advance is great and the sum subscribed by him is insufficient 
for the expenses to be incurred. 


(2) The-following are examples of occasions on which the grant of advances 
may be considered, provided the circumstances are exceptional : 


(a) to pay expenses incurred in connection with illness of a depositor or 
any of his dependants; 


(b) to pay for the passage of any dependant of a depositor coming from 
beyond the sea to join him, or requiring to make a journey beyond 
the sea for some urgent cause; and 


(c) to pay expenses in connection with marriages, funerals or ceremonies 
which by the religion of the depositor it is incumbent upon him to 
perform, and in connection with which it is obligatory that expen- 
diture should be incurred. 


Note: Advances, though not confirmed rigidly to the objects laid down in 
clauses (a) to (c) above, should be made with due regard to the principle 
expsessed in clause (1) of this regulation as illustrated by the foregoing examples. 
The order sanctioning the advance should state the specific purpose for which 
the advance 15 granted. 


(3) Advance will be recovered at the discretion of the authority sanctioning 
them, in not less than 12 instalments or more than 24. A Depositor may, 
however, at his option make repayment in less than 12 instalments or may repay 
two or more instalments at the same time; Recoveries will commence from the 
first payment of the full months salary after the advance is granted or (in the 
case of advance to an officer going on leave) after the officer’s return from 
leave. The instalments will be paid by compulsory deduction from salary, and 
will be in addition to the usual subscription : 


Provided that if in the opinion of the Chairman of the Cooch Behar Zilla 
Parishad the recovery of an ordinary advance in 24 instalments is likely to cause 
excessive hardships, recovery may be made in not more than 36 instalments with 
the sanction of the Commissioner of the Division.

(4) When an advance is paid to a depositor in excess of the amount shown 
against him in column 9 of the Provident Fund ledger (a portion of his sum 
having been invested in postal cash certificates), a minus balance should be shown 
in red ink in column 9 till it is wiped off by subsequent payment of subscription, 
contribution, etc.; and, similarly, a minus entry in red ink should be made in 
column 12 of the ledger for interest at 24 per cent. or at such rate as may be 
allowed at the time by the Post-office Savings Bank on the debit balance in 
column 9. If, however, the advance is to be paid by the sale of a poprtion of 
the investment either in Government promissory notes, bonds or postal cash 
certificates, etc., the loss, if any, by this sale should be recovered from the 
depositor taking the advance. 


(5) When an advance is repayable as regards principal in not more than 12 
instalments, an additional instalment representing interest and equivalent to 3 
per cent. of the total amount of the advance should be paid in the month 
following that in which the last instalment is paid. Similarly, two additional 
instalments representing interest each equivalent to 3 per cent. of the total 
amount of the advance should be paid when the advance is repayable in more 
than 12 instalments. In either case, the instalment of interest, when realised, 
should be credited to the account of the depositor himself. 


11. In the following cases a depositor may be permitted to withdraw the 
deposits up to 90 per cent. of his own subscription with interest at his credit 
before the actual date of his retirement on the conditions laid down against each: 


(1) A subscriber proceeding on leave preparatory to retirement at any time 
between the date of his proceeding on leave and the date of 
retirement, subject, however, to the condition that he will be 
required, should he return to duty at the end of his leave, to repay 
to the Fund in one or more instalments the whole amount withdrawn 
by him with interest thereon, unless his active service actually 
terminates within six months. 


(2) A subscriber who produces a medical certificate of incapacity for further 
service, at any time between the date of his producing such certificate 
and the date of retirement. 


In both the cases referred to above the previous sanction of the Cooch Behar 
Zilla Parishad at a meeting should be obtained and no refund shall be made until 
the Chairman after due enquiry certifies that no dues are outstanding against the 
depositor. 


12. Withdrawals on retirement: (1) When a depositor in permanent 
employ ceases to be a servant of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad by resignation, 
retirement, reduction of establishment, or by permanent transfer to service under 
some other 10091 fund or to Government service, the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad 
at a mectirg shall cause the amount standing to his credit (1.e., the deposits and 
contributions with interest thereon) to be withdrawn and subject to rule 18 to be 
handed over to him unless the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad has received notice 
of an ussignment made before 18th February 1928, affecting the disposal of the 
amount of any portion of it; should such notice have been received the Cooch 
Behar Zilla Parisiad will hand over to the depositor only that portion of the 
amount which is not affected by the assignment or by the operation of rule 18 
and will disposc of the balance after taking the opinion of the Legal 
Remembrancer through the District Officer. 


(2) A depositor holding a temporary appointment may, subject to the same 
conditions, either withdraw the amount on the termination of his appointment 
or leave it in the Fund to be withdrawn at the time he finally 00119 the service. 


(3) If in the opinion of the Chairman of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad 
the withdrawal of interest from the Savings Bank would unduly trench upon 
the deposits at credit of the other depositors, the interest shall not be paid at 
once from the Provident Fund, but be temporarily advanced from the funds of 
the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad. The advance shall be adjusted when the 
difference between the total of the ledger balances and the balance of the 
Provident Fund in the Pass Book may be withdrawn from the Savings Bank 
under regulation 21. 

(4) In the case of final withdrawal of the cntire balance standing to the

may be advanced temporarily from the funds of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad.

13. Disposal on depositor’s death: Each depositor will as soon after he 
joins the Fund as possible be called upon by the Chairman of the Cooch Behar 
Zilla Parsshed to furnish “Form of Declaration”, showing how he wishes the 
amount of his accumulations to be disposed of on his death. A specimen of 
this form will be found at the end of these regulations. 


14. An adopted child shall be considered to be a child for the purpose of 
these rules when under the personal law of the depositor adoption is legally 
recognised as conferring the status of a natural child, but in this case only. If 
doubts 21150 in an indvidual case, the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad will take 
the opinion of the Legal Remembrancer through the District Officer and his 
opinion shall be final for the purposes of these rules. A declaration in favour 
of an adopted child is made at the depositor’s risk and can be challenged at 
any time. 


15. A depositor may in his declaration provide for the distribution of a 
portion only of the amount. Thus the Form of Declaration may mention a 
specific sum or a specific proportion of the total amount. The disposal of the 
balance will be governed by regulation 17 . 


Any Form of Declaration submitted by a depositor is revocable at any time 
and from time to time. A fresh declaration shall, subject to regulation 16, be 
operative only on being 1eceived by the Chairman of the Cooch Behar Zilla 
Parishad. On a depositor’s marriage, or remarriage, any declaration already 
submitted by him will forthwith become null and void and, unless a revised 
Form of Declaration is received, the amount of his accumulation will be dealt 
with under regulation 17. 


J£ minors are nominated in Form of Deciaration, the person or persons to 
whom sums intended for their benefit are to be paid should be stated in the 
Form of Declaration. 


16. In the event of the depositor having a dependant, he is not permitted in 
his Form of Declaration tu leave the amount of his accumulations or any part 
of it to any one who is not his dependant. Where a Form of Declaration 
purports to 108৮০ money otherwise than to a depositor’s dependant, the Chairman 
of the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad shall call upon the depositor to state whcther 
he has a dependant, and if it is found that he has one, the Form of Declaration 
shall not be accepted. A depositor who has dependants has absolute discretion 
regarding the distribution of the amount at his credit at the time of his death 
among those dependants. He may exclude any one or more of them in favour 
of another or others of them and the manner in which the distribution is to be 
made among them is also within his absolute discretion. 


17. The disposal of the balance at credit of deceased depositors is regulated 
by section 4(1) of the Provident Fund Act, 1925. 


18. The Cooch Behar Zi}la Purishad will not be bound by, or to recognise, 
any assignment or cncumbrance executed or attempted to be cieated which 
affects the disposal of the accumulations of a depositor who dies before returement.

dismissed or removed or called upon to resign on account of misconduct, cr

of or by such servant, the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad may, with the sanction 
of the Conimissioner of the Division, withhold all or any 7211 of the contribution 
alloted to him with the interes! eccrued thereon, and to pay 10 the servant only 
the balance to his credit without such contribution and the interest thereon.

service, the Cooch Behar Zilla Parishad may, with the sanction of the 
Commissioner, w:thhold a poprtion of the contribution alloted to him with interest 
bearing the same ratio to the whole amount so contributed with interest thereon, 
as the number of years required to complete a service of five years bears to five

22. (1) Calculation of the interest due on each account shall be made at 
the rate of 24 per cent. or at such rate as may be allowed at the time by the 
Post-ofice Savings Bank per annum for each calendar month on the lowest 
balance at credit of an account between the closing of the fourth day and the 
end of the month. The yearly interest thus calculated on each account shall be 
entered in column 16 of the abstract of balances prescribed in regulation 21. As 
soon, after the 30th of April, as the interest for the previous year is added by 
the post-office to the principal of the Fund and the interest on investment through 
other agencies is drawn by the Chairman and credited in the Saving Banks 
account [see rule 8(2)], the total (—) yearly interest calculated at the aforesaid 
rate of 24 per cent. or at such rate as may be allowed at the time by the Post- 
office Savings Bank and entered in the depositor’s accounts, as shown in column 
16 of the said abstract of balances, shall be deducted from the total interest (-) 
actually reccived for the year, and this excess interest (—) together with the gain 
or loss by the (+) sale of Government security, if any, during the year [see 
rule 8(3)] shall be shared by those depositors whose credits in the Provident 
Fund exceed Rs. 100 in proportion to their balances on the 31st March, provided 
that, for the purpose of calculating and adjusting against crediting to each 
00009110175 account his share of the excess interest the total balance at the 
depositor’s credit shall be taken as the nearest hundred. The interest thus 
calculated shall be added to the principal in column 9 of the depositor’s ledger 
account (see form in regulation 21), 


(2) In the case of the rost-office Five-year Cash Certificates or other certi- 
ficates, the’total amount received from the post-office shall be apportioned to 
each depositor, when the certificate matures or is cashed, in the proportion fixed 
at the time of purchase. 


(3) If any payment has to be made during the year on a depositor’s account 
the interest calculated monthly at 24 per cent. or at such rate as may be allowed 
at the time by the Post-office Savings Bank on that account shall be added to 
the principal in column 9 (see form in regulation 21) and for his proportionate 
share in the Post-office Cash Certificates, the amount due as calculated from 
the figures given at the back of the Cash Certificate shall be added. 


(4) The provisional increase to contributions under regulation 6 or -the 
temporary advance under sub-rule (4) of the regulation 12 shall be credited to 
the Zilla Parishad as a miscellaneous receipt. If however the total of the 
provisional increase and temporary advance is, or contains, a fraction of a rupee 
this fraction of a rupee shall be left in the Savings Bank for adjustment at the 
close of the following year. When the balances have been thus compared and 
adjusted, the ledger account of the next year shall be opened. 


23. A copy of this ledger account signed by the Vice-Chairman shall be 
given to each subscriber after the annual comparison and adjustment of balances. 
Subscribers must satisfy themselves as to the correctness of these accounts, and 
unless errors in them are brought to the notice of the Vice-Chairman within 
one month from the date of their receipt, no claim based on such error will be 


subsequently recognised.

closed and unless the amount at his credit be withdrawn within a certain period, 
viz., for balances of Rs, 10 and under, one year, and for balances over Rs. 10,

ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA 


NOTIFICATIONS 


Dated New Delhi, the 16th July 1974. 


No. 479/74.—Whereas the term of office of Shri 
V. V. Giri, President of India, is due to expire on 
23rd August 1974; 


And whereas under sub-section (3) of section 4 
ef the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections 
Act, 1952 (31 of 1952), the Election Commission 1s 
required to appoint the dates for the election to fill 
the office of the President of India so that it will be 
completed in time to enable the President thereby 
elected to enter upon his office on the 24th day of 
August 1974; 


Now therefore in pursuance of sub-section (1) of 
section 4 of the said Act, the Election Commission 
hereby appoints in respect of the said election— 


, (a) 30th July 1974 (Tuesday), as the last date 
for the making nominations; 


(b) 31st July 1974 (Wednesday), as the date 
for the scrutiny of nominations ; 


(c) 2nd August 1974 (Friday), as the last 
date for the withdrawal of candidatures; 
and 


(d) 17th August 1974 (Saturday), as the date 
on which a poll shall, if necessary, be 
taken. 


By order, 


A. N. Sen, 
Secretary to the Election Commission. 


Dated New Delhi, the 16th July 1974 


No. 479/74(6)I—In pursuance of rule 7 of the 
Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Rules, 
1974, the Election Commission hereby— 


(a) fixes each of the places specified in column 
1 of the table below to be a place of 
polling at the Presidential election to be 
held in accordance with its notification 
No. 479/74, dated 16th July 1974, and 


(b) with respect to each such place of polling, 
specifies in the corresponding entry in 
column 2 of the said table the group of 
electors who will be entitled to vote at 
that place.

RAJYA SABHA SECRETARIAT , 


Public Notice of Election to the office of Pres:dent of India 
Dated New Delhi, the 16th July 1974 


‘Whereas a notification under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Presidential 
and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952, for the holding of an election to fili 
the office of President of India has been issued by the Election Commission, 
I, B. N. Banerjee, the Returning Officer for such election, do hereby give notice 
that— 

(i) nomination papers may be delivered by a candidate or any one of his 
proposers or seconders to the undersigned at his office in Room 
No. 29, Ground Floor, Parliament House, New Delhi, or if he is 
unavoidably absent, to Shri S. S. Bhalerao, Assistant Returning 
Officer and Joint Secretary, Rajya Sabha Sccretariat, st the said 
office between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. on any day (other than a public 
holiday) not later than the 20th July 1974; 


(ii) each nomination paper shall be accompanied by a certified copy of 

the entry relating to the candidate in the electoral roll for the Parlia- 

mentary constituency in which the candidate is registered as an 
elector; 


(iii) every candidate shall deposit or cause to be deposited a sum of rupees 
two thousand five hundred only. This amount may be deposited 
in cash with the Returning Officer at the time of prcseniation of the 
nomination paper or deposited earlier in the Reserve Bank of India 
or in a Government Treasury and in the latter case a receipt showing 
that the said deposit of the sum has been so made is required to be 
enclosed with the nomination paper; 


(iv) forms of nomination papers may be obtained from the above said 
office at the times aforesaid; 


(v) the nomination papers, other than those rejected under sub-section (4) 
of section 5B of the Act, will be taken up for scrutiny at the said 
office in Room No. 29, Ground Floor, Parhament House, New 
Delhi, on Wednesday, the 31st July 1974, at 11 a.m., 


(vi) the notice of withdrawal of candidatures may be delivered by a 
candidate, or any one of his proposers or seconders who has been 
authorised in this behalf in writing by the candidate, to the under- 
signed at the place specified in paragraph (1) above before 3 o’clock 

in the afternoon of Friday, the 2nd August 1974, 

(vii) in the event of the election being contested, the poll will be taken 
on Saturday, the 17th August 1974, between the hours from 10 a.m. 
to 5 p.m. both inclusive, at the places of polling fixed under the 
rules. 


B. N. BANERJEE, 


Returning Officer for the Presidential Election 
and Secretary-Gencral, Rajya Sabha.

PART I—Orders and notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT 
HOME DEPARTMENT 


Political 


RESOLUTION 


No. 5798-P.—15th July 1974.—Whereas it has 
been decided to instal commemorative stones in 
Calcutta and the Community Development Blocks 
with names of martyrs and freedom fighters of the 
area inscribed thereon as a part of the 25th Indepen- 
dence Jayanti Programme; 


And whereas the question of setting up a Committee 
for preparing lists of martyrs and freedom fighters of 
Calcutta area and also for finalising sites in Calcutta 
where commemorative stones are to be installed has 
for sometime past been under the consideration of 
Government; 


Now, therefore, the Governor is pleased to direct 
that the State Advisory Committee constituted under 
the Home (Political) Department Resolution 
No. 5369-P., dated the 18th June 1973, published in 
“Calcutta Gazette, Extraordinary”, dated the 18th 
June 1973, shall. in addition to the functions enume- 
rated in the terms of reference included in the said 
Resolution, have the following further functions, 
namely;— 


OF WEST BENGAL 


(a) The Committee will select the names of 
martyrs and freedom fighters of Calcutta 
area for inscription on commemorative 
stones, taking into consideration the cases 
which have already been verified. 


(b) The Committee will finalise the sites in 
Calcutta where commemorative stones are to 
be installed. 


_ The Committee will make appropriate recommenda- 
lions to the Government of West Bengal in the Home 
(Political) Department in the light of its findings. 


The Committee will devise its own procedure and 


may call for such information and take such evidence 
as 1) may consider necessary. 


Order 


Ordered that the Resolution be published 11) the 
“Calcutta Gazette” for general information. 


Ordered also that a copy of the Resolution be for- 
warded to all the Members of the Committee and to 
811 Departments of this Goternment for information. 


By order of the Governor, 
B. R. GUPTA, 
Chief Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

for general information: — 


THE ECONOMIC OFFENCES (INAPPLICABILITY OF 
LIMITATION) ACT, 1974 
(No. 12 of 1974)

An Act to provide for the inapplicability of the provisions of 
Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 


1973 to certain economic Offences. 


BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fifth Year of 
the Republic of India as follows: —

The following Act of Parliament received the assent of 
the President on the 27th March, 1974, and is hereby published 
for general information :— 


THE GUJARAT STATE LEGISLATURE (DELEGATION OF 
POWERS) ACT, 1974 


(No. 11 of 1974) 
[27th March, 1974.] 


An Act to confer on the President the power of the Legislature 
of the State of Gujarat to make laws. 


Be it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fifth Year of 
the Republic of India as follows: — 


1. This Act may be called the Gujarat State Legislature short 
(Delegation of Powers) Act, 1974. title 


2. In this Act, “Proclamation” means the Proclamation 10987515100, 
issued on the 9th day of February, 1974, under article 356 of 
the Constitution, by the President, and published with the 
notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of 
Home Affairs No. G.S.R. 34(E) of the said date. 


3. (J) The power of the Legislature of the State of Confer- 
Gujarat to make laws, which has been declared by the Pro- ment 
clamation to be exercisable by or under the authority of مو‎ tHe 
Parliament, 1s hereby conferred on the President. dent of 


(2) In the exercise of the said power, the President may, ee 
from time to time, whether Parliament is or 1s not in session, of the 
enact, as a President's Act, a Bill containing such provisions State 
as he considers necessary: Logis- 


Provided that before enacting any such Act, the 1১155109181 6م‎ 
shall, whenever he considers it practicable to do so, consult 
a committee constituted for the purpose, consisting of thirty- 
four members of the House اہ‎ the People nominated by the 
Speaker and seventeen members of the Council of States 
nominated by the Chairman. 


(3) Every Act enacted by the President under sub-section 
(2) shall, as soon as may be after enactment, be laid before 
each House of Parliament. 


(4) Either House of Parliament may, by resolution passed 
within thirty days from the date on which the Act has been 
laid before it under sub-section (3), which period may be 
comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, direct 
any modifications to be made in the Act and if the modifica- 
tions are agrced to by the other House of Parliament during, 
the session in which the Act has been so laid before it or 
the session succeeding, such modifications shall be given 
effect to by the President by enacting an amending Act under 
sub-section (2): 


Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall affect the 
validity of the Act or of any action taken thereunder before 
it is so amended. 


Shri K. K. SUNDARAM, 
Secy. to the Govt. of ۰

the principal Act) shall have effect subject to the amendments 
specified in sections 3 to 12 (both inclusive) and the Criminal

100. (1) In any prosecution for any offence under this 
Act which requires a culpable mental state on the 
part of the accused, the court shall presume the 
existence of such mental state but it shall be a, 
defence for the accused to prove the fact that he 
had no such mental state with respect to the act 
charged as an offence in that prosecution. 


Ezxplanation.—In this section, ‘‘culpable mental state’’ 
includes intention, motive, knowledge of a fact and 
the belief in, or reason to believe, a fact. 


(2) For the purposes of this section, a fact is said to be 
proved only when the court believes it to exist 
beyond reasonable doubt and not merely when its 
existence is established by a preponderance of 
probability.’.

An Ordinance to amend tie Indian trou and Steel Company

WHEREAS the management of the undertaking of ط٥‎

Central Government, the Board of management, 
Shall be entit'ed, notwithstanding anything con- 
tained in the Companies Act, 1956, to exercise, in 
reiation to the undertaking of the company, 21] 
the powers of the Board of Directors of a com- 
pan - (including powers to dispose of any properties 
or a'sets of the company), whether such powers 
are derived from the Companies Act, 1956, or from 
the memorandum or articles of association of the 
company or from any other source. 


4. (1) There shall be an Administrator, to be appoint- 
ed by the Centra] Government, to assist the Board 
of management to manage the affairs of the under- 
taking of the company. 


(2) The Chairman or any other member of the Board of 
management may be appointed by the Central 
Government as the Administrator. 


(3) All officers and other persons emp!oyed in connection 
with the affairs of the undertaking of the company 
shall be subordinate to the Administrator. 


(4) The Acministritor sha‘l exercise, subject to the 
direction, control and supervision of the Board of 
management, such powers and discnarge such func- 
tions of manazema2nt in relation to the u.dertaking 
of the company as the Central Government may, 
specify in this behalf. 


(5) The Administrator sna!l receive from the funds of the 
undertaking of tre company such remuneration as. 
the Central Goveinment may fix. 


4D. (J) The Custodian shall, on and from the date on 
which the management of the undertaking of the 
company is taken up by the Board of management, 
vacate his office as such; but nothing in this sub- 
section shall be construed as_ prohibiting his 
uppointment as a member of the Beard of manage- 
ment or as the Administrator. 


(2) On the vacation of his office, the Custodian _ shall, 
where he is not appointed as the Administrator, 
forthwith deliver to the Administrator possessior 
of all assets and properties of the company which 
are in his possession, custody and control on the 
date immediately preceding the date on which he 
vacates his office as the Custodian.

transaction of its business at such time and place 
as it may think fit:

and shall, upon the written requisition of not less — 


than two members, call a special meeting.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


HOME DEPARTMENT 
Political 


RESOLUTION 


No. 6072P.—22nd July 1974.—In connection with 
ie grant of pension to freedom fighters and the 
18181170101) in Calcutta and the Community Develop- 
ent Blocks, of commemorative stones with names 
: martyrs and freedom fighters of the respective 
rea inscribed thereon under the Government of 
dia Scheme, the Governor 15 pleased to set up a 
pmmitte for each district with the members 
lentioned in the schedule hereunder. 


2, The terms of reference of the Committee will 
> as follows: 

(1) The Committee will scrutinise such cases of 
freedom fighters applying for pension as 
may be referred to it by the State Advisory 
Committee constituted by this Department 
resolution No. 5369P., dated the 18th June 
1973, published at page 2145 of Part I of 
the “Calcutta Gazette, Extraordinary”, 
dated the 18th June 1973. 


(ii) The Committee on being satisfied about the 
political sufferings of applicants and after 
taking such evidence as may be necessary 
will forward to the State Advisory Com- 
mittee the cases with its views as to their 
eligibility for pension under the Govern- 
ment of India Scheme. 


(iii) The Committee will prepare block-wise lists 
of martyrs and freedom fighters of the 
respective area whose names are to be 
inscribed on commemorative stones, taking 


into consideration the cases which have 
already been verified by Government and 
will make appropriate recommendations to 
the Government in the Home (Political) 
Department through the District Magistrate 
in the light of its findings. 


3. The Committee will devise its own procedure 
cnd may call for such information and take such 
evidence as it may consider necessary. 

Order 


রর Ordered that the Resolution be published in the 
Calcutta Gazette” for general information. 


Ordered further that a copy of the resolution be 
forwarded to all the members of the Committee, to 
all Departments, to all the Divisional Commissioners 
and to all the District Officers of this Government

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


OFFICE OF THE COMMISSIONER OF POLICE, 
CALCUTTA 


ORDER 


Whereas information has been received from 
credible sources that violent demonstrations are 
likely to take place resulting in large scale dis- 
turbances of the public tranquility and breach of 
the peace in the area mentioned دز‎ the schedule 
below in the suburbs of the town of Calcutta (here- 
inafter referred to as the said area) ; 


And whereas, I, S. C. Chaudhuri, Commissioner 
of Police, Calcutta, being an Executive Magistrate in 
the district of 24-Parganas, have been _ spectally 
empowered by the State Government under notifica- 
tion No. 2505-GA, dated the Ist April 1974, to act 
under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 
1973 (Act 2 of 1974); 

And whereas, in my 011 1010, there is sufficient 
ground for proceeding under the said section for 
immediate prevention of disturbances of the public 
tranquility and breach of the peace within the said 
area in the suburbs of the town of Calcutta; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 144 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1972 (Act 2 of 1974), read 
with sub-section (3) of the said section, 1, the said 
S. C. Chaudhuri, Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, 
and an Executive Magistrate in the district of 
24-Parganas, do hereby prohibit from the 26th July 
1974, until further orders, any assembly of five or 
more persons, or any procession, or the carrying of 
any lathis or other dangerous weapons, or the doing 
of any act which is likely to cause a disturbance of 
the public tranquility and breach of the peace with- 


= 


1301 


in the said area in the suburbs of the town of 


Calcutta. 
The Schedule 


The area wthin the jurisdiction of Garden Reach 
police-station in the suburbs of the town of Calcutta 
bounded— 


On the north—By Old Budge Budge Railway 
line from its junction with Hyde Road Exten- 
sion up to Majerhat Bridge ; 

On the east—By Diamond Harbour Road from 
the southern slope of Majerhat Bridge up to 
C.P.C. Drain (Diamond Harbour Road 
excluded) ; 


On the scuth—By C.P.C. drain from its junction 
with Diamond Harbour Road up to Budge 
Budge Road; and 


On the west—By Budge Budge Road from its 
junction with C.P.C. drain, Taratolla Road, 
Hyde Road Extension up to its junction with 
Old Budge Budge Railway line (all the roads 
included). 


Explanation:In this order, the “suburbs of the 
town of Calcutta’? means the suburbs of the town 
of Calcutta as defined by a_ notification under sec- 
tion 1 of the Calcutta Suburban Police Act, 1866 
(Bengal Act II of 1866). 

Given under my hand and seal this twenty-sixth 
July 1974. 


5. C. CHAUDHURI, 


Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, 
And 
Executive Magistrate, 24-Parganas.

NOTIFICATION 


No. 23.—25th July 1974.,-In exercise of powers 
conferred by sub-section (1) of section 61A of the 
Calcutta Police Act, 1866 (Ben. Act IV of 1866) and 
by sub-section (1) of section 38A of the Calcutta 
Suburban Police Act, 1866 (Ben. Act II of 1866), 
the Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, hereby pres- 
cribes with the previous sanction of the State Govern- 
ment, that the type of vehicle known as ‘Auto Rick- 
shaw’ shall not be driven or used in streets or public 
places within the limits of the town of Calcutta and 
its suburbs as defined in section 3 of the Calcutta 
Police Act, 1866 (Ben. Act IV of 1866) and in the 
notification No. 3000-PL., dated the Ist July 1960, 
published in the ‘‘Calcutta Gazette, Extraordinary”’, 
of the same date under section ] of the Calcutta 
Suburban Police Act, 1866 (Ben. Act II of 1866). 


This order shall come into force with effect from 
the date of its publication in the Official Gazette. 


Explanation: In this order, “Auto Rickshaw’ means 
a Motor Cycle or a Scooter having three wheels 
constructed for the purpose of carrying passengers.

PART V—<Acts of the Parliament of India assented to by the President and Ordinances promulgated 
by the President 


GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 


MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS 
(Legislative Department) 


THE COMPANIES (TEMPORARY RESTRICTIONS ON 
DIVIDENDS) ORDINANCE, 1974 


No. 7 oF 1974 


Promulgated by the President in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
Republic of India. 
[6% July 1974.] 


An Ordinance 


to provide, in the interests of national economic development, 
for temporary restrictions on the power of certain com- 
panies to declare dividends out of profits and for matters 
connected therewith or incidental thereto. 


WHEREAS Parliament is not in session and the President 
is satisfied that cicumstances exist which render it necessary 
for him to take immediate action; 


Now, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by 
clause (1) of article 123 of the Constitution, the President is 
pleased to promulgate the following Ordinance :— 


1. (1) This Ordinance may be called the Companies Short title, 


(Temporary Restrictions on Dividends) Ordinance, 1974. দস টে 


(2) It extends to the whole of India. 0০৮০৪ 


(3) It shall come into force at once. 
2. In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise Definitions. 
requires,— 


(a) ‘‘appointed day’’ means the day on which this Ordi- 
nance comes into force; 


1 4228 


1422) THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JULY 29, 1974 


a سے‎ 


Com- 

ies to 
Phich the 
Ordinance 
applies. 


(৮) “company” has the meaning assigned to it in the 
Companies Act, 1956, and includes a foreign com- 
pany within the meaning of section 591 of the 
Companies Act, 1956, which has made arrange- 
ments prescribed under the Income-tax Act, 196], 
for the declaration and payment of dividends 
within India; 


(c) “distributable profits”, in relation to a financial year 
of a company to which this Ordinance applies, 
means,— 


(6 one-third of the net profits of the company for that 
financial year, or 


(8) an amount required to pay twelve per cent. 
dividend on the face value of the equity shares 
of the company and dividend payable on its 
preference shares, 


whichever is lower; 


(d) “financial year” has the meaning assigned to it in 
section 2 of the Companies Act, 1956; 


(6) ‘net profits” means net profits of the company, as 
computed in accordance with the provisions of 
sections 349 and 350 of the Companies Act, 1956. 


3. This Ordinance shal] apply to the following categories 
of companies, namely : — 


(a) a company in which the public are substantially 
interested, as defined in clause (18) of section 2 
of the Income-tax Act, 1961; 


(b) a company, at least seventy-five per cent. of the share 
capital of which is, throughout the financial year 
for which any dividend is declared or paid, bene- 
ficially held by an institution or fund established 
in India for a charitable purpose, the income from 
dividend whereof is exempt from income-tax under 

» section 11 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 ; 


(c) an Indian company whose business consists mainly, 
in the construction of ships or in the manufacture 
Or processing of goods or in mining or in the 
generation or distribution of electricity or any’ 
other form of power; 


(৫) an Indian company, the value of whose capital assets, 
being machinery or plant (other than office 
appliances or road transport vehicles), as shown 
in its books on the last day of the financial year 
for which any dividend is declared or paid, is fifty 
lakhs of rupees or more ; 


fe) a company which has been exempted under sub- 
section (3) of section 104 of the Income-tax Act, 
1961, from the operation of that section. 


Ezplanation.—For the purpose of clause (c), the business 
of a company shall be deemed to consist mainly 
in the construction of ships or in the manufacture 
or processing of goods or in mining or in the 
generation or distribution of electricity or any, 
other form of power, if the income attributable 
to any of the aforesaid activities included in its 
gross total income for the relevant financial year 
is not Jess than fifty-one per cent. of such total 
income.

4. (1) For a period of two years from the appointed day, 
no company to which this Ordinance applies shall declare or 
pay dividends for any financial year exceeding, in the aggre- 
gate, its distributable profits for that financial year irrespec- 
tive of whether such declaration or payment is made out of 


the net profits of the company for that financial year or from 088 


the accumulated profits for any previous financial 
years. 


year or 


(2) In computing the aggregate amount which may be 
declared or paid as dividends in accordance with the pro- 
visions of this Ordinance for any financial year, any amount 
paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised before 
the appointed day by way of interim dividends for that 
financial year shall be taken into account; but where the 
amount of such interim dividend paid before the appointed 
day exceeds its distributable profits for the financial year for 
which the interim dividend was paid, no further dividend 
shall be declared or paid by the company for that financial 
year. 


5. Any dividend declared or paid after the appointed day 
by a company to which this Ordinance applies in excess o 
its distributable profits shall, to the extent of such excess, be 
void, and any amount paid by the company to 200 share- 
holder in excess of its distributable profits shall be recovered 
by the company and no such recovery shall be waived by 
the company. 


6. For a period of two years from the appointed day, 
no company to which this Ordinance applies shall, except 
with the previous approval of the Central Government and 
subject to such conditions and limitations as may be specified 
by the Government, pay or distribute any interim dividends 
for any financial year, whether ending before or after the 
appointed day. 


7. For a period of two years from the appointed day, na 
company to which this Ordinance applies shall, except with 
the previous approval of the Central Government,— 


(a) make any distribution out of its assets; 


(b) assume, whether conditionally or otherwise, any 
obligation to make distribution out of its assets; 


(c) grant any loan to any shareholder of the company. 


8. The provisions of this Ordinance shall have effect 
notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in 
the Companies Act, 1956, or in any other enactment (other 
than this Ordinance) or in any contract or instrument having 
effect by virtue of any enactment other than this Ordinance. 


§. Whoever contravenes any provision of this Ordinance, 
shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to 
twice the amount in relation to which such contravention has 
been made, or with both. 


10. (1) Where an offence under this Ordinance has been 
committed by a company, every person who at the time the 
offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible 
to, the company for the conduct of the business of the com- 
pany as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of 
the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and 
punished accordingly:

visions of this Ordinance, the Central Government may, by: 
order, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance, 
remove the difficulty.

No. 1807-L.—29th July , 1974.—The following Act of the West Bengal Legislature, having been assented 
to by the President, is hereby published for general information :— 


Short title. 


West Bengal Act XXXV of 1974 


THE BASUMATI PRIVATE LIMITED (ACQUISITION 
OF UNDERTAKINC) ACT, 1974. 


[Passed by the West Bengal Legislature.] 


[Assent of the President was first published in the Calcutta 
Gazette, E.wrtraordinary, of the 29th July, 1974.] 


An Act to provide for the acquisition, for public purpose, 
of the undertaking of the Basumati Private Limited with 
a view to securing the proper adtninistration and manage- 
ment thereof for the purpose of ensuring efficrent 
publication of the Basumuati, a daly newspaper ہر‎ the 
Bengali language which has a great past and tradition and 
timely publication of journals and periodicals published 
by it and resum.ng the publication of books, particularly 
Sanskrit Classics in Bengali version and other Bengali 
Classics, and also with a vieu’ to assuring the retention 
of the services of the workmen whose continued employ- 
ment has been threatened, so that the interests of the 
public may be better served. 


WHEREAS it will be useful to the public and it will result 
in benefit and advantage ito the public and having regard to 
the public utility it is expedient to provide for the acquisition 
of the undertaking of the Basumati Private Limited with a 
view to securing the proper administration and management 
thereof for the purpose of ensuring efficient publication of the 
Basumati, a daily newspaper in the Bengali language which has 
a great past and tradition and timely publication of journals and 
periodicals published by it and resuming the publication of 
books, particularly Sanskrit Classics in Bengali version and 
other Bengali Classics, and also with a view to assuring the 
retention of the services of the workmen whose continued 
employment has been threatened, so that the interests of the 
public may be better served; 

It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
Republic of India, hy the Tegislature of West Bengal, as 
follows :— 

1. This Act may be called the Basumati Private Limited 
(Acquisition of Undertaking) Act, 1974.

(Sections 2—4.) 


2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) ‘‘appointed day’? means such date as the State 
Government may, by notification, appoint: 


(৮) ‘‘Commissioner’’? means the Commissioner of Pay- 
ments appointed under section 9: 


(c) ‘‘company’’ means the Basumati Private Limited, 
being a company as defined in the Companies Act, 
1956, having its registered office at 166, Bepin 
Behari Ganguli Street, Calcutta; 


(d) ‘‘notification’’ means a notification published in the 
Oficial Gazette; 

(e) ‘‘prescribed’’ means prescribed by rules made under 
this Act; 


(f) ‘‘sacheduled bank’’ has the same meaning assigned to 
it in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and 
includes a nationalised hank; 


(9) ‘‘undertaking’’, in relation to the company, means 
the properties and assets of the company referred 
to in sub-section (7) of section 4. 


3. On and from the appointed day, the undertaking of 
the company shall, by virtue of this Act, stand transferred 
to, and vest in; the State Government free from all trusts, 
liabilities and encumbrances. 


4 (1) The undertaking of the company shall be deemed 
to include all assets, rights, powers, authorities and privileges 
and all properties, movable and immovable, machinery includ- 
ing rotaries and composing machine, reserve funds, investments 
and all other rights and interests arising out of such properties 
as were immediately before the appointed day in the ownership, 
power or control of the company in relation to the under- 
taking, or in the possession of the company irrespective of the 
fact whether the company has any right, title or interest in 
such properties or not, and all documents of whatever nature 
relating thereto but does not include the right, title and 
interest of the owners of lands and buildings in possession of 
the company, cash balance of the company and the amounts 
receivable by the company from its debtors. 


(2) Any contract, whether express or implied, or other 
arrangement, whether under any statute or otherwise, in so 
far as it relates to the management of the business and affairs 
of the company in relation to its undertaking and in force 
immediately before the appointed day, or any order made by 
any court in so far as it relates to the management of the 
business and affairs of the company in relation to its under- 
taking and in force immediately before the appointed day, 
shall be deemed to have terminated on the appointed day. 

(3) All persons in charge of the management, including 
persons holding offices as directors, managers or any other 
personnel connected with the management of the company 
immediately before the appointed day, shall be deemed to 
have vacated their offices as such on the appointed day. 

(4) Notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of 
any court, tribunal or other authority or anything contained 
in any law for the time being in force, every Receiver, Official 
Liquidator or any other person in whose possession or custody 
or under whose control the undertaking of the company or 
any part thereof may be, shall forthwith deliver possession 
of the said undertaking or such part thereof, as the case 
may be, to the State Government or to such person‘as the( 
State Government may appoint in this behalf.
