PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF PANCHAYATS 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 12220/Panch.—29th July 1974.—The following draft of rules which, in 
exercise of the power conferred by section 224 of the West Bengal Panchayat 
Act, 1973 (West Bengal Act XLI of 1973), the Governor proposes to make, is 
hereby published as required under sub-section (1) of that section for the in- 
formation of persons likely to be affected thereby. 


The draft will be taken into consideration on or after the fifteenth day from 
the date of its publication in the Official Gazette and any objection or sugges- 
tion with respect thereto which may be received by the undersigned before that 


day shall be considered. 
DRAFT RULES 
CHAPTER I 
Preliminary 


]. Short Title—These rules may be called the West Bengal Panchayat 
(Constitution) Rules, 1974. 
2. Definition—(1) In these rules,— 


(a) “Act” means the West Bengal Panchayat Act, 1973 (West Bengal Act 
XLI of 1973); 


(b) “Form” means a Form appended to these rules and includes a transla- 
tion thereof in Bengali and Nepali; 


(c) “Section” means a section of the Act; 


(2) The expressions used in these rules, but not defined shall have the 
meanings assigned to them respectively in the Act. 


(3) The Bengal General Clauses Act, 1899 (I of 1899) shall apply for inter- 


retation of these rules as it applies for the interpretation of an Act of the 
est Bengal Legislative Assembly.

CHAPTER II 


Election of Pradhan and Upa-Pradhan of Gram Panchayat 


3. (1) As soon as may be after the constitution of a Gram Panchayat is 
notified in the Official Gazette under sub-section (4) of section 4, but not later 
than fifteen days from the date of publication of the notification, the prescribed 
authority appointed for the purpose of sub-section (2) of section 9 shall call a 
meeting of all the members of such Gram Panchayat for the taking of oath and 
for the election of a Pradhan and a Upa-Pradhan of the Gram Panchayat, by 
fixing a date, place and time and causing a written notice to this effect in 
Form | to be served on each member of the Gram Panchayat at least ten days 
before the date fixed for the meeting. 


(2) Such meeting shall be presided over by such officer as may be authorised 
by the prescribed authority in Form 2, and such officer shall not be entitled to 
vote at the election. 


(3) On the date of the meeting if there is no quorum as provided for in sub- 
section (3) of section 16 the Presiding Officer shall adjourn the meeting. The 
adjourned meeting shall be held on such date, place and time as may be fixed 
by the prescribed authority and the provisions regarding notice to members of 
Gram Panchayat referred to in sub-rule (1) shall apply. 


(4) The membes who are required to take oath under section 197 shall, 
before taking the seats, make and subscribe an oath or affirmation in Form 3 
before the Presiding Officer. 


(5) The Presiding Officer shall, immediatley after the commencement of the 
meeting, satisfy all members present that the ballot box is empty and shall 
then close and seal it. The ballot box shall be placed in view of the Presiding 
Officer. 


(6) The Presiding Officer shall call upon the members present to propose 
and second the names of the candidates for election of the Pradhan of the 
Gram Panchayat. He shall record the names of the candidates proposed to- 
gether with the names of the proposers and seconders. He shall reject any 
proposal after the list of candidates has been finalised by him. 


(7) If only one candidate is proposed and seconded the Presiding Officer 
shall, in Form 4, declare him to be duly elected Pradhan of the Gram Panchayat. 
If more than one candidate have been proposed and seconded, the Presiding 
Officer shall cause to be prepared as many ballot papers as there are members 
present containing the names of candidates arranged according to the alphabeti- 
cal order of their surnames in Form 5 and hand over one such ballot paper to 
each member present after putting his initial on the back of each ballot paper. 
The Presiding Officer shall then ask each member in turn to record his vote 
at a table so placed that no other person can overlook him, by placing the mark 
“X” in the place provided for the purpose in the ballot paper opposite to the 
name of the candidate for whom he intends to vote, to fold it up and to insert 
into the ballot box. Immediately after the voting is over, the Presiding Officer 
shall open the ballot box in presence of the members present, take out the ballot 
papers therefrom, count them and record the number thereof in Form 6. The 
Presiding Officer may reject any ballot paper which, in his opinion, raises a 
reasonable doubt as to for whom the voter has cast his vote. A note to this 
effect shall be made by the Presiding Officer upon ballot paper so rejected and 
it shall not be included in the count. The Presiding Officer shall, in Form 7, 
declare the candidate who has secured the largest number of votes to be duly 
elected Pradhan of the Gram Panchayat. In case of equal number of votes 
being recorded in favour of two or more candidates, selection shall be made 
from such candidates by Jot in such manner as the Presiding Officer shall deem 
fit and thereupon the candidate thus selected shall be declared to be duly 
elected as Pradhan of the Gram Panchayat. 


(8) After the election of the Pradhan, election of the Upa-Pradhan shall be 
held in the aforesaid manner. 


MRT 1 


THE CALCUITA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JULY 30, 1974 


০০০০০০০০১২২ 


(9) The Presiding Officer shall forward the names of the Pradhan and the 
Upa-Pradhan to the prescribed authority who shall publish the same in the 
locality in such manner as he may think fit. The prescribed authority shall 
forward the names of Pradhan and Upa-Pradhn to the District Panchayat Elec- 
tion Officer, State Panchayat Election Officer and the State Government for 
information. The State Panchayat Election Officer shall publish the names of 
the Pradhan and the Upa-Pradhan in the Official Gazette. 


(10) The papers relating to the election of the Pradhan or the Upa-Pradhan 
shall be sent by the Presiding Officer to the prescribed authority for safe custody. 


The prescribed authority shall keep the papers in safe custody for six months 
after which they may be destroyed. 


CHAPTER III 


Election of Sabhapati and Sahakari Sabhapati of Panchayat Samiti 


4. (1) As soon as may be after the constitution of a Panchayat Samiti is 
notified in the Official Gazette under sub-section (3) of section 94 but not later 
than fifteen days from the date of publication of the notificaion, the prescribed 
authority appointed for the purpose of sub-section (2) of section 98 shall call 
a meeting of all the members of the Panchayat Samiti for the taking of oath 
and for the election of a Sabhapati and a Sahakari Sabhapati of the 
Panchayat Samiti, by fixing a date, place and time and by causing a written 
notice to this effect in Form 1 to be served on each member of the Panchayat 
Samiti at least ten days before the date fixd for the meetnig. 


(2) Such meetnig shall be presided over by such officer, not below the rank 
of a Gazetted Officer, as may be authorised by the prescribed authority in 
Form 2, and such officer shall not be entitled to vote at the election. 


(3) On the date of the meeting if there is no quorum as provided for in sub- 
section (3) of section 105 the Presiding Officer shall adjourn the meting. The 
adjourned meeting shall be held on such date, place and time as may be fixed 
by the prescribed authority and the provisions regarding notice to members of 
Panchayat Samiti referred to in sub-rule (1) shall apply. 


(4) The Presiding Officer shall then conduct the election of the Sabhapati 
or Sahakari Sabhapati in the same manner as laid down under sub-rules (4), 
(5), (6), (7), (8), (9) and (10) of rule 3. 


CHAPTER IV 


Election of Sabhadhipati and Sahakari Sabhadhipati of Zilla Parishad 


5. (1) As soon as may be after the constitution of a Zilla Parishad is noti- 
fied in the Official Gazette under sub-section (3) of section 140 but not later 
than fifteen days from the date of publication of the notification, the prescribed 
authority appointed for the purpose of sub-section (2) of section 143 shall call 
a meeting of all the members of the Zilla Parishad for the taking of oath and 
for the election of a Sabhadhipati and a Sahakari Sabhadhipati of the Zilla 
Parishad, by fixing a date, place and time and by causing a written notice to 
this effect in Form | to be served on each member of the Zilla Parishad at 
least ten days before the date fixed for the meeting. 


(2) Such meeting shall be presided over by such officer not below the rank 
of a Gazetted Officer, as may be authorised by the prescribed authority in Form 
2, and such officer shall not be entitled to vote at the election. 


(3) On the date of the meeting if there is no quorum as provided for in sub- 
section (3) of section 150 the Presiding Officer shall adjourn the meeting. The 
adjourned meeting shall be held on such date, place and time as may be fixed 
by the prescribed authority and the provisions regarding notice to members 
of Zilla Parishad as referred to in sub-rule (1) shall apply. 


(4) The Presiding Officer shall then conduct the election of the Sabhadhipati 
or Sahakari Sabhadhipati in the same manner as laid down under sub-rules (4), 
(5), (6), (7), (8), (9) and (10) of rule 3.

CHAPTER VI 


Election of members of Sthayee Samiti of Panchayat Samiti 


7. (1) Within one week from the date of election of the Sabhapat: of a 
Panchayat Samiti the Subdivisional Officer shall call a meeting of the members 
of the Panchayat Samiti for election under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of 
section 124, of members of the Sthayee Samitis by fixing a date, time and 
place and by causing a written notice thereof in Form 1 to be served on each 
member of the Panchayat Samiti at least ten days before the date fixed for 
the purpose. 


(2) Such meeting shall be presided over by such officer not below the rank 
of a Gazetted Officer as may be authorised by the Subdivisional Officer in 
Form 2 and such Officer shall not be entitled to vote at the election. 


(3) If on the date of the meeting there is no quorum, the Presiding Officer 
shall adjourn the meeting which shall be held on a date to be fixed by the 
Subdivisional Officer. The adjourned meeting shall be held on such date, 
place and time as may be fixed by the Subdivisional Officer and the provisions 
regarding notice to members of Panchayat Samiti referred to in sub-rule (1) 
shall apply. 


(4) The Presiding Officer shall immediately after the commencement of 
the meeting satisfy all the members present that the ballot boxes are empty 
and shall then close and seal them. There shal] be as many ballot boxes as 
there are Sthayee Samitis to be constituted, each ballot box bearing a label 
mentioning the name of Sthayee Samiti for which it is meant. The ballot box 
shall be placed in the view of the Presiding Officer. 


(5) The election of Sthayee Samiti shall be conducted one after another 
in the same order as mentioned in sub-section (1) of section 124. 


(6) The Presiding Officer shall call upon the members present to propose 
and second the names of candidates for election as members of a Sthayee 
Samiti. He shall record the names of the candidates proposed for the Sthayee 
Samiti together with the names of their proposers and seconders. If the 
number of candidates proposed and seconded for a Sthayee Samiti is equal to, 
or less, than the number of seats prescribed under rule 6 the Presiding Officer 
Sekt declare them in Form 4 to be duly elected members of the Sthayee 

miti. 


(7) When the number of candidates declared to be elected under sub-rule 
(6) is less than the number of seats prescribed, the Subdivisional Officer shall 
call a meeting of members of the Panchayat Samiti for a fresh election to 


. complete the number and the provisions regarding notice to members referred 


to in sub-rule (1) shall apply.

(8) If more than the prescribed number of seats are proposed and 
seconded for a Sthayee Samiti, the Presiding Officer shall cause to be prepared 
as many ballot papers in Form 5 as there are members present, each ballot 
paper bearing the name of the Sthayee Samiti and containing the names of 
the candidates arranged according to their surnames for election to the 
Sthayee Samiti. 


(9) The Presiding Officer shall hand over the ballot paper to each member 
present after putting his initials on the back of each such ballot paper. He 
Shall then ask each member to record his vote at a table so placed that no 
other person can overlook him by placing the mark “X” in the place provided 
for the purpose in the ballot paper opposite to the name of the candidate or 
candidates for whom the member intends to vote, to fold it up and to insert 
it into the ballot box bearing the label of the Sthayee Samiti concerned. 


(10) Immediately after voting is over the Presiding Officer shall open the 
ballot box in the presence of the members, take out the ballot papers there- 
from, count them and record the number thereof in Form 6. 


(11) The Presiding Officer may reject any ballot paper which, in his 
opinion, raises a reasonable doubt as to for whom the voter cast the vote, 
after recording a note to this effect on the ballot papers so rejected. He shall 
in Form 7 declare the prescribed number of candidates who have secured the 
larger number of votes in order of merit to be duly elected as membes of the 
Sthayee Samiti concerned. 


(12) In case of an equal number of votes recorded in favour of two or 
more candidates selection shall be made of such candidates by lot in such 
manner as the Presiding Officer shall deem fit and thereupon the candidates 
سا‎ selected shall be declared to be duly elected as member of the Sthayee 

amiti. 


(13) As soon as election of members to all the Sthayee Samitis is com- 
pleted in the aforesaid manner the Presiding Officer shall forthwith forward 
the names of elected members of all the Sthayee Samitis to the Sabhapati of 
Panchayat Samiti and to the Subdivisional Officer for publication in their 
offices. The Subdivisional Officer shall forward the names of elected members 
of all the Sthayee Samitis to the District Panchayat Election Officer, State 
Panchayat Election Officer and the State Government for information. The 
State Panchayat Election Officer shall publish the names of the members of 
the Sthayee Samiti in the Official Gazette. 


(14) The papers relating to the election of members to Sthayee Samitis of 
the Panchayat Samiti shall be sent to the Subdivisional Officer for safe custody. 
The Subdivisional Officer shall keep the papers in safe custody for three 
months after which they may be destroyed. 


CHAPTER VII 


Election of Karmadhyaksha of a Sthayee Samiti of Panchayat Samiti 


8. (1) Within one week from the date of the election of members of a 
Sthayee Samiti under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 124, the Subdivi- 
sional Officer shall by a notice in Form 1 call a meeting of the members of 
each Sthayee Samiti other than members appointed under clause (c) of sub- 
section (2) of that section for the election of a Karmadhyaksha. 


(2) The election meeting shall be presided over by an officer not below the 
rank of Gazetted Officer as may be authorised by the Subdivisional Officer in 
Form 2. Such officer shall not be entitled to vote at the election. 


(3) The election of the Karmadhyaksha of the Sthayee Samiti shall be con- 
ducted in the same manner as laid down under sub-rules (3), (5), (6), (7) of 
rule 3 as far as applicable: 


Provided that one-half of the total number of members of the Sthayee 
Samiti shall form a quorum for the meeting.

CHAPTER IX 


Election of members of Sthayee Samitis of Zilla Parishad 


10. (1). Within one week from the date of election of the Sabhadhipati 
of a Zilla Parishad the District Magistrate shall call a meeting of the members 
of the Zilla Parishad for election of members of the Sthayee Samitis by fixing 
a date, time and place and by causing a written notice thereof in Form 1 to 
be served on each member of the Zilla Parishad at least ten days before the 
date fixed for the purpose. 


(2) The election meeting shall be presided over by an officer not below 
the rank of a Gazetted Officer authorised in this behalf in Form 2 by the 
District Magistrate. Such officer shall not be entitled to vote at this election. 


(3) The election shall be conducted, as far as possible, in the manner as 
laid down under sub-rules (3) to (12) of rule 7. 


(4) As soon as election of members to all Sthayee Samitis is completed the 
Presiding Officer shall forward to the District Magistrate and the Sabhadhipati 
of the Zilla Parishad, the names of the candidates elected as members of each 
Sthayee Samiti for publication in their offices. The District Magistrate shall 
forward these names of elected members of Sthayee Samitis to the District 
Panchayat Election Officer, the State Panchayat Election Officer and the State 
Government for information. The State Panchayat Election Officer shall 
pee the names of the members of the Sthayee Samiti in the Official 

azette. 


(5) The papers relating to the election of members to the Sthayee Samitis 
shal] be sent to the District Magistrate for safe custody. The District 
Magistrate shall keep the papers in safe custody for three months after which 
they may be destroyed.

CHAPTER X 


Election of Karmadhyaksha of Sthayee Samiti of Zilla Parishad 


11. (1) Within one week from the date of the election of members of 
Sthayee Samiti under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 17] the District 
Magistrate shall, by a notice in Form 1, call a meeting of the members of 
each Sthayee Samiti other than the members appointed under clause (c) of 
sub-section (2) of that section for the election of a Karmadhyaksha. 


(2) The election meeting shall be presided over by such officer, not below 
the rank of a Gazetted Officer, as may be authorised in this behalf, in Form 2 
by the District Magistrate. Such officer shall not be entitled to vote at the 
election. 


_ (3) The election of Karmadhyaksha of a Sthayee Samiti shall be conducted 
in the same manner: as laid down under sub-rules (3), (5), (6) and (7) of rule 
3 as far as applicable: 


Provided that one-half of the members of a Sthayee Samiti shall form a 
quorum for the meeting. 


(4) The Presiding Officer shall send the name of the Karmadhyaksha of 
each Sthayee Samiti to the Sabhadhipati of the Zilla Parishad and the District 
Magistrate who shall forward the same to the District Panchayat Election 
Officer, the State Panchayat Election Officer and the State Government for 
information. The State Panchayat Election Officer shall publish the name of 
Karmadhyaksha in the Official Gazette. 


(5) The Presiding Officer shall send the papers relating to the election of 
Karmadhyaksha to a Sthayee Samiti of a Zilla Parishad to the District 
Magistrate for safe custody. The District Magistrate shall keep the papers in 
safe custody for three months after which they may be destroyed. 


(6) The names of Karmadhyaksha along with the names of the members 
of each Sthayee Samiti shall then be published in the offices of the Zilla 
Parishad and the District Magistrate. 


CHAPTER XI 


Resignation of and filling up of casual vacancy in the office of the 
Karmadhyaksha or any member of a Sthayee Samiti, of a Panchayat 
Samiti or a Zilla Parishad. 


12. (1) The Karmadhyaksa or any member of a Sthayee Samiti of a 
Panchayat Samiti may resign his office by notifying in writing his intention 
to do so to the Subdivisional Officer and shall vacate his office on such resigna- 
tion being accepted by the said officer. 


(2) The KarmadhyakslHa or any member of a Sthayee Samiti of a Zilla 
Parishad may resign his office by notifying in writing his intention to do so 
to the District Magistrate and shall vacate his office on such resignation being 
accepted by the said officer. 


13. (1) Any casual vacancy in the office of the Karmadhyaksha of a 
Sthayee Samiti of a Panchayati Samiti or a Zilla Parishad by death, resigna- 
tion, removal or otherwise shall be filled by election in the manner laid down 
in rules 8 or 11 as the case may be. 


(2) When a casual vacancy in the office of a Karmadhyakshya of a Sthayee 
Samiti of a Panchayat Samiti occurs, the Subdivisional Officer shall by a notice 
in Form 1 call a meeting within thirty days from the date of the casual 
vacancy of the members of the Sthayee Samiti for election of a 
Karmadhyaksha.

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


oe 


EDUCATION DEPARTMENT 
Secondary 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 864Edn(S)/8B-8/74.—23rd July 1974.—In exercise of the power 
conferred by rule 33 of the Management of Recognised Non-Government 
Institutions (Aided and Unaided) Rules, 1969, the Governor, on the application 
of Ramakrishna Sarada Mission, Dakshineswar, on behalf of a class of Institu- 
tions to which the provisions of article 26A of the Constitution of India apply, 
is pleased hereby to make the following other rules for the composition, 
eee function of the Managing Committees of such class of Institution, 
namely: 


Rules 


1. Short title, application and commencement: (1) These rules may be 
called the Special Rules for the Management of Ramakrishna Sarada Mission 
(Dakshineswar) Schools. 


(2) They shall apply to the Secondary School specified in the Schedule run 
by the Ramakrishna Sarada Mission, Dakshineswar. 


(3) They shall come into force with effect from the date of their publication 
in the Calcutta Gazette. 


2. Definitions: In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) “Ramakrishna Sarada Mission” (hereinafter referred to as the Mission) 
means the Association constituted by the Memorandum of Associa- 
tion dated the 7th day of May, 1960, and registered under the Socie- 
ties Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860), on the 13th May, 1960 and 
deemed to have been registered under the West Bengal Societies 
Registration Act, 1961 (West Bengal Act XAVI of 1961). 


(b) ‘‘Governing Body” means the Governing Body of the Mission. 


(c) “School Committee” means the Managing Committee of a school 
constituted under these Rules. 


(d) “Branch Managing Committee” means the Managing Committee of a 
Branch centre of the Mission appointed by the Governing Body.

(e) “Employee” includes a member of both teaching and non-teaching 
staff of the respective school. 


_ 3. School Committee: (1) Every school founded by the Mission and recog- 
nised under the provisions of the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education 
Act, 1963 (West Ben. Act V of 1963), shall have a School Committee for its 
proper management. 


(2) The School Committee shall consist of not more than twelve members 
and there shall be a Sub-Committee appointed by the Branch Managing Com- 
mittee and approved by Governing Body. 


(3) The School Committee shall be constituted as follows: 


(i) Representative of the Branch Managing Committee of whom 


one shall be its Secretary 3 
(ii) Representatives of donors, benefactors and persons, interested 
in education, owing allegiance to the aims and ideals of the 

Mission 7 as = 3 

(iii) Guardians’ representative و ہیی‎ 
(iv) Teachers’ representatives to be selected by rotation according 
to seniority from amongst the teaching staff (for one year 

each) 2 کی‎ ne se ہت‎ “al 

(v) Headmistress or Principal (ex officio) ee, ہپ ےہ‎ তত 
(vi) An officer of the State Government, nominated by the Direc- 
tor of Public Instruction, West Bengal, or by an officer 
authorised by him in this behalf... ve va 

Total 7۰ 332 


Provided that in the case of residential institutions having students from 
far off places, the teachers and wardens looking after the students in their 
hostels may also be nominated as Guardians’ representatives: 


Provided further that in the case of Junior High Schools, there shall be only 
one Teachers’ representative. 


(4) The Branch Managing Committee shall appoint from amongst the mem- 
bers of the School.Committee a President, a Vice-President, and a Secreta 
{who will be the Secretary of the Branch Managing Committee). The Head- 
mistress or the Principal shall be the ex officio Assistant Secretary. 


4. The Committee to act notwithstanding vacancies: The Committee shall 
have power to act notwithstanding any vacancy in the membership thereof. 


5. Term of office of the Committee: The Committee shall hold office for 
not more than two years, but the period may be extended by the Governing 
Body at its discretion. 


6. Power to supersede Committee: The Governing Body of the Mission 
may, if in its opinion there are sufficient grounds so to do, supersede the School 
Committee and appoint an ad hoc Committee or a suitable person to discharge 
all the functions and exercise all the powers of the Schoo! Committee pending 
its reconstitution. In such cases the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education 
and the Director of Public Instruction, West Bengal, shall be duly informed. 


7. Casual vacancy: The Branch Managing Committee shall, with the 
approval of the Governing Body, fill all casual vacancies in the Committee by 
nomination or selection, as the case may be, of persons‘belonging to the cate- 
Bory or categories in respect of which the vacancies arise. Persons so appointed 
shall hold office for the remainder of the term of office of the School 
Committee. 


8. Vacancy caused by absence: If anv member of the School Committee 
absents himself from four consecutive meetings without sufficient reasons, the 
Branch Managing Committee may replace him by appointing a person belong- 
ing e the category to which the member belongs, in the manner specihed in 
rule 7, 


۶۸۶۳۲ 1] THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JULY 30, 1974 1451 
০০০০০ সত ain ee a -- بسح‎ rs chen ০০ 
9. Quorum: Five members shall form a quorum. 


10. Committee meetings: The Secretary or in his absence, the Assistant 
Secretary shall call a meeting of the Committee at least once in two months 
except during vacations. At least seven clear days’ notice shall be given for 
Calling a meeting of the Committee. 


11. Special meeting: A special meeting may be called by the Secretary 
on the requisition of not less than four members of the Committee. At least 
three days’ clear notice shall be given for calling a special meeting. 


12. Emergency meetings: The President may call an emergency meeting 
of the Committee after giving at least 24 hours’ notice. 


_ 13. Confirmation of proceedings: All resolutions passed at ordinary meet- 
ings, special meetings or emergency meetings shall be subject to confirmation 
or revision at the next ordinary meeting. 


14. Agenda: The Secretary shall prepare the agenda in consultation with 
the Headmistress or the Principal. No matter outside the agenda shall be 
discussed at the meeting without the permission of the Chairman. 


15. Presdent or Vice-President to preside: The President or in his 
absence, the Vice-President shall preside over the meetings of the Committee. 
In the absence of both the President and the Vice-President, the members 
present shall elect one amongst themselves as Chairman. 


16. Casting vote: All questions before a meeting of the Committee shall 
be decided by a majority of votes. In case of equality of votes, the Chairman 
shall have a casting vote in addition to his ordinary vote. 


17. Place of meetings: All meetings of the Committee shall be held at the 
premises of the Institution unless otherwise decided by the Comniittee itself 
or by the President in consultation with the Secretary. 


18. Finance and Audit: (1) Subject to the condition that the ultimate 
financial and administrative responsibility of the school shall rest with the 
Governing Body, the Committee shall be responsible for the finances of the 
Institution and shall— 


(a) see that accounts are maintained properly, 
(b) pgepare budget estimates in time, 

(c) consider the audit report, 

(d) check all bills, 

{e) invite tenders, 

(f) place work orders, 

(g) scrutinise vouchers: 


Provided that the Committee may delegate any of these powers to the 
Secretary or the Assistant Secretary to be exercised by him subject to the 


general control and supervision of the Committee. 


(2) The accounts of the Institution shall be audited every year by an 
Auditor appointed by the Managing Committee from a panel approved by the 
State Government and the Governing Body. 


(3) The Auditor's report shall be taken into consideration at the first 
ordinary meeting of the Committee held after the receipt of the report. Copies 
of the report shall thereafter be sent to the Education Department of the 
State Government, the Director of Public Instruction, West Bengal, and the 
West Bengal Board of Secondary Education, together with a note on the action 


taken thereon. 

(4) The Government may call fo. an explanation of any irregularity dis- 
closed by the Auditor’s report and may give such directions as it may deem 
fit in the circumstances of the case.

19, Duties of Secretary and Assistant Secretary: (a) All correspondence 
for and on behalf of the Committee shall be carried on by the Secretary under 
the direction of the Committee. The Secretary shall keep a report of the 
proceedings of the Committee in a book maintained for the purpose. 


(b) The Assistant Secretary shall perform such duties as may be assigned 
to her by the Committee and shall in the absence of the Secretary perform 
the duties of the Secretary. 


20. When President can convene a meeting: In the temporary absence of 
the Secretary and the Assistant Secretary, the President may convene a meet- 
ing of the Committee. 


21. Documents: (i) The Secretary of the School Committee, by virtue of 
her position as the ‘Secretary of the Branch Managing Committee, shall be in 
charge of the invested funds, title deeds and other legal documents in respect 
of the properties acquired for the school and vesting in the Governing Body. 


(ii) All books, records and registers relating to the institution may be made 
available for inspection by the members of the School Committee or any 
person authorised by the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education, the 
Education Directorate or the Education Department. 


(iii) Unless otherwise directed by the Branch Managing Committee, the 
accounts of the Institution shall be operated jointly by the Secretary and 
the Assistant Secretary and all bank transactions shall, be carried out over the 
signature of the Secretary. 


22. Powers of the School Committee: (1) The School Committee shall 
have the power— 


(a) to appoint teachers and other employees, both permanent and tempo- 
rary, salaried or honorary, and for good and sufficient reasons to 
dismiss or otherwise terminate their services. Provided that in 
cases of appointments to posts salaries of which are paid wholly or 
partly out of Government grants, the rules laid down by the State 
Government in this respect shall be observed. 


(b) to extend the services of a teacher or any employee beyond the date 
of his superannuation: 


Provided that in case a teacher or any employee is not given an extension 
he may appeal to the Branch Managing Committee against the 
decision of the School Committee. The decision of the Branch 
Managing Committee shall be final in such cases. 


(c) to grant leave other than casual leave which shall be granted ste the 
ماس‎ of the Committee on the recommendation of the Head- 
mistress or the Principal and increments in pay to teachers and 
other employees as per rules of the Board of Secondary Education. 


(d) to grant free and half-free studentship and similar facilities to deserv- 
ing students on the recommendation of the Headmistress or the 
Principal of the Institutions. 


(e) to manage the funds of the Institution. 


(f) to prepare an annual report. 


(g) to deal with all schemes of development of the Institution and such 
other matter subject to the approval of the Branch Managing 
Committee. 


(h) to prepare a list of holidays to be observed in the Institution. 


(i)sto grant deputation facilities to teachers where such deputation is in 
the interest of the Institution. 


(j) to frame rules and regulations regarding attendance of teachers and 
employees, service rules for all the staff in conformity with 
Government rules. 

(k) to realise fees and fines, etc., to fix rates for fees for both curricular 


and co-curricular activities and other purposes relating to the wel- 
fare of the students and the Institution as a whole.

(1) to select textbooks and introduce any additional courses of study that

e 
Provided that in the case of Institutions receiving financial assistance from 
the Government in any form the School Committees shall exercise their powers, 
in matters specified above, subject to any general or special orders of the State 
Government. 


(2) The School Committee to ewercise powers subject to the direction of 
the State Government: In matters specified below the School Committee shall 
exercise powers subject to the directions of the State Government: 


(i) to determine the number of teachers and non-teaching employees in 
every aided institution; 


(ii) to prescribe the scales of pay and allowances and qualifications for 
recruitment; 


(iii) to prescribe the minimum rates of tuition fees; 
(iv) to frame rules and regulations for payment of pension; 
(v) to prescribe the age of retirement; 


(vi) to 8 the maximum number of students in the Institution and in each 
class. 


১3, Appointment, confirmation, dismmssal, appeal and termination: (1) In 
all cases of appointments, permanent or temporary, the Comm.tiee shall issue 
letters of appointment specifying the terms and conditions governing such 
appointments. When a permanent appointment is made, the selected candi- 
date shall be on probation for a specified period after which he or she may or 
may not be confirmed. If he/she is not confirmed he/she may then appeal to 
the Branch Managing Committee of the Mission, the decision of the Branch 
Managing Committee in that case being final. In the case of termination of 
service of an employee, on probation, the School Committee shall communicate 
its decision to the employee concerned at least six weeks before the expiry of 
the period of probation. If no such intimation is given the employee shall stand 
confirmed on the expiry of the period of probation. 


(2) No permanent employee including members of the teaching staff shall 
be dismissed except after giving him an opportunity to defend himself/herself, 
and in such cases the teacher or the employee concerned may appeal to the 
Branch Managing Committee of the Mission against its decision. The decision 
of the Branch Managing Committee of the Mission shall be operative. But the 
Director of Public Instruction, West Bengal, shall have the right to call for all 
the relevant papers relating to an employee who is dismissed. And if the 
Director of Public Instruction, West Bengal, is not satisfied with the decision 
he may then advise the authorities concerned for reconsideration of the matter. 
The final decision shall, however, be with the Branch Managing Committee. 


(3) The services of an employee who remains absent without leave or 
authority for a continuous sash of more than ten days shall stand automati- 
cally terminated unless otherwise directed by the School Committee. This 
shall apply also in cases where an employee overstays the period of his/her 
sanctioned leave for more than five days without prior sanction. 


(4) The services of a permanent employee may be terminated with three 
months’ notice on either side or in lieu thereof three months’ pay. Neither 
side need show any reason in such cases. For termination of services of a 
temporary employee, one month’s notice or in lieu thereof one month's pay 
will be sufficient. 


24, Suspension: The School Committee may suspend any employee— 


(a) where a disciplinary proceeding against him/her is contemplated or 
pending; or 
(b) where, on account of a criminal charge against him/her, an investiga- 
tion is proceeding or he/she is undergoing trial in a court of law. 
Nore: During the period of suspension the employee concerned shall be 
paid pay and allowances equal to fifty per centum of the pay and allowances 
drawn by the employee immediately before such suspension:

Provided that where the period of suspension exceeds ninety days the

Provided further that an employee shall not be entitled to any subsistence

any place other than the Institution where he/she had been working imme- 
diately before suspension. 


25. Age of superannuation and period of extension: ہا‎ the case of the 
members of the teaching staff and other employees the age of superannuation 
is 60. Extension may be given in deserving cases on a year to year basis up 
to the age of 65. 


26. Terms and conditions of grants-in-aid: The School Committee shall 
strictly follow the terms and conditions subject to which the grants-in-aid are 
sanctioned and all grants shall be used exclusively for the purposes and objects 
for which they are given. 


27. Syllabus: The Committee shall follow the syllabus prescribed by the 
Board of Secondary Education without prejudice to its right to impart instruc- 
tions in additional subjects in keeping with the ideals, aims and objects of the 
Mission. 


28. Assets: All assets of the Institution shall vest in the Governing Body 
of the Mission and if the Institution is closed down, no assets created partly 
or wholly out of Government grants shall be disposed of without the prior 
approval of the Government. 


29. Staff Council: The Committee may, with the approval of the Branch 
Managing Committee, constitute, for a period not exceeding its own term of 
office, a Staff Council with the Headmistress or Principal as ex officio President 
and such number of members representing teachers, librarians and clerks as it 
may deem fit to consider all matters relating to the welfare of the Institution 
and make recommendations thereon for consideration by the School Committee. 


30. Academic Council: (1) The Headmistress or Principal may constitute 
with the approval of the Branch Managing Committee an Academic Council 
which shall consist of the Headmistress or Principal, the Assistant Head- 
mistress and not more than three teachers to be selected by her. In the case 
of a Multipurpose School, with more than one stream, there shall not be 
more than one teacher selected from a given stream. 


(2) The Academic Council shall hold office for the duration of the term of 
office of the School Committee. 


(3) The Academjc Council may discuss matters connected with— 


(a) admission of students, 
(b) promotion, 

(c) selection of textbooks, 

(d) time-table, 

(e) measures relating to the improvement of teaching and extracurricular 

activities. 

(4) The Headmistress or the Principal shall take into consideration the 
advice tendered by the Council, but subject to the supervision and control of 
the School Committee, the authority to take a final decision in academic as 
well as other matters concerning the welfare of the students shall vest in the 
Headmistress or the Principal. 


31. The School Committee may appoint such other Committce or Com- 
mittees as may be authorised from time to time by the Governing Body. 


32. These rules may be altered, revised or amended according to the 
exigencies of the circumstances subject to mutual agreement between the 
Mission and the Government.

No, 9-I.—Hth August 1974.—Whereas the Gover- 
hor is of opinion that lands in the area included 
within the boundaries specified in Part II of the 
Schedule below (hereinafter referred to as the 
৭110. area) have been benefited or are likely to be 
venefited by irrigation during the kharif season by 
the water supplied from the irrigation work, namely,

Part I of the Schedule below; 


And whereas an Ordinance, namely, the West 
Bengal Irrigation (Imposition of Water Rate) Ordi- 
nance, 1974 (West Ben. Ord. No. VII of 1974) 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Ordinance) 
providing for a simplified procedure for imposition, 
assesament an collection of water rates in respect 
of lands benefited or likely to be benefited by irriga- 
fn during different cultivation seasons by water 
pep tet from any irrigation work has since been 
romulgated by the Governor; 


‘Now, therefo:e, in exercise of the power conferr- 
ed by section 4 read with sub-section (1) of section 
6 of the said Ordinance, and in supersession of all 
tders made under the Bengal Irrigation Act, 6 
Ben, Act 111 of 1876), determining the rates to be 
charged for canal water supplied for purposes of 


irrigation of any land in the said area, the Governor 
is pleased hereby to declare its intention to impose 
with effect from Ist day of July 1974 in the said 
urea a water rate for kharif season every year. 


Any person interested in any land likely to be 
affected by such imposition of the water rate may, 
within a period of thirty days from the date of 
publication of this notification in the ‘Calcutta 
(xazette’’, prefer objection to the State Government 
against the intended imposition of the water rate or 
inclusion of such land in the said area.

PART II 


Boundaries of the area 


Starting from a point in Mauza Rajprasadpur, 
jurisdiction list No. 72, Barjora police-station of 
district Bankura, wherefrom the west boundary 
line of the declared area, under Bengal Irrigation 
Act, vide Notification No. 32-I of the 17th Septem- 
ber 1951, published at page 2561 of ‘‘Calcutta

Annas Danra in Mauza Dewangarya, jurisdiction 
list No. 81 and in Mauza Arjuni, jurisdiction list 
No. 89 respectively in Barjora police-station of dis- 
trict Bankura and ‘goes down towards south and 
meets the Sali river in Mauza Muktapur, jurisdic- 
tion list No. 184, Sonamukhi police-station of dis- 
trict Bankura, wherefrom it turns towards down 
stream of Sali river along its left bank for a length 
of 3 miles 660 ft. and then it goes towards east and 
up to Mauza Joypur, jurisdiction list No. 45, Sona- 
mukhi police-station of the same district forming 
the south boundary line of the said declared area. 
It then turns towards north forming the east bound- 
ary line of the said declared area and meets the 
north-east corner in Mauza Suratpur, jurisdiction 
list No. 65, Barjora police-station, of the north 
boundary line of the said declared area. There- 
after it turns towards north-west and forms the 
north boundary of the abovementioned declared 
area to meet the starting point. The whole area is 
within police-stations Barjora and Sonamukhi of 
the district Bankura.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


HOME DEPARTMENT 
Transport 
NOTIFICATION 


No. ۷۷۔9325‎ /3T-21/72. — 6th August 1974. ے‎ 
In pursuance of the provisions of sub-section (3B) 
of section 63 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Act 
4 0. 1939), the Governor is pleased hereby to 
puljish the following reciprocal transpott agreement 
arrived at between the Government of West Bengal 
and the Government of Punjab, after previous publi- 
cation of the draft of the same under notification 
No. 2152-۷۷۴۰ dated 25th February 1974, at pages 
390(a) and 390(b) of Part I of the “Calcutta Gazette, 
Extraordinary”, of the 26th February 1974, as 
required by sub-section (3A) of section 63 of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. 


RECIPROCAL AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE 
STATE OF WEST BENGAL AND THE STATE 
OF PUNJAB IN RESPECT OF MOVEMENT OF 
TRANSPORT VEHICLES ON  INTER-STATE 
ROUTES BETWEEN PUNJAB AND WEST 
BENGAL. 


Preamble 


Whereas an agreement was made between the 
Government of West Bengal and the Government 
of Punjab in the month of February 1963, for the 
Operation of road transport services between the 
two States; and 


Whereas the aforesaid agreement expired in the 
month of February 1965, and status quo ante had 
been ‘rraintained since then in anticipation of 
revision and renewal of the agreement; and 


Whereas it is necessary to renew the. agreement 
for facilitating the movement of goods between the 


two States and assisting tourists of one State to visit. 


the other whenever necessary; 


Now, therefore, it is hereby agreed between the 
Government of West Bengal and the Government 
of Punjab as follows: 


1. Preliminary. 


This agreement shall come into force immediately 
after the requirements of publication and considera- 
tion of representations, envisaged under sub-section 
(3A) of section 63 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, 
are fulfilled and shall be effective for a period of five 
years in the first instance from the date it is brought 
into forge. It shall be subject to revision every six 
months or periodically at the instance of either 
State. For reason*to be given in writing by either 
State Government, it may be revoked on three 
months’ notice and suspended on one month’s notice. 
Such revocation or suspension will not, however, 
affect plying of vehicles covered by a permit already 
issued and/or countersigned under this agreement. 
Permanent permits shall be countersigned for the 
entire period of their validity in spite of the fact that 


* such period may extend beyond validity of the 


agreement, 
2. Public Carriers 


It is agreed that public carrier’s permits for 60 
goods vehicles shall be countersigned by the Trans- 
port Authorities of either State. The counter- 
signature shall be valid for the entire State permitt- 
ing Operation on all National and State Highways, 
only with deviation up to 30 kilometres from these 
roads to reach a manufacturing concern or an indus- 
trial centre. The countersignature so granted shall 
be subject to the following conditions: 


(a) That such countersigned vehicles shall not 
be engaged in intra-Stale movement of 
goods within the jurisdiction of the coynter- 
signing State and shall not pick up such 
goods lying whelly within the jurisdiction 
of the countersigning State. 


1507 


1508 THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, AUGUST 6, 1974 


——— Ee ———————— I , 3 


(b) That countersignature shall be subject to the 
provisions of section 56 of the Motor 
Vehicles Act. 

3. Private Carriers 


(1) It is agreed that private carrier’s permits for 
10 goods vehicles shall be countersigned by the 
Transport Authorities of either State. Such counter- 
signature shall be for the entire area of the recipro- 
cating States subject to the following conditions: 


(a) Private carriers of either State operating 
under this Agreement shall not ply for hire 
or reward and _ shall not pick up or set 
down goods within any two points lying 
wholly in the jurisdiction of the counter- 
signing State. 

(b) Goods specified in the private carrier’s permit 
only shall be carried. j 

(2) Recommendations for the countersignature of 
private carrier’s permits shall be made by the State 
Transport Authority concerned only after it is satis- 
fied from a thorough enquiry that countersignature 
is required for a bona fide private purpose. 


4. Temporary permits 
(A) Public carriers and private carriers 


Temporary permits for 75 publi¢ carriers and 10 
private carriers may be issued in a month by the 
State Transport Authority of either State without 
prior concurrence of the other State Transport 
Authority subject to the following conditions:— 


(a) The permits shall be issued in strict con- 
formity with the provisions of section 62 
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. 


(b) The permits shall be valid for a period not 
exceeding 30 days but during this period 
vehicles can perform any number of trips 
between the two States. 


(c) The permits shall be valid, for 1115 entire 
State permitting operation on all National 
and State Highways, only with deviation up 
to 30 kilometres from these roads to reach 
a manufacturing concern or an _ industrial 
centre. 

(d) Copies of temporary permits issued by either 
State Transport Authority shall be 001 
warded forthwith to the other State 
Transport Authority. 

(e) Vehicles of one State shall not pick up or set 
down goods within any two points lying 
wholly in the jurisdiction of the other 
State. 

(0 Goods of only specified description shall be 
Carried in private carriers. 


{B) Tourtst cars and cOaches 


Special permits under sub-section (6) of section 
63 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, may be issued 
by either State Transport Authority as and when 
necessary. 


। 


বা পা সস a পপ সস ০৯৮ সপ ge শা পপ তা = পপ পপ NN Re পো এনা Fe 


5. Taxation 


The principle of single-point taxation shall apply 
to the vehicles of each State operating on any 
Inter-Slate route under this agreement. 


6. Corridor arrangements 


In order to _ facilitate the movement of motor 
vehicles through the territory falling in the States 
of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh the following corridor 
arangements shall be accepted subject to the 
approval of the Governments of Bihar and Uttar. 
Pradesh:— ۱ 


(i) Vehicles shall traverse the territories of 
Bihar and Uttar Pradesh through the 
shortest practicable route if no route is 
specified for the purpose by the Govern- 
ments concerned. 


(ii) Vehicles shall neither pick up nor set down 
goods within Bihar or Uttar Pradesh. 


(iii) The Governments of Bihar and Uttar 
Pradesh shall have the right to prescribe . 
the time within which vehicles shall pass. 
through their jurisdiction. 

(iv) The Governments of Bihar and _ Uttar 
Predesh shall be at liberty to take such 
action as may be permissible under the 
law for any breach of the above conditions 
or of any provision of the law, 


(2) The Governments of West Bengal and Punjab 
shall move the Governments of Bihar and Uttar 
Pradesh for their concurrence to the conditions 
stated above and for the countersignature, subject 
to these conditions, of permits issued by the two, 
State Transport Authorities. 


7. General 


Each State shall accord recognition to tax tokens, 
registration certificates, certificates of fitness of 
vehicles, conductors’ licences, authorisation 10 
drive transport vehicles, etc,, issued by the other 
State in respect of vehicles operating, or to be 
operated, on Inter-State routes in accordance with 
this agrement. 


R. P. OTHA, 


Secy. to the Govt. of Punjab, 
Transport Department. 


M. M. KUSARI, 
Transport Commissioner and Ex Officio 
Secretary, Home (Transport) Department. 
Government of West Bengal 


By order of the Governor, 
D. CHAKRABARTI, 
Dy. Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal

Land Acquisition 
NOTICE 


24-PARGANAS.—No. 15382L.A.(P.W.)/11-405/73.— 
6th August 1974.—-Whereas 14.2185 hectares (35.135 
acres), more or less, of land situate in or near the villages 
of Nehalpur, Srinagar, Sibchandrapur and Begampur des- 
cribed below have been requisitioned under sub-section 
(1) of section 3 of the West Bengal Land (Requisition 
and Acquisition) Act, 1948, by the person authorised 
under section 3(1A) of the Act for the public purpose 
of providing facilities for irrigation and drainage, 
namely, for excavation of main channel from Matia 
Road Bridge to Bibeknagar in connection with Sealdah 
gong Basin Drainage scheme. 


Now, therefore, notice is hereby given that in pur- 
suance of section 4 of the said Act, the Governor 
acquires such land being required for a public purpose as 
aforesaid. 


This notice is given under the provisions of sub- 
seotion (la) of section 4 of the West Bengal. Land 
(Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 (West Bengal 
Act II of 1948), to all whom it may concern. 


A plan of the land may be be inspected in the office 
of the Special Land Acquisition Officer, 24-Parganas 
(North), Bhabani Bhaban, Alipur, Caloutta-27.

the Governor acquires such land being required for a

7 (1) Every compulsory deposit made by or recovered 
from a depositor shall carry simple interest at a rate equal

means the highest of the maximum rates at which interest 
may be paid on different classes of deposits (other than those 
maintained in savings account or those maintained by charit~ 
able or religious institutions) by different classes of scheduled 
banks in accordance with the directions given or issued to 
banking companies generally by the Reserve Bank of India 
under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, 


(2) The interest shall be calculated in such manner as may 
be specified in the scheme framed under section 13. 


(3) For the purposes ot the deduction under section 80 
of the Income-tax Act, interest received on a compulsory. 
deposit shall be deemed to be interest received on a deposit 
with a banking company to which the Banking Regulation 
Act, 1949, applies.

be equal to twenty-five per cent. of the amount 
by which the compulsory deposit made by him 
falls short of the compulsory deposit calculated 
with reference to his correct income.

be made against any person unless such person has been

11. Any depositor, aggrieved by any order of the Income- 
tax Officer imposing a penalty under section 10, may appeal 
to the Appellate Assistant Commissioner and the provisions 
of the Income-tax Act relating to appeals, reference and 
revision Shall, so far as may be, apply in relation to such’ 
order as they apply in relation to an order of the Income-tax 
Officer imposing a penalty under section 22] of that Act. 


12. Any arrear of compulsory deposit and any penalty. 
imposed under this Ordinance shall be recoverable in the 
manner provided in Chapter XVII-D of the Income-tax Act 
for the recovery of arrears of tax. 


13. (1) The Central Government shall, by notification in. 
the Official Gazette, frame a scheme or schemes, to be called: 
Compulsory Deposit (Income-tax Payers) Scheme or Schemes, 
in relation to compulsory deposits. 


(2) A scheme framed under sub-section (J) may provide 
for— 


(a) the manner in which compulsory deposits shall be 
made ; 


(b) the documents to be issued to persons by whom 
deposits have been made 95 evidence of such 
deposits ; 


(c) the authority or authorities by or through whom the 
deposits may be collected ; 


(d) the nomination of any person to receive the amount 
standing to the credit of a depositor in the event 
of his death or in cancellation or change of such 
nomination ; 


(6) the issue of duplicate of any document issued as 
evidence of any’ deposit in the event of loss or 
destruction of the original and the fee (not exceed- 
ing two rupees) on the payment of which such, 
duplicate may be issued ; 


(f)vany other matter which may be necessary or proper 
for the effective implementation of the scheme. 


(3) A scheme framed under this section may provide that 
all or any of its provisions shall take effect either prospectively 
or retrospectively on such date as may be Specified in this 
behalf in the scheme. 


(4) Any scheme framed under this section shall have 
effect notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the 
time being in force (other than this Ordinance) or any instru- 
ment having effect by virtue of any law other than this 
Ordinance. 


14. The Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, add to, amend, vary or rescind any scheme 
framed under this Ordinance. 


15. (2) The amount of any compulsory deposit shall be 
rounded off to the nearest multiple of ten rupees and for 
this purpose any part of a rupee consisting of paise shall be 
ignored and thereafter if such amount is not a multiple of 
ten, then, if the last figure in that amount is five or more, 
the amount shall be increased to the next higher amount 
which is a multiple of ten and if the last figure is less than 
five, the amount shall be reduced to the next lower amount 
which is a multiple of ten. 


(2) The amount of penalty payable under the provisions 
of this Ordinance shall be rounded off to the nearest rupee 
and, for this purpose, where such amount contains a part of

16. The provisions of Chapter XV of the Income-tax Act 
relating to liability in special cases shall, so far as may be, 
apply in relation to compulsory deposits and penaltics im- 
posable under this Ordinance as they apply in relation to 
income-tax payable and penalties imposable under that Act. 


17. (J) The amount of compulsory deposit and interest 
thereon standing to the credit of any depositor shall not be 
liable to attachment under a decree or order of any court in 
respect of any debt or liability incurred by the depositor. 


(2) The amount of compulsory deposit and interest thereon 
standing to the credit of a depositor at the time of his death 
and payable to his nominee shall vest in the nominee and 
shall be free from debt or other liability incurred by the 
deceased or incurred by the nominee before the death of the 
depositor. 


18. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding 51911 
lie against the Government or against any officer of the 
Government for anything which is in good faith done or 
intended to be done under this Ordinance or any scheme 
framed thereunder. 


19. Every scheme framed under this Ordinance shall be 
laid, as soon as may be, after it is framed before each House 
of Parliament while it is in session for a total period of thirty 
days which may be comprised in one session or in two. or 
more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the 
session immediately following the session or the successive 
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any modifica- 
tion in the scheme or both Houses agree that the scheme 
should not be made, the scheme shall thereafter have effect 
only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case 
may be; so, however, that any such modification or annul- 
ment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything 
previously done under that scheme. 


20. If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provi- 
sions of this Ordinance, the Central Government may, by 
order, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance, 
remove the difficulty: 


Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry 
of a period of two years from the commencement of this 
Ordinance.

amount by which the current income exceeds Rs. 25,000;

income exceeds Rs. 70,000:

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


OFFICE OF THE COMMISSIONER OF POLICE, 
CALCUTTA 
ORDERS 


Whereas information has been received from 
credible sources that violent demonstrations are 
likely to take place resulting in large-scale disturb- 
ances of the public tranquillity and breach of the 
peace in the area mentioned in the Schedule below 
in the town of Calcutta (hereinafter referred to as 


the said area); 


And whereas I, S. C. Chaudhuri, Commissioner 
of Police, Calcutta, being an Executive Magistrate 
for the Metropoljtan Area of Calcutta, have been 
specially empowered by the State Government under 
Notification No. 2504-G.A., dated the Ist April 1974, 
to act under section 144 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1973 (Act 2 of 1974); 


And whereas, in my opinion, there is sufficient 
sround for proceeding under the said section for 
immediate prevention of disturbances of the public 
tranquillity and breach of the peace within the said 
area in the town of Calcutta; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 144 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Act 2 of 1974), read with 
sub-section (3) of the said section, I, the said S. C. 
Chaudhuri, Commissiorer of Police, Calcutta, and 
an Executive Magistrate for the Metropolitan area 
of Calcutta, do hereby prohibit from the Tenth day 
of August 1974, until further orders, any assembly 
of five or more persons, or any procession, OF the 
carrying of any lathis or other dangerous weapons, 


or the doing of any act which is likely to cause a 
disturbance of the public tranquillity and breach of 
the peace within the said area in the town of 
Calcutta.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


IRRIGATION AND WATERWAYS 
DEPARTMENT 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 11-1.--120) August 1974. — Whereas the 
Governor is of opinion that lands in the area includ- 
ed within the boundaries specified in Part II of the 
Schedule below (hereinafter referred to as the said 
area) have been benefited or are likely to be benefit- 
od by irrigation during the kharif season by the 
water supplied from the irrigation work namely, 
the Kangsabati Reservoir Project in the districts of 
Bankura, Midnapore and Hooghly, the full descrip- 
2 whereof is stated in Part I of the Schedule 

elow; ] 


And whereas an ordinance, namely, the West 
Rengal Irrigation (Imposition of Water Rate) 
Ordinance, 1974 (West Ben. Ord. No. VII of a 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Ordinance 
providing for a simplified procedure for imposition, 
assessment and collection of water rates in respect 
of lands benefited or likely to be benefited by irriga- 
tion during different cultivation seasons by water 
supplied from any irrigation work has since been 
promulgated by the Governor; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferr- 
ed by section 4 read with sub-section (1) of section 
201 the said Ordinance, and in supersession of all 
orders made under the Bengal Irrigation Act, 1876 
(Ben. Aot III of 1876) determining the rates to be 
charged for canal water supplied for purposes of 
irrigation of any land in the said area, the Governor 
is pleased hereby to declare its intention to impose 


with effect from Ist day of July, 1974, in the said 
area a water rate for kharif season every year. 


Any person interested in any land likely to be 
affected by such imposition of the water rate may, 
within a period of thirty days from the date of 
publication of this notification in the ‘‘Calcutta 
Gazette’, prefer objection to the State Government 
against the intended imposition of the water rate 
or inclusion of such land in the said area.

2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (XIV of 
1947), for adjudication on the following 15806 : 


Issue 


Whether the termination of service of Shri Nripen 
Sen is justiied ۶ To what relief, if any, is he 
entitled ?

The case of the workman, in short, is as follows; 


The workman was appointed by the Company, Messrs. 
Bitumenons Constructors, on 151 April 1968 as a 
Genera; AssiStant and had been working 51006 that date 
meritoriously and efficiently with spotless revOrd of 
Service. 45100100617 the workman had been working 51000 
Ist Apri] 1968, no appointment letter was issued by the 
Comnan,. Thereafter, on 15th April 1969, the Com- 
pany handed over an appointment letter to the work- 
man sctting {orti the terms and cONditions Of service. 
The wOrkn.an acknowledged the reccipt of the letter 
and prayed for (1186 for consideration Of the terms and 
conditions Of the service. But Suddenly on 18th April 
1969, the woikman réc@ived a letter from the Company 
terminating his services On 50116 flimsy pretext. The 
wOrkman has contended that the decision was taken 
unilaterally by the management and that the workman 
wis Not given any Opportunity to defend himself before 
৪12 dOmcSiic enquiry. The workman requested the 
management to withdraw the illegal termination order, 
but to no effect, 


The Company, in its written statement, has denied 
the material allegations made by the workman and has 
contended, inter alia, that the Company etarted its 
business from 1st April 1968, that a large number of 
rctrenched staff of Shalimar Tar Products including the 
wOrkman were taken in without any formal appoint- 
ment Jetter allhough the terms were verbally expressed 
to them, that subsequently on 15th April 1969, the 
Company 150০০ appointment letters to those workmen 
including the concerned workman regarding the terms 
aud cOndiliuns under which the workmen had been 
wOrking, that the workman saw the maNagement and 
represented that the terms were not satisfactory and 
gave out that he would not attend the firm any longer, 
and that since 16th April 1969, the workman began to 
absent himseif. The Company has contended that the 
wotkmad rcSigned from the service of the Company 
voluntarily and, therefore, the Company issucd the 
letter on 18th April 1969, accepting such resignation 
of the workman. The Company has further contended 
that Shri Sen, the claimant ig not a workman but his 
duties were mainly mattagerial and/or superviSOry in 
Nature. 


In this case two points have been presSed for congi- 
aeration by the Company. The first contention is that 
the claimant Shri Sen is not a workman within the 
meafling of section 2(s) of the Industrial Disputes Act 
(hereinafter referred to as the Act). The Company 
haS made a twofold submission on this point. The 
first 15 that the employee Shri Sen was employed mainly 
in managerial or administrative capacity and alter- 
natively he was employed in 3 superviSOfy capacity 
drawing wages mOre than Rs. 500. In suppOrt of its 
sontention the Compafy has relied on a number 01 
documents, and let me examine them one by 0886. 
Ext. 1 is the appointment letter of the claimant Shri 
Sen. It appears from the appointment letter that Shri 
Sen was appointed as a Technical Executive and the 
material terms Of his appointment reads as follows : 


“You will be jn genera] control of the Technical and 
cOmméercia] side Of the Firm and be directly res- 
ponsible to the undersigned or his succ€sSOr Or 19 
Other similar rank. Your job will also comprise 
of SecuriNg Orders, executing them satisfactorily 
afd profitably and collecting payments”, 


AccOrding to the terms of appointment Shri Sen was 
to yet a consolidated salary of Rs. 500 per month and 
in addition to that commission at the rate of 5 per cent 
on the nett profit, of the Company. There is no dis- 
pute also that Shri Sen was given a Power of Atlorney 
for the performance Of his duties and Ext. A-11 is a 
copy Of the same. This Power of Attorney termed as 
Genera] Power of Attorney was executed by Shri P. N. 
Sen Gupta, one of the employers and partners of the 
Company and Shri Sen Gupta executed the Power of 
Attorney as 0116 of the Constituted Attorneys of the 
Company. Under the said Power of Attorney Shri Sen 
was authorised to make sign tenders aNd execute con- 
tracts up to individual yalue of Rs. 1,00,000 with 
different aulhuritics, to ask demand, Sue, collect, receive 
٣:٤:٤ sums due to the Company and to grant necessary 
receipts on behalf of the Company. These documents 
undOubtedly lay down the terms and conditions of the 
Service Of Shri Sen and on a plain reading of the same 
it is clear that Shri Sen was appointed in a Supervis®ry 
capacity within the meaning of clause (iv) of séction 
2(s) of the Act. The evidence of actual duties per- 
formed by Shri Sen comes in the shape of certain 
letters referred to by the Company. Ext. E is a cOpy 
of agreement entered into between the Company on 
one side and Hindusthan Steel Limited, Rourkela 
Fertiliser Plant on the other side for 25060701017 of cer- 
tain works described as Acid Alkali resisting lining 
wOrks in Nitrate Division of Fertiliser Plant, and the 
value Of the contract is Rs. 8,000. It appears that 
Shri Sen signed the contract on behalf of the Com- 
pany. There is no doubt that he was authorised to do 
so under the Power Of Attorney (Ext, A-11) executed 
in his favOur. The next document is a letter, dated 0 
March, 1969 (Ext, A-22), written by the claimant Shri 
Sen to one M. C. Chatterjee of Durgapur in connection 
with mastic flooring at Dairy Farm, Durgapur, ٣ 
Messrs. Durgapur Projects. The contents of the fetter 
show that Shri Sen, on behalf of the Company, was 
asking for certain clarification regarding the work 
undertaken by the Company. This document, in my 
opinion, does not help the Company very much. Ext. 
۸-25 is a lettcr, dated Ist May 1968, written by Hin- 
dusthan Stee] Ltd, to Shri Sen described دو‎ Bitumenous 
Contructors. In this fetter Hindusthan Stee] Ltd. 
wanted to know the rate Of expenditure for repairs of 
certain expansion joints. The endorsement on the 
letter indicates that Shri Sen forwarded the same to 
the Manager of the Company for submission of earliest 
report alid 01509 gave hig cOmments thereon. This 
letter, though filed by the Company, goes to show that 
Shri Sen had not the independent authority to take a 
decision about the quotation of rates by the Company. 

The C ompany hag next relied on the letter, dated 5th 
July 1969, written by it to the Labour Officer regarding 
the present dispute and assorted therein that Shri Sen 
was not a “workman” within the definition of the Act. 

In doing so the Company set out the duties performed 
by Shri Sen under the Company. Obviously that was 
written after the dispute arose and, therefore, much 
reliance should not be pi@ced on it. 


Coming now to the oral Cvidence jt would appear 
that Shri Sen, as P.W. 1, has Stated in his evidence that 
ie main duti¢s where to contract parties to s€cure jOb, 

to sign bills, to collect bills, to make payment and to 
carry Out orders of the management. He denied the 
Suggestion that he was in charge of all the Construction © 
Projects on behalf of the Company. Against that the 
evidence of O.P.W. 1 Surajit Roy, one of the Techni- 
cal Assistants of the Comnany, is that he used to work

THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, AUGUST 13, 1974 


1584(9) 


ander Mr. Nripen Sen afd according to his instruction 
He has also stated that there were about 6 or 7 Techni- 
cal Assistants working under Mr, Sen. But in cross- 
examination he has stated that he is one of the super- 
yisOry staff Of construction job at Rourkela and his 
duly was to Supervise the technical side of the work. 
He has further admitted that since his appointment he 
way posted at Rourkela whereas Shri Sen was posted 
in Calcutta. So he is not a truthful witness when he 
says that he along with other used to work under the 
supervision and on the instruction of Shri Sen. 
O.P.W. 2, Shri P. N. Sen Gupta is one of the Em- 
ploveras who waS examined on behalf of the Company. 
His evidence is that Shri Sen was a sole Technica] Exe- 
cutive in charge of the contract works, securing وم‎ 
tracts, Signing agreements and everything enumerated 
in the Power of Attorney given to him. We have 
already referred to the terms in the Power of Attorney 
earlier and his evidence does not improve the case of 
the Company beyond that. But onc significant fact 
emerges from his evidence. He has categorically stated 
that Shri Sen did not complete his service for the 
purpose Of CarniNg commission. The other witness 
O.P.W. 3, Parimal Chandra Roy Choudhury has stated 
that Shri Sen’s duty was the execution of job such as 
walerpivofing, 10850119001 flooring, ete. 


Upon @ reading of the evidence discussed above 
if is quite clear to me that Shri Sen was appointed 
in a supervisory capacity. But from the whole 
body of evidence it is difficult to say that Shri 
Sen was appointed mainly in managerial and 
administrative capacity. 


_ The Company has, however, relicd on two 
decisious to show that Shri Sen was appointed in 
manageria! capacity. The first is a decision of 
Madras High Court reported in 1959, Vol.-II 
LI..J, page 771 (Standard Vaccum Oi! Co. versus 
Commissioner of Labour), In that decision the 
meaning of management under section 4(i)(a) 
the 1٥۸۲۰۰١ Shops and Establishments’ Act. came 
in for interpretation, Obviously that interpreta- 
tion was of س‎ different statute and not the defni- 
tion of workman in the Act, with which we are 
concerned. Secondly, the facts of that reporred 
decisian have no bearing with the facts of the 
present cause. The other case cited by the Com- 
pany is reported in AIR 1965, Supreme Court, 
page 111, atising out of the appeal from the 
decision of the above case. In that decision also 
the Supreme Court was called upon 10 interprete 
section 4(i)(a) of the Madras Shops and 
Establishments Act. For reasons already re- 
cotded carlitr that decision cannot be applied to 
the present case. 


Therefore, upon a consideration of the factual 
position stated above. I hold that Shri Sen was 
employcd in a supervisory capacity within the 
meaning of clause (iv), and not in managerial or 
administralive capacity within the meaning of 
clause (iii) of section 2(s) of the Act. But to 
take him out of the 06517101011 of workman it در‎ 
191৮2 proved that his wages exceeded Rs, 500. | 
haye already stated earlier that his consolidated 
salary was Rs. 500 and O.P. W. 2, P; N. Sen 
Gupta has stated that Shri Sen did not earn any 
COmmission, That apart, commission, 11) my view, 
Cannot come within the meaning of wages because 
it is dependent on the profits of the Company, It 


may so happen that the Company did not earn 
afly profit ul all, Be that as it might. Shri Sen 
did 1101 receive anything more than Ps, 500 as his 
wages and, therefore, he is a workman within the 
meaniug cf the Act. The contention of the Com- 
pany, to the contrary, is over ruled. 


That takes us to the other point as to whether 
Shri Sen voluntarily resigned from the service or 
not, It is not disputed that Shri Sen received 
the appointment Jetter, Ext. 1, on 15th Aprt! 1969. 
It is also nol in the dispute that on receipt of the 
said appoiiiment letter Shri Sen protested to the 
Company against the terms of his service. 
Ext, A-4 is a copy of the said letter, dated 16th 
April 1969, In that letter Shri Sen wrote to the 
Company that he would intimate the Company 
about the acceptance of the appointment on {he 
Stated terms after giving a thought over it. But 
the admitied position is that although lie formal 
appointment letter was delivered on 15th April 
1969, Shri Sen had been serving under the Com. 
pany since 151 April 1968. In his letter Shri Sen 
also stafed that as he was indisposed he could 
not come earlier. It is in the evidence of 
O.P.W, 2 that Shri Sen personally handed cver 
the said letter to the Company on 747th April 
1969. But it is the positive case of the Company 
that on 15th April 1969, on receipt of the formal 
appointment letter (Ext. 1) Shri Sen gave out that 
he would not accept the appointment and serve 
wider the Company any longer . The Company 
took that as his voluntary resignation, and as Shri 
Sen admittedly did not attend office on 16th and 
17th the Company wrote the letter on 18th April 
1969 (Ext. 1-A), treating the services of Shri

of India Rules, 1971 or any other law in force.

CHAPTER VII 


University Funds, Annual Report and Accounts 


33. (1) The University shall have a fund to be called 
the Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswa Vidyalaya Fund, herein- 
after referred to as the Universtiy Fund. 


(2) All monies received by the University by way of fees, 
fines, endowments, grants, donations, bequests or loans or on 
any other account whatsoever, shall be credited to, and all 
expenditure incurred by the University shall be paid out of, 
the University fund. 


34. The State Government muy in every year make such 
recurring and non-recurring grants to the aivarsity as the 
State Government may deem necessary for the proper 
functioning of the University and for carrying out its 
objectives as envisaged in this Ordinance. 


35. An annual report showing the various activities of 
the University shall be prepared under the direction of such 
subordinate authority or officer and shall be submitted to the 
University on or before such date as may be prescribed. 
The annual report shall be considered by the University at 
a meeting. 


36. (£) As soon as may be after the close of a year 
the accounts of the University for that year shall be audited 
by an auditor appointed by the State Government or in such 
other manner as the State Government may direct. 


(2) The University shall consider the audited annual 
accounts at a meeting aud may take such action thereon as 
it thinks fit. 


(3) The budget for each year shall be presented to and 
considered by the University at a meeting convened for the 
purpose not less than one month before the end of the 
preceding year. 


(4) Copies of the budget as passed by the University and 
the audited accounts together with copies of the audit report 
shall be submitted to the Chancellor and to the State 
Government. 


(5) The State Government may require the University 
to supply to it anv information in regard to the accounts 
and the budget of the University and the University shall 
comply with such requisition. :

Now I turn to the merits of the case, Evident-

victimisation Or unfair labour practice, (iii) when

or violation of a pruiciple of natural justice, ani 
(iv) when on the materials the finding is complete. 
ly haSeless or petverse. The classic decision on

91901 Co, Vs. their workmen reported in AIR 1958 
SC 130-1958 I, LLJ 260. These principles afte all, 
along since followed. Of the several tests laid

that the workman in his written statement has only
