GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


LAND UTILISATION AND REFORMS AND LAND +8 LAND 
REVENUE DEPARTMENT 


Land Reforms 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 16292-L.Ref.—13th August 1974.—In exercise of the power ঠাপা ভি 
by section 60 of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955 (West Ben. Act X 
of 1956), the Governor is pleased hereby to make, ‘after previous publication 
as required by sub-section (1) of the said section, the following amendments in 
the West Bengal Land Reforms Rules, 1965, as subsequently amended (herein- 
after referred to as the said rules), namely : 


Amendments 
In the said rules,-— 
(i) after rule 14D, insert the following rules, namely سے‎ 


“14E. Manner in which compensation for the vesting of any land is to 
be determined and given.—(1) Applications for payment of 
compensation for vesting of any land in the State under the 
provisions of chaptcr HI-B of the Act shall be presented to the 
Revenue Officer having jurisdiction in the area in which the land 
or major portion thereof are situated and shall be in Form No. 7B 
or in a form substantially similar thereto. 


(2) The amount of compensation payable to a raiyar for the land vested 
in the State under section 145 and taken possession of under 
sub-section (3) of section 14T, shall be determined in the follow- 
ing manner, namely سس‎ 


(a) Where the land belongs to a class which ordinarily yields any 
agricultural produce, the Revenue Officer shall, after making 
such enquiry as he may think fit and having taken into account 
the 2۴٥ آ۵‎ productivity of such class of land, determine the 


1609 


1610 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, AUGUST 14, 1974 


0--000 
তিনি 


annual produce of the land on the assumption that it yields 
only one normal crop of paddy. He shall then determine the 
average rate of price of paddy during a period of seven years 
immediately preceding the date of vesting or any shorter period 
for which evidence is available, after taking into consideration 
the publications of the rates of prices authorised by the Govern- 
ment and shall calculate the value of the annual produce of 
the land by multiplying together the annual produce and the 
average rate of price so determined. In cases where the land 
is cultivated by a bargadar one-fourth and in other cases one- 
third of the value of the annual produce so calculated shall be 
the annual income of the land which shall be taken to be the 
gross income. 


(b) Where the land belongs to a class which does not ordinarily yield 
any agricultural produce, the Revenue Officer shall determine 
the annual income of the land to the best of his judgment having 
regard to the nature of the land and its utility to the owner 
thereof and the annual income so determined shall be taken 
to be gross income. 


(c) After the gross income has been determined under clause (a) or 
clause (b), the net income shall be computed by deducting from 
the gross income the following, namely :— 


(i) any sum payable as land revenue, cesses, rates or taxes during 
the previous agricultural year in respect of the land to which 
the gross income relates; and 


(ii) charges on account of management and collection at the rates 
given in sub-clause (iv) of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of 
section 16 of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953 
(West Ben. Act I of 1954). 


(d) After the net income has been computed under clause (c) the 
Revenue Officer shall then proceed to determine the amount of 
compensation payable to the raiyat in accordance with the table 
given in sub-section (1) of section 17 of the West Bengal 
Estates Acquisition Act, 1953 and shall also prepare and 
publish a Compensation Assessment Roll containing particulars 
about the gross income, the net income and the amount of 
compensation payable to a raiyat. 


(e) Within one month from the date of publication of the Compensation 
Assessment Roll under clause (d) a raiyat may file before the 
Revenue Officer an objection in writing in respect of any entry 
therein or any omission therefrom relating to his lands or 
income. 


(f) The order of the Revenue Officer in deciding an objection filed 
under clause (e) shall contain a concise statement of the fact 
of the case, the points for determination, the decision thereon 
and the reasons for such decision. 


(g) The provision for appeal contained in section 20 of the West 
Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953, shall mutatis mutandis, 
apply to appeals against the order of the Revenue Officer. 


(h) Where no objection has been filed or where all such objections 
have been disposed of, the Revenue Officer shall make such 
alterations, if any, in the Compensation Assessment Roll as may 
be necessary to give effect to any order passed on objections 
filed and shall cause the roll or the roll as so altered to be 
finally published by placing it for public inspection free of charge 
during a period of not less than one month at such convenient 
place as he may determine, and cause a public notice to be given 
to that effect stating the place where it shall be open to public 
inspection and the period during which it shall be open to such 
inspection. The Revenue Officer shall make a certificate stating 
the fact of such final publication and the date thereof and shall 
date and subscribe the same with his name and official 
designation.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


DEPARTMENT OF MUNICIPAL SERVICES 


ORDER 


No. 4349/MIM-62/73.—16th Augus; 1974.—In 
exercise of the power conferred by sub-clause (bb) 
of clause (ii) of sub-section (1) of section 654 of 
the Benga] Miunicipal Act, 1932 (Ben. Act XV of 
1932), and in partial modification of Government 
order No. 2666/MIM-142/70, dated the 16th May 
1972, the Governor is pleased hereby to direct 
tha, with immediate effect, all the powers and 
duties which may, under the provisions of the 
Bengal Municipal Act, 1932 (Ben. Act XV of 
1932) or any other Act or any Ordinance or any 
Regulation or any rule, by-law, order, notification 
or subsidiary legislution made under the provis,ons 
of the said Act or such other Act or such Ordinance 
or such Regulation, be exercised and performed 
by the Chairman and by the Commissioners 
whether at a meeting or otherwise, shall be exercised

6 per cent. West Bengal Loan, 1984, issued at Rs.99.00 per cent. and redeemable 
at par on 27th August 1984, ee! 


1. Object,—The proceeds of the loan will be utilised towards meeting the 
Capital expenditure of developmental schemes included in the State Plan. 


oa Security for loan.—lIn accordance wjth Article 293(1) of the Constitution 
of India, the loan will be secured on. tht ‘whole of thé Consolidated Fund of the 
Government of West Bengal. 7 ; : 

The consent of the Central Government has been obtained to the floatation of 
this loan as required by Article 293(3) of the Constitution of India. 


3. Description.—The loan will be briefly described as the 6 per cent. West 
Bengal Loan, 1984. 


1625 


1626 THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE,  XTRAORDINARY, AUGUST 17, 1974 [PART এ

4. Amount of Issue.—The amount of the loan will be Rs.13.50 crores. 


5. Issue price.—The issue price will be Rs.99.00 for every Rs.100 of the loan” 
applied for. ° 


6. Subscriptions.—Subscriptions will be received from 27th August, 1974 
to 3151 August 1974, both days inclusive. ,Subscriptions may be হা? the form of 
“he bait or securities of 44 per cent. West Bengal Loan, 1974. The loan will 
be closed without notice as soon as it appears that the total subscriptions in cash 
and securities of the 44 per cent. West Bengal Loan. 1974 amount approximately 
to Rs.13.50 crores and in any case not later than the close of business on 
31st August, 1974. The Government reserves the right to retain subscriptions 
received up to 10 per cent. in excess of the sum of Rs.13.50 crores. 


od 
a 


7. Partial allotment.—If the total subscriptions exceed the sum of Rs.14.85 
crores, partial allotment will be made to the subscribers in cash. If partial allotment 
is made, a proportionate refund will be made as soon as possible after allotment. 
No interest will be paid on the amount so refunded. 


8. Date of repayment.—The loan will have a currency of 10 years from the 
27th August 1974 and will be repaid at par on the 27th August 1984. 


9. dnterest.—The loan will bear interest at the rate of 6 per’ cent. per anhum 
from 27th August 1974. Interest will be payable half-yearly on the 27th February 
and 27th August and will be subject to tax under the Income Tax Act, 1961. 


Refunds of tax deducted, if any, at the time of payment (at 1৪0৬ prescribed 
by the annual Finance Acts) will be obtainable by holders of the loan, who are not 
liable to tax or who are liable to tax at a rate lower than the rate at which tax was 
deducted. A holder who is not liable to tax or who is liable to tax at a rate lower 
than the prescribed rate can obtain, on application, a certificate from the Income-tax 
Officer of the district authorising payment of interest to him without deduction of 
tax or with deduction of tax at such lower rate as may be applicable to the holder. 


Interest on Goverament securities along with income in the form of interest or 
dividends on other approved investments, will be exempt from income-tax subject to 
a limit of Rs.3,000 per annum and subjéct to the other provisions of section 80L 
of the Income Tax Act, 19091

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 19452-6.S. /FS/9S-9 /72.—24th August 1974.— 
Whoreas the Governor is of opinion that it 1s 
necessary and expedient so to do far the maintenance 
of supplies of iodised and _  non-iodised salt 
essential to the life of the community, and for 
securing the equitable distribution and availablility 
at a fair price, in West Bengal, of iodised and 
non-iodised salt; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred 
by sub-rule (2), read with clause (a) of sub-rule 
(3), of rule 114 of the Defence of India Rules, 1971, 
the Governor is pleased hereby to make the 
following order, namely: 


Order 


No consignment of iodised and/or non-iodised 
salt or any part thereof arriving in any of the 
railway or steamer stations in the State of West 
Bengal from any of the railway or steamer stations 
outside the State of West Bengal shall be delivered 
to the consignee or to anybody else unless such 
delivery is authorised by an endorsement in writing 
to this effect by the Director of Non-cereal Essential 
Commodities or by the Assistant Director of Non- 
cereal Essential Commodities in the Department of 
Food and Supplies, Government of West Bengal, in 
Calcutta area, and by the District Magistrates / Deputy 
Commissioners or by the Subdivisional Officers 
concerned in other areas of the State outside 
Calcutta area, on the relevant railway or steamer 
receipts under which such consignment or part 
thereof is deliverable: 


Provided that nothing in this order shall apply to 


the delivery of any consignment of iodised and/or 
non-idesed salt which is booked— 


(a) on Government account, 
(০) on Food ‘Corporation of India account, 


(c) on West Bengal Essential Commodities 
Supply Corporation Limited account, 


(d) under and in accordance with a Military 
Credit Note, 


(e) to an officer of the Defence Services by 
designation, 


(f) on R.M.C. or 
(g) as parcels. 


2. No railway or steamer receipt in respect of 
any consignment of iodised and/or non-iodised salt 
or part thereof arriving in any of the railway or 
steamer کا‎ in the State of West Bengal from 
any of the raffway or steamer stations outside the 
State of West Bengal shall be transferred by sale 
or otherwise to any person unless such transfer 1s 
permitted by an order in writing to this effect made 
by any of the officers referred to in paragraph 1 of 
this order. 


Explanation.—In this order,— 


(a) “Calcutta area’’ means— 

(i) the area described in Schedule I to the 
Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951 (West 
Bengal Act XXXIII of 1951), as amended 
by notification under section 594 of the 


1860(a)

said Act, together with the Fort William 
and that part of Hastings north of the

(ii) the area within the limits of the Port of 
Calcutta as defined by notification under

NOTIFICATION 


No. 2074-L.—30th August, 1974.—The following Act of the West Bengal Legislature, having been 
assented to by the President, is hereby published for general information :— 


West Bengal Act XXXVIII of 1974 


THE WEST BENGAL LABOUR WELFARE FUND 
ACT, 1974. 


[Passed by the West Bengal Legislature.} 


[Assent of the President was first published in the Calcutta 
Gazette, E.traordinary, of the 30th August, 1974.] 


An Act to provide for the constitution of a fund for promot- 
wg activities connected with the welfare of labour in 
West Bengal and for matters connected therewith. 


_  WHBREAS it is expedient to constitute a fund for promot- 
ing activities connected with the welfare of labour in West 
Bengal and for matters connected therewith ; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
Republic of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 


follows : سس‎

title, Welfare’ Fund Act, 1974.

rules made thereunder, in respect of which no 
penalty is provided, 

he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which, 
may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to 
two thousand rupees or with both. 


22. (2) No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magis- 
trate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence 
punishable under section 21. 


(2) No prosecution for such offence shall be instituted 
except by an Inspector with the previous sanction of the 
Welfare Commissioner. 

(3) No Court shall take cognizance of such offence, unless 
complaint thereof is made within six months of the date on 
which the offence is alleged to have been committed.

NOTIFICATION 


No, 1353-Pr/53/74.—3l1st August 1974 —Whereas 
it appears to the Governor that the July 20, 1974, 
issue Qf ““SORGANISER’’, an English weekly, edited 
by Shri V. P. Bhatia, printed at Bharat Mudranalaya, 
Rani Jhans: Road, New Delhi, and published by Shri 
Bry Bhusan for Bharat Prakashan (Delhi) Ltd., E-7, 
Jhandewala Extension, New Delhi-110055, published 
an article entitled “The Arabs are the cultural 
children of India’’, purported to have been written by 
H G. Mudgal, containing matters which deliberately 
and maliciously intend to outrage the religjous feel- 
ings and beliefs of the Muslim and other communities 
and the publication of which is punishable under 
section 295A of the Indian Penal Code (Act 45 of 
1860) ۰ 


Now, therefore, tn exercise of the power conferred 
by section 95 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 
1973 (Act 2 of 1974), and in consideration of the 
srounds of opinion mentioned below, the Governor 
is pleased hereby to declare every copy of the said 
issue of the said English weekly newspaper and all 
other documents containing copies, reprints and 
translations thereof, or extracts therefrom, be for- 
feted to the Government.

of Kaaba the Black stone and other traditional Gods 
of the Arabs till the age of forty’’, “....the Quran

the New Testament, of the Quran, is a weak God 
and has power only over weakminded men and 
women’’, etc., which are deliberately and maliciously 
intended to outrage the religious feelings and beliefs 
of the Muslim and other communities.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


CO-OPERATION DEPARTMENT 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 3141-Co-op. /2R-14/74.—30th August 1974.—In exercise of the power 
conferred by section 142 of the West Bengal Co-operative Societies Act, 1973 
(West Ben. Act XX XVJII of 1973), and in supersession of the Bengal Co- 
operative Societies Rules, 1942, as subsequently amended, the Governor is 
pleased hereby to make, after previous publication as required by sub-section 
(1) of section 142 of the said Act, the following rules, namely: 


THE WEST BENGAL CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES RULES, 1974 
CHAPTER I 


Preliminary 


1. Short title—These rules may be called the West Bengal Co-operative 
Societies Rules, 1974. 


2. Definitions.—({1) In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in 
the subject or context,— 


(a) “the Act’? means the West Bengal Co-operative Societies Act, 1973; 

(b) “borrowed capital” means the total of loans, deposits and other 
borrowings of a co-operative society; 

(c) “ Additional Registrar of Co-operative Societies”, “Joint Registrar of 


Co-operative Societies”, “Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Socie- 
ties”, “Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Societies”, “Chief 


1€83(5)

بج .رس٠‏ ہے سے تو نہ ہی 
শপ তা -_‏ 


Auditor of Co-operative Societies”, “District Auditor of Co-opera- 
tive Societies”, and “Co-operative Development Officer” mean 
respectively persons appointed by those designations by the State 
Government to assist the Registrar of Co-operative Societies; 


(d) “director” means a member of a managing committee but excludes a 
managing director; 


(e) “distrainer” means a person who is empowered by the Registrar to 
distrain and sell the produce of mortgaged land including the 
standing sears thereon, in accordance with the provisions of 
section 99; 


(f) “member” includes delegates of members referred to in the proviso 
to sub-section (1) of section 20; 


(g) “owned capital” means the total of paid-up share capital and accumu- 
lated reserve fund and other funds created out of profits of a 
co-operative society or otherwise; . 


(h) “schedule” means the schedule of forms appended to these rules; 


(i) “secretary” sneans a person who, subject to the control of the manag- 
ing committee, is entrusted with the managemnet of the affairs of 
a co-operative society and includes a member of a ,managing 
committee or any other person discharging the duties of a secretary 
by whatever name called and whether under a contract of service 
with the society or not; 


(j) “section” means a section of the Act; 


(k) “working capital” means the total capital of a co-operative society 
consisting of borrowed capital and owned capital; and 


(1) words and expressions used in these rules but not defined and defined 
in the Act shall have the same meanings as are respectively 
assigned to them in the Act. 


(2) Unless otherwise specified in these rules and the bye-laws of a 
co-operative society— 


(a) words importing the masculine gender include the feminine gender; 
(b) words in the plural include the singular and vice versa; 
(০) the word “person” includes a body of persons corporate or otherwise; 


(d) expressions “referring to writing include printing, typing, lithography, 
photography, and other methods of representing or reproducing 
words in a visible form; and 


(e) with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, the word 
“signature” shall include his thumb impression or other mark duly 
attested to signify his signature. 


(3) There shall be the following classes of co-operative societies, namely;:— 


(i) “agricultural society” meaning a co-operative society of which the 
majority ہ٥‎ members are agriculturists; 


(1) “agro-service co-operative society” meaning a co-operative society 
formed of unemployed— 


(a) degree holders in any branch of engineering, technology, science, 
commerce, arts or agriculture, or 


(b) diploma-holders in any branch of engineering or technology, or 


(৫) certificate-holders in any industrial trades, for their exclusive 
bencfits, the percentage of degree or diploma-holders in agricul- 
tural engineering and in any branch of agriculture in the 
membership of the co-operative society being not less than sixty 
per cent.; 


(iii) “housing society” meaning a society the object of which jis providing 
its members with dwelling houses, flats or lands for construction of 
dwelling houses and maintenance of common services in connection 
therewith;

(iv) ‘marketing society” meaning a primary society composed of primary 
agr.culutral credit societies, service co-operatives and agriculturists 
as its members; 


(v) “multipurpose society” meaning a co-operative society which includes 
among ats object two or more of the primary objects specified in 
clauses (a), (c), (ii), (iit), (vi), (x) and (xi) or any other object for 
which a transport co-operative society is formed; 


(vi) “mutual benefit society” meaning a co-operative society, the primary 
ob,.ct of which is to create funds by raising contributions from its 
members by accepting grants and donations or otherwise, and to 
employ such funds for the benefit of its members or their nominees; 


(vii) “processing society” meaning a co-operative society, the prima 
object of which is to process agricultural produce into a state whic 
is fit for consumption; 


(viii) “production and sale society” meaning a co-operative society, the 
primary object of which is the collective production and/or disposal 
of goods of its members or otherwise; 


(ix) “purchase and sale society” meaning a co-operative society, the pri- 
mary object of which is to purchase goods and distribute them 
amongst its members; 


(x) “students co-operative” meaning a co-operative society formed mainly 
of students of educational institutions for their exclusive benefit; 


(xi) “thrift and savings society” meaning a co-operative society, the pri- 
mary object of which is to encourage and provide facilities for the 
exercise of thrift among its members; 


(xii) “transport society” meaning a co-operative society, the members 
whereof shall be drivers, cleaners, mechanic and others and the 
object of which shall be to operate transport vehicles for use by the 
members of such a society as well as for carrying passengers: 


Provided that the percentage of drivers, conductors, cleaners, mechanics 
and other workers shall not be less than 70 per cent. of the total 
membership of the society. 


3. Determination of one-half, one-third, etc.—When any rule requires the 
determination of one-half, one-third or any other fraction of a number and 
that number is not evenly divisible by 2, 3 or such other figure as may be 
required, the number next below, which ig evenly divisible by 2, 3 or such 
other figure, shall be taken for the original number. 


4, Forms.—The forms set forth in the schedule or forms as near thereto 
7 circumstances admit shall be used in all matters to which these forms 
relate: 


Provided that the Registrar may at his discretion— 
(i) modify any of the forms set forth in the schedule; or 


(ii) suggest new forms in their places or for any other matter for which 
forms are required. 


5. Net profits.—The ‘net profits’ of a co-operative society shall be the 
profits remaining after allowing for the following charges in addition to those 
specified in clause (z) of section 2, namely— 


(a) all other usual working charges, such as, repairs, rent, taxes and the 
like, bounties or subsidies received; depreciation and irrecoverable 
book debts written off; 


(b) capttal expenditure written off either wholly or in part; 


(c) capital loss actually incurred and not adjusted against any fund created 
out of profits; 


(d) provision for estimated bad debts, if any; and 


(e) such other charges as may be specified by the Registrar upon advice of 
the Reserve Bank of India. ia

6. Co-operative year.—The co-operative year shall mean the year 
commencing on the Ist day of July. 


7. Functions of the State Co-operative Union.—Subject to such directions 
as the State Government may, from time to time, issue regarding utilisation 
of its funds or otherwise, the State Co-operative Union may carry out the 
following functions, namely— 


(i) to promote and develop the co-operative movement in West Bengal, 
to educate, guide and assist the people in their efforts to build up 
and expand the co-operative sector and to serve as an exponent of 
co-operative principles and ideas; 


(ii) to organise co-operative training programmes and run training centres 
according to the schemes of the State Government or otherwise; 


(iii) to develop inter-co-operative relationship and help the co-ordinated 
functioning of the co-operative movement in various sectors; 


(iv) to organise, conduct, collaborate and assist in carrying out research 
and investigation on important co-operative problems; 


(v) to maintain an information bureau and a library; 


(vi) to express and organise Opinion on matters of co-operative policy and 
act as the accredited representative of West Bengal’s Co-operative 
Movement in the national and international spheres; 


(vii) to convene, organise and hold co-operative seminars, meetings, confer- 
ences and exhibitions; to spread the message and_ ideals of 
co-operative movement in the State and to mould public opinion in 
respect thereof; 


(viii) to facilitate the promotion of co-operative societies and assist the 
affiliated societies in resolving their problems and difficulties; 


: (ix) to select delegates, representatives or observers on behalf of the 
Union for participation in the international, national and State 
conferences, 


(x) to organise, promote or undertake such other activities or functions 
as are considered beneficial or conducive towards the attainment of 
the ra of the aforesaid Union in accordance with the bye-laws 
thereof. 


CHAPTER 0 


Registration 


8. Formation of Co-operative Society.—{1) No primary co-operative credit 
society shall be registered unless the applicants— 


(i) reside or hold landed property in the same town or village or in the 
same group of villages; or 


(ii) are members of the same class or occupation. 


(2) The State Government may, if it is satisfied that it is necessary so to 
do to ensure at the very inception that the societies hold reasonable promise of 
future growth, self reliance, broad numerical and financial base and other ele- 
ments of assured viability, by general or special order, direct that different 
classes of co-operative societies shall be registered with such contribution to 
নস টা of such societies by the members thereof as may be specified in 
the order. 


(3) No Apex or Central Society shall be registered unless it has among its 
applicants at least— 


(a) six co-operative societies; or 


(b) six applicants composed of individual persons and co-operative 
societies: 


Provided that the number of individual persons shall not exceed one-third 
of the total number of applicants.

9. Application for registration._(1) An application for registration of a 
society shall be submitted to the Registrar in the form set forth in the schedule 
and shall be signed by the applicants. 


(2) Where a co-operative society is an applicant, the application shall be

10. Registration of society and refusal to register.—(1) On receipt of the 
application, the Registrar shall satisfy himself that the bye-laws are— 


(a) in conformity with the Act and the rules, 
(b) suitable for carrying out the objects of the society, and 
(c) suitable for ensuring the safe conduct of the business of the society. 


(2) When a society is registered, the Registrar shall grant certificates of 
registration in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(3) On the registration of a society, two copies of its approved bye-laws 
shall be stamped with the official seal of the Registrar. One of the said copies 
shall be retained in the office of the Registrar and the sécond™ copy together 
with the certificate of registration shall be forwarded to the society. 


(4) If the society intends to be a member of a financing bank, a third copy 
Shall be authenticated and sent to the financing bank. 


(5) In every case in which the Registrar refuses to register a society, he 
shall record in writing the reasons for his refusal and shall communicate 1115 
decision by registered post to the applicant whose name appears at serial No. 1 
in the application for registration. 


11. Restriction on membership.—No person qualified under the bye-laws 
to be a member of a co-operative society shall be excluded from membership 
without sufficient cause: 


Provided that without the permission of the Registrar— 


(1) no person shall be entitled to membership of any society with 
unlimited liability who is, or has at any time during the two preced-

(ii) no person shall be entitled to membership of any credit society even 
with limited liability if he is a member of or is indebted to any 
other such society until he has obtained in writing the consent of 
the society of which he is already a member. 


12. Making of bye-laws.—{]1) Every co-operative society shall make bye- 
laws in respect of the following matters, namely:— 


(a) the name and registered address of the society; 


(0) the extent of the area the inhabitants of which or the persons carrying 
on their trade, profession or occupation at which are eligible to 
apply for membership of the society; * 


(c) the object for which the society is established and the purpose to 
which its funds may be applied; 


(d) the qualifications required for membership and the terms of admission 
of members; 


(e) the rights and liabilities of membership; 
(f) the manner in which the capital may be raised; 


(g) the mode of appointment and removal of the directors and officers of 
the society, and the duties and powers of the Managing Committee; 


(h) the mode of summoning and conducting meetings, and the right of 
voting; 


(i) the general conduct of the business of the society; 
(j) the disposal of profits

13. Withdrawal, removal or expulsion of member.—({1) A member of any 
registered society may, if he is not in debt to the society or is not surety, 
withdrew from the society after giving one month’s notice in writing to the 
Secretary or any officer performing the duties of the Secretary. 


(2) .A member may be removed or expelled from a registered society only 
for suca ‘causes, and in accordance with such procedure, as may be provided 
in the bye-laws. 


(3) A member who ceases to be qualified under the bye-laws may be 
removed by the managing committee. ' 


14. Amendment of bye-laws.--(1) After the bye-laws have been registered, 
a co-operative society sip amend them by altering or rescinding any bye-law 
or by making a new bye-law. No such amendment shail be made save in 
accordance with a resolution passed at a general meeting: 


Provided that subject to sub-rule (2), no such resolution shall be valid 
unless it is passed by one-third of the total number of members subsisting as 
such on the date of issue of the notice of the general meeting and by two-thirds 
of the members present at such meeting. ١

(2) In special cases the Regittr.r inzy register an amendment which is

(3) In every case in which the bye-laws of a society are amended, an

(6) When the Registrar finds that there are prima facie grounds for refus-

15. Antendment of bye-laws at the instance of the Registrar.—(1) If it 
appears to the Registrar to be necessary or desirable in the interest of any co- 
Operative sociéty to amend the bye-laws of such society, the Registrar may, on 
his own motion or on the application of a financing bank of which the society 
is a member and a debtor, supported by a resolution of the managing committee 
of the financing bank indicating the amendment and the reasons justifying the 
same, authorise any person, by special order in writing, to call a special general 
meeting of the soctety to make the amendment within one mgnth or such 
longer period as may be specified by the Registrar. 


(2) Notwithstanding any rule or bye-law prescribing the period of notice 
for, and the method of summoning, a general meeting, the Registrar, in the 
case 01 a meeting called under sub-rule (1), may specify the time and place for 
the meeting, the manner in which it shall be summoned and the matter which 
shall be discussed thereat. 


(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 14, 
the Registrar shall registér the amendment, if passed by two-thirds of the

amendment inconsistent with the provisions of the Act and the rules there- 
under. 


(4) When the Registrar registers the amendment of bye-laws, he shall retain

dule. If the society is a member of a financing bank, a third copy duly authen- 
ticated by the Registrar shall be sent to such bank.

CHAPTER III 
Management of Co-operative Societies 


16. Notice of general meeting.—({l) A general meeting shall be convened 
by the Secretary or any Officer authorised by the managing committee, in 
accordance with the direction of the managing committee: 


Provided that where a Government officer has been deputed to the service 
of a co-operative society under section 24 he shall. where there is no Secretary, 
convene the general meeting in accordance with the provisions of the Act and 
the rules thereunder. 


(2) Unless otherwise provided in the bye-laws, a notice of the meetin 
stating the place, date and hour of the meeting together with a statement o 
business to be transacted at it shall be sent to every member or any delegate, 
as the case may be, fifteen clear days before the date of the meeting in ihe 
manner provided in the bye-laws. 


(3) Any accidental omission to give notice to any member or the non- 
receipt of the notice by any member shall not invalidate the proceedings of 
any meeting. 

(4) When the Registrar or the officer or person, as the case may be, autho- 
rised by him, call a general meeting under section 21(3) or 22(2) or when the 
Registrar calls such meeting under section 21(4), the Secretary or any other 
officer authorised by the bye-laws to call general রক shall arrange for 
issue and despatch of notices of the meetings as may be required by the 
Registrar or the officer or persons authorised by him. 


17. General meeting.—{1) A general meeting of every co-operative society, 
to be called the annual general meeting, shall be held within fifteen months 
from the date of its registration and thereafter as provided in section 21. 


(2) (i) If the managing committee fails to take steps, or does not give 
direction, to convene the annual general meeting at least two months 
before the expiry of the period referred to in sub-rule (1), the Chairman, or 
in his absence the Vice-Chairman or the Executive Officer or the Managing 
Director, as the case may be, shall convene the meeting. 


(ii) Where the general meeting is required to be held by convoking 
representatives, the election of delegates shall be completed before the 
aforesaid period of two months: 


Provided that in case of failure of the managing committee to take steps or 
to give direction, sufficiently in advance, towards holding of such election 
within the period prescribed just above, the Chairman. and in his absence the 
Vice-Chairman, shall perform, within the said prescribed period, such duties 
on behalf of the managing committee: 


Provided further that where a general meeting is called by the Registrar, 
he shall take steps or authorise any of his officers to hold election of delegates 
in case the managing committee fails to hold such election of delegates within 
ie time specified by the Registrar or by the officer or person authorised by 

im. 


(iii) No person shall be qualified to be chosen as a representative or elected 
as a delegate to join the general meeting of an apex or a central society. as 
the case may be, if he is not a member of that apex or central society, as the 
case may be, or of any society affiliated to that apex or central society. 


18. Special general meeting.—(1) The rules concerning general meeting 
shal] apply, mutatis mutandis, to special general meetings called under 
section 22. 


(2) At a special general meeting, no business other than that specified in 
the notice issued under sub-rule (2) of rule 16 shall be discussed. 


19. Requisition of special general meeting—A requisition for a special 
general meeting to be convened under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 22 
Shall state the object of the meeting, shall be signed by the members requisi- 
tioning it and shall be sent to the registered office of the society. 


20. Powers of general meeting.—{1) The general meeting of a co-operative 
society shall examine, subject to the provisions of section 21, the annual report 
regarding working of the society and, in particular, the work of the managing

the interest of the society. 

(2) Every resolution at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes 
of members, and if the votes be equal, the Chairman shall have a second or 
Casting vote. 


21. Chairman of general meeting.—({1) The Chairman, or in his absence 
the Vice-Chairman, of a society shall preside over the general meeting of a 
society. In the absence of the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman, one of the 
directors in the panel mentioned in sub-rule (5) of rule 28, in order of their 
names in the panel, shall be the Chairman of the meeting. 


The said Chairman shall preside over the meeting till the item for electing 
members of the managing committee is taken up; and thereafter, if the said 
Chairman is a candidate for election, the members present at the meeting 
shall elect from amongst them one who is not a candidage for election to 
preside over the meeting till the election is over. The Presiding Officer elected 
or the Election Officer appointed in terms of rule 29, as the case may be, shall 
conduct the election, and at the conclusion of the meeting the Presiding Officer 
or the Election Officer, as the case may be and the Chairman or Chairmen, as 
the case may be, shall sign the proceedings of the meeting. 

(2) The Chairman of the general meeting shall maintain order in the meet- 
ing and shall control and conduct the proceedings in such manner as may be 
conducive to expeditious and satisfactory disposal of business. He _ shall 
decide all points of order and his decision upon such points shall be final. 

(3) The Chairman of the general meeting may direct any member to 
withdraw for disorderly conduct, and the member so ordered shall immediately 
withdraw and unless otherwise directed by the Chairman shall remain absent 
during the remaining period of the me2ting on that date and shall not be 
entitled to vote without the permission of the Chairman. 

(4) In the event of disorder, the Chairman of the meeting may suspend the 
mecting and adjourn it. 

(5) In case where the business of the general meeting cannot be completed 
in the course of one Sitting, the same may be adjourned by the Chairman of 
the meeting. 


22. Quorum of general meeting. -(1) Unless otherwise provided in the 
bye-luws, the quorum for a general meeting shall be one-fifth of the total 
number of members subsisting as such as on the date of notice of the meeting. 
After the issue of such notice, no new member shall be admitted till the 
general meeting 15 over. 

(2) No business shall be transacted at any meeting unless there is a quorum 
at the time when the business of the meeting is due to commence. 

(3) 1f within half-an-hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum 
is not present, the meeting shall stand adjourned: 


Provided that— 

(i) no quorum shall be necessary at a meeting adjourned in accordance 
with this sub-rule, and 

(ii) a meeting, which has been called on requisition under clause (a) of 
sub-section (1) of section 22, shall not be adjourned but dissolved. 

(4) If at any time during the meeting sufficient number of memters are not 
present to form a quorum, the Chairman of the meeting, on his attention being 
drawn to this fact, shall adjourn the meeting, and the business that remains 
to be transacted at this meeting, if any, shall be disposed of in the usual manner 
at the adjourned meeting. 

(5) Where a general meeting is adjourned under sub-rule (4) or sub-rule (5) 
of rule 21 or under sub-rule (3) or sub-rule (4) of this rule, the adjourned 
meeting shall be held ordinarily at the same place, on the same day of the 
next week and at the same time, and the fact of adjournment shall be notified 
at the office of the society and at its branches, if any, and on the notice board 
of the local panchayat office, if there be any. 


23. Minutes of general meeting.—-(1) Every co-operative society shall cause 
minutes of proceedings of general meetings to be entered in a book kept for 
that purpose. 

(2) Unless the minutes are drawn up and are duly signed by the Chairman 
immediately on the termination of the meeting, the minutes free from all 
alterations or corrections shall be drawn up and shall be signed by the

terminated. The minutes so signed shall be evidence of the proceedings of

(3) Until the contrary is proved, every general meeting of a Society, in 
respect of the proceedings whereof minutes have been so recorded, shall be 
deemed to have been duly called and held.

24. Voting of general meeting.—(1) A resolution which is put to the vote 
of a general meeting shall be decided on a show of hands unless (whether 
before or after the declaration of the result of the show of hands) a poll is 
demanded by at least ten members, and if no poll is demanded, a declaration 
by the Chairman of such meeting that a resolution has been carried or lost 
and an entry to that effect in the minutes of the proceedings shall, for the 
purposes of the Act, be conclusive proof of the fact that such resolution has 
been duly carried or lost but it shall not be proof of the number or proportior 
of the votes recorded in favour of or against such resolution. 


(2) If a poll is demanded, the votes shall be taken in such manner and at 
such time as the Chairman of the meeting directs, and the result of such poll 
shall be deemed to be the decision regarding the resolution over which the poll 
is demanded: 

Provided that when a poll is taken, the voting shall be by ballot. 


(3) When a pol] is taken, the number of members voting for or against 
a resolution shall be recorded in the minutes of the proceedings. 


25. General meeting by delegates.—(1) A primary co-operative society with 
a membership of 1,500 or more but not exceeding 3,000 may, if the bye-law so 
provides, and a co-operative society with a membership exceeding 3,000 shall 
hold their general meetings by convoking representatives (hereinafter referred 
to as delegates) of areas, sections, constituencies or categories, as the caSe may 
be, instead of summoning all members in person, on the basis of the following 
slabs of the representation, namely:— 
(a) one delegate for every 25 members or major fraction thereof for a 
society with a membership from 1,500 to 3,000; 
(b) one delegate for every 50 members or major fraction thereof for a 
society with membership from 3001 to 5000; 


(c) one delegate for every 100 members or major fraction thereof for a 
society with a membership from 5,001 to 10,000; 

(d) one delegate for every 200 members or major fraction thereof for a 
society with a membership from 10,001 to 30,000; 

(e) one delegate for every 250 members or major fraction thereof for a 
Society with a membership of 30,001 or more. 


(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1), the West Bengal 
State Co-operative Bank Limited, the West Bengal Central Co-operative Land 
Development Bank Limited and the Central Co-operative Banks shall hold their

to as the delegates) of sections or categories, as the case may be, instead of 
summoning all members in person, on the following basis, namely:— 


(a) in case of the West Bengal State Co-operative Bank Ltd.— 


(i) one delegate for every member Central Bank and one delegate from 
the area of operation of each Central Bank (if any) amalgamated 
with the State Co-operative Bank in terms of the scheme drawn 
by the State Government; 


(11) one delegate for every member Apex Society; 


(iii) one delegate for every category of other member societies: provided 
that where the number in any category exceeds 25, there shall be 
one delegate for every 25 or a fraction thereof; and 


(iv) one representative of the State Government: 


(b) in case of the West Bengal Central Co-operative Land Development

(111) one delegate for every class of the other members: and 
(iv) one representative of the State Government;

26. Division of area of a society for election of dclegates.—{1) The manag- 
ing committee shall, subject to approval of the Registrar, divide the area of 
the society into convenient areas, sections, constituencies or categories for the 
purpose of election of delegates. 


(2) The division of the area of operation of a society under sub-rule (1) shail 
be duly notified to all the members, and a member in a particular area, section, 
constituency or category shall be entitled to vote in the election of the delegate 
only for that particular area, section, constituency or Category. 


27. Framing of regulations by managing committee.—The managing 
committee shall make regulations to provide for all matters relating to the 
election of delegates, and in particular for— 

(a) the manner of nomination and election of delegates, 

(b) the total number of delegates to be elected, and the number of delegates 
to be elected from each area, section, constituency or category in 
accordance with sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 25. 


28. Constitution of managing committee.—(]) The managing committee of 
a co-operative society shall be constituted by— 

(a) election from amongst members at an annual general meeting: 

Provided that when the general meeting of a co-operative society is held 
for electing members of the managing committee thereof, and the 
affiliated societies are represented by delegates in such meeting, only 
such delegates of such affiliated societies and no other member 
thereof shall be eligible for election as directors of the first mention- 
ed co-operative society representing the respective affiliated societies; 


(b) appointment by such bodies as may be specified in this behalf in the 
bye-laws of the society; and 

(c) nomination by State Government when it decides to make such nomina- 
tions in terms of section 28. 


(2) A member nominated by the State Government to the managing com- 
mittce of a co-operative sotiety under sub-section (1) of section 28 shall hold 
Office until a fresh nomination is made in his place, and the State Government 
may similarly nominate a new member to fill up any casual vacancy among the 
nominated members.

29. Procedure of holding election in a general meeting.—(1) The election 
of the members of the managing committee (hereinafter in this rule referred 
to as “the committee’) and its necessary office-bearers of every apex socicty, 
central society and primary society having working capital or annual transac- 
tions of rupees five lakhs and above shall be held and conducted in the manner 
specified in this rule: 


Provided that a society may, for the purpose of election of members to the 
committee, divide its membership into different convenient groups, specify in 
its bye-laws the number or proportion of the members of the committce who 
may be elected to represent each such group in the committee and _ specify 
further that such representatives may be elected— 


(a) by all the members of the society, or 


(b) by only that particular group of members of the society to which the 
reperesentative vacating the office belonged. 


(2) The election of the members of the committee shall be held at a general 
meeting of the members of the society or of delegates of such members, 
with not less than fifteen clear days’ notice to each of the members. The 
member elected to preside over the said meeting (hereinafter in 0015 rule 
referred to as the “Presiding Officer”) shall commence and conduct the election: 


Provided that at the commencement of the meeting, except an adjourned 
meeting, there shall be the quorum specified in the rules or the bye-laws: 


Provided further that no member seeking election shall act as the Presiding 
ae and only a member not seeking election shall be chosen as the Presiding 
cer. 


(3)(i) The notice of the general meeting shall be sent to the members or to 
the delegates in one or more of the following modes, namely:— 


(a) by local delivery under proper receipt, or 
(b) by post under certificate of posting, or 
(c) by publication through press. 


Notice of the general mecting shall also be affixed to the notice board of the 
society and published at such public places of importance as may be decided 
by the committee of society. 


(ii) The notice shall contain information regarding— 


(a) the number of vacancies to be filled up by election; 


(b) any area or constituency, that is specified in the bye-laws, {rom which 
the members are to be elected; 


(c) the qualification, if any, prescribed in the rules and bye-laws for 
eligibility for membership of the committee: 


Provided that when there is a conflict between the rules and the bye-laws, 
the provision or the provisions in the rules shall prevail; and 


(d) the date on which, the place at which and the hours between which 
the nomination papers shall be filed by a member, such date being 
not less than four clear days before the date fixed for election; or 
if that day is a public holiday, the next succeeding day which is 
not a public holiday; 


Eaplanation.—in this clause “public holiday” means any day which is a 
ublic holiday for the purposes of section 25 of the Negotiable 
nstruments Act, 1881 (Act 26 of 1881), or any day which has been 

notified to be a holiday for the Government offices in the State. 


(e) the date on which, the place at which and the hour when the nomina- 
tion papers will be scrutinised; and 


(f) the date on which, the place at which and the hours between which 
the polling will take place, if necessary. 


(4) The managing committee shall prepare a list of the members or of the 
delegates who are, on the date of the notice referred to in sub-rule (3), qualified 
in accordance with the provisions of the Act, and the rules and the bye-laws

(10) If the number of candidates for any area or constituency exceeds the

perform the functions of Polling Officers. The provisions in sub-rules (11) to 
(18) shall apply when the election is required to be held by ballot. 


(11) The Presiding Officer shall provide the Polling Officer or Officers with 
the ballot papers, copy of the list of members or of delegates, referred to in 
sub-rule (4) and such other papers and articles as may be necessary for the 
conduct of the election. 


(12) The ballot paper shall contain the names of the candidates, their 
symbols other than accredited symbols approved by the Election Commissioner 
of India, if so desired by the candidate and the seal of the society. 


(13) No ballot paper shall be issued to a voter unless the Polling Officer 19 
satisfied that the person concerned is the same as noted in the list of members 
or of delegates furnished to him. 


(14) If owing to blindness or other ھ7‎ infirmity, or illiteracy, a voter 
is unable to mark the ballot paper, the Polling Officer shall ascertain from him, 
the candidate or candidates in whose favour he desires to vote and shall 
accordingly make the mark on his behalf openly. 


(15) The counting of votes shall commence immediately after the polling 
is declared over by the Presiding Officer and no member shall be allowed to cast 
his vote after such declaration. Votes shall be counted by or under the direct 
supervision of the Presiding Officer. Each candidate and his authorised agent 
shall have a right to be present at the time of counting. 


(16) (i) A ballot paper shall be rejected— 


(a) if it bears any mark by which the member, who voted, can be 
identified; or 


(b) if it does not bear the seal of the society; or 


(c) if the mark indicating the vote there is placed in such manner as to 
make it doubtful to which particular candidate the vote has been 
cast. 


(ii) The Presiding Officer shall be the authority competent to reject a ballot 
paper. 
(17)(i) Soon after the counting of votes is over, the Presiding Officer shall 
prepare and certify a return setting forth— 
(a) total number of ballot papers issued; 
(b) the number of valid votes given to each candidate; and 
(c) the number of ballot papers declared to be invalid or rejected. 


(ii) On the basis of the return, the candidates who have secured the largest 
number of valid votes shall be declared elected at the general meeting and 
their names shall be immediately published on the notice board of the society 
under the signature of the Presiding Officer; and in case of equality of votes 
pulled by two or more candidates, lots shall be drawn in such manner as the 
Presiding Officer may fix, to determine the names of the successful candidate 
or candidates.

the managing committee in the event of the Chairman failing to attend shall 
immediately take custody of the ballot papers and shall preserve them for three 
months from the date of the poll. The ballot papers and other records relating 
to the election shall immediately, in presence of the candidates or their 
representatives as may be available, be secured in a container which shall be 
athxed with the seal of the society and of candidates who desire to afhy their 
seals, if any. They shall, unless otherwise directed by the Registrar, be 
destroyed after the said period of three months, if no dispute relating to, or in 
connection with, that election is referred to the Registrar.

reasons to be recorded by him in writing, of the opinion that the continuance 
in office of such director is not desirable in the interests of the society. 


ee Directors appointed under this rule may or may not be members of the

Shall be filled up by appointment. 


(5) Where the first directors including the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman 
are named in the bye-laws, or in the application for registration of a society, 
a casual vacancy occuriing in the office of such director shall be filled up by 
co-option by the remaining directors.

31. Election and retirement of directors in a primary society other than 
a non-agricultural credit society—{1) The directors of a primary society other 
than a non-agricultural credit society shall retire annually from office and shall 
be eligible for re-election. 


(2) The vacancies caused by the retirement of the directors shall be filled 
up by election at the general meeting at which they retire. 


(3) If at any meeting at which an election of directors ought to be held in 
the place or places of all or any of the vacating directors be not filled up, 
election for filling up the place or places shall be held within three months 
from the date of such meeting and the vacating directors shall be deemed not 
to have vacated their offices till the directors required to be elected in their 
places have been duly elected. 


32. Election and retirement of dirctors in an Apex, Central or Primary 
non-agricultural Credit Society—(1) At every annual general meeting of an 
Apex Society, a Central Society or a primary non-agricultural credit society, 
one-third of the directors elected by the members shall retire from office and 
shall, subject to the provisions of section 23, be eligible for re-election. 


(2) The vacancies caused by the retirement of directors under sub-rule (1) 
Shall be filled up by election at the general meeting at which they retire. 


(3) If at any meeting at which an election of directors ought to be held in 
place or places of all or any of the vacating directors be not filled up, election 
for filling up the place or places shall be held within three months from the 
date of such meeting and the vacating directors shall be deemed not to have 
vacated their offices till the directors required to be elected in their places 
have been duly elected. | 


33. Qualifications of members of Managing Committee.—Subject to the 
provisions of these rules, every member of a co-operative society above the age 
of 21 years shall be qualified to “bé-elécted or appointed as director: 


Provided that in the case of a Students’ Co-operative, a member below the 
age of 21 years may also be elected or appointed as a director. 


34. Nomination by a co-operative society of one of its members as its 
representative to another co-operative society—The Managing Committee of 
a cO-operative socicty may, in a meeting with specific agenda, nominate 
a member of such society as its representative to another co-operative society 
to which the first named society is affiliated and may also recall such represen- 
tative if a resolution is passed by the committee in that behalf at a meeting for 
which such an agenda item was given: 


Provided that at the same meeting, where a resolution of such recall is made, 
there shall be a fresh nomination of another representative of such society, 
that no new representative shall be nominated under this rule until the repre- 
sentative previously nominated has been recalled, that no one shall be nomi- 
nated as representative of a society 1f he is individually a member of the other 
society, and that in case of such recall and fresh nomination by an affiliated 
society in a Single-member constituency, the freshly nominated representative 
shall automatically be a director of the other society. 


35. Cessation of membership of managing committee.—A _ director shall 
cease to hold office— 


(a) if he resigns his office, or 
(b) if he is removed by the general meeting held in accordance with rule 36, 


(c) where he has been chosen as, and is, a director of a society by virtue 
of his qualification of being— 


(i) a member of that society, or 


(ii) a member of ت7‎ other society which is a member either of the 
society hereinbefore in this rule first referred to or of another 
society which, in its turn, is a member of the society herein- 
before in this rule first referred to, 


if such membership of the said director or of any of the aforesaid 
societies linking up the said director with the society hereinbefore 
in this rule first referred to is discontinued for any of the reasons 
provided for in the Act, rules or bye-laws,

(d) if he becomes subject to any disqualification which debars him from 
seeking election as a director, or 


(e) if he fails to attend six consecutive meetings of the Managing 
Committee. 


The cessation of directorship shall be deemed to occur at, and be effective 
from, the time when the disability concerned referred to in this rule first arises. 


36. Removal, expulsion, etc. of the Chairman, directors and other officers.— 
The Chairman of a society or any other officer elected under sub-rule (5) of 
rule 28 may be removed from his office by a resolution of a general meeting 
specially convened for the purpose. 


37. Notice of meeting.—Notice of a meeting of the Managing Committee 
in respect of any society or class of societies shall be given in writing, subject 
to the provision of section 27(1), by the Secretary, or any officer performing the 
duties of Secretary, to every director specifying the place, date and hour of 
the meeting together with a statement of the business to be transacted thereat, 
not less than seven days before the date of the meeting. In case of urgency, 
the Chairman may convene a meeting of the Managing Committee with clear 
three days’ notice: 


Provided that any urgent business, not included in the statement accom- 
panying the notice, may be brought up and considered with the consent of 
two-thirds of the directors present at the meeting. 


38. Meeting of Managing Committee.—The و ا‎ Committee shall 
meet for the transaction of the business of the society at least once in every 
two months; and unless the minutes are drawn up and duly signed by the 
Chairman immediately on the termination of the meeting, the minutes free 
from all alterations and corrections shall be drawn up and _ signed by the 
Chairman within 72 hours from the time when the meeting terminated. 


39. Voting at the meeting of Managing Committee.—Every resolution at 
a meeting of the Managing Committee shall be decided by a majority of votes, 
and if the votes be equal, the Chairman shall have a second or casting vote. 


40. Chairman of meeting.—The Chairman of a society shall preside over 
all meetings of the Managing Committee at which he is present. In the absence 
of the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman shall take the chair and in absence of 
the Vice-Chairman, One of the directors in the panel mentioned in sub-rule 
(5) of rule 28, in order of their names in the panel, shall be the Chairman of 
the meeting. 


41. Quorum of meeting.—{1) Unless a larger proportion is provided in the 
bye-laws, the quorum at a meeting of the Managing Committee shall be 
one-third of the total number of directors subsisting on the date of issue of 
the notice for the meeting. 


(2) No business shall be transacted at any meeting including an adjourned 
meeting of the Managing Committee unless there is a quorum at the time when 
the business of the meeting is scheduled to commence or within half-an-hour 
from the time appointed for the meeting, and a fresh notice in terms of rule 
37 shall then be issued for holding the next meeting. 


42. Requisition meeting.—(1) One-third of the directors may requisition 
a special mecting of the Managing Committee by giving seven clear days’ notice. 


(2) The requisition shall specify the object of the meeting and _ shall be 
signed by the requisitionists and shall be delivered at the office of the society. 


(3) If the Secretary or anybody performing the duties of the Secretary does 
not convene the meeting within seven days from the date of receipt of the 
requisition, a notice signed by the requisitionists specifying the object and 
appointing the date, time and place of the meeting shall be sent to all the 
directors. No separate notice as per rule 37 shall be necesary for such meet- 
ings to be held at the office of the society. 


(4) At such special meeting no business other than that specified in the 
requisition shall be transacted, and if there is no quorum within half-an-hour 
from the time appointed, the meeting shall not be adjourned but dissolved.

43. Powers of the Managing Committee.—The Managing Committee of a 
co-operative society shall exercise all or any of the following powers as may 
be provided in the bye-laws— 

(a) to admit new members; 


(b) to fine, suspend, remove or expel existing members by the votes of 
two-thirds of the members of the Managing Committee present and 
voting at a meeting: 


Provided that no such action shall be taken by the Managing Committee 
without giving the member concerned an opportunity of explaining 
his conduct for which he is to be fined, suspended, removed or 
expelled; 

(c) to raise funds; 

(d) to invest funds; 


(e) to empower any employee, other than those mentioned in clause (21) 
of section 2, to give direction in regard to the business of the 
society; 

({) to appoint, discharge or to dismiss or to remove salaried or ۱18-0 
otticers and other employees of the society, to define the duties 
and responsibilities of the officers subject to the provision of rule 53, 


or to determine the securities to be furnished by the officers and 
other employees: 


Provided that no officer or employee of a co-operative society can be 
dismissed or removed from service of such society except after an 
7و‎ in which he has been informed of the charges against him 
and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those 
charges, and where it is proposed, after such enquiry, to dismiss 
or remove him, until he has been given a reasonable opportunity 
of making representations on the penalty proposed: 


Provided further that in case of urgency, the Chief Executive Officer of 
the society, by whatever designation he may be called, who is 
empowered to settle the duties of other employees, may also 
reallocate the duties and responsibilities of the officers of the society 
temporarily, as the circunst-necs demand, in-between the two 
meetings of the Managing Committee, but if such reallocation is 
required to be continued for a period of more than thirty days, the 
Chief Executive Officer shall obtain the approval of the Chairman 
in respect thereof, and the fact of such reallocation shall also be 
brought to the notice of the Managing Committee at its meeting 
immediately following the date of such reallocation; 


(g) to compound or abandon or delay the enforcement of any debt or 
demand of the society, with the prior permission of the Registrar, or 
to institute, defend or compromise legal proceedings; 


(h) to dispose of application for shares and to issue shares against rebate 
as declared by the Managing Committee, subject to directions given 
by the general meeting from time to time; 


(i) to dispose of applications for loans and to determine the security to be 
taken; and 


(j) to appoint sub-committees as may be deemed necessary from time to 
time and to confer such powers and impose such duties upon such 
sub-committees as may be deemed proper. 


44. Duties of the Managing Committee.—The Managing Committee shall 
observe, in all their transactions, the provisions of the Act, rules and bye-laws 
and shall cause to perform the following duties, namely,— 


(a) to receive and disburse money; 


(b) to maintain true accounts of money received and expended, and 
accounts of the assets and liabilities; 


(c) to prepare for submission to the annual general meeting— 
(i) an annual report on the working of the society; 
(ii) an annual statement of accounts which shall include— 
(a) trading account, 
(b) profit and loss account, 
(c) balance sheet, and 
(d) profit and loss appropriation account;

45. Powers and duties of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman of the society. 
—Unless otherwise provided in the Act, the rules or the bye-laws the Chair- 
man or in his absence, the Vice-Chairman, shall for the transaction of the 
business of the society in cases of urgency exercise all powers and perform all 
duties required to be exercised and performed under the Act, the rules or the 
bye-laws by the managing committee except the power of sanctioning loans 
and ex gratia payments. The Chairman or in his absence the Vice-Chairman 
shall have the power to call for any record of the society or any report from 
the Executive Officer to satisfy himself that the affairs of the society are being 
managed in accordance with the resolutions of the managing committee: 


Provided that the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman, as the case may be, 
shall not act in opposition to, or in contravention of, any order given or 
decision taken by the Managing Committee at its meeting. 


46. Orders of Chairman and Vice-Chairman to be placed before meeting.— 
All orders passed and all acts done by the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman in 
the absence of the Chairman in exercise of his powers and performance of his 
duties under rule 45 shall be placed for confirmation before the Managing 
Committee in the meeting immediately following. 


47. Government officer on deputation to be called Executive Officer.— 
(1) A Government officer, when deputed to the service of a co-operative society 
under section 24, shall be called the Executive Officer of the society. 


(2) Subject to any condition to the contrary that the State Government may 
in any particular case think fit to impose, the Executive Officer shall be under 
the general control of the Managing Committee of the society and shall, in the 
conduct of the business of the society, exercise the following powers, namely:— 


(i) have control over the salaried officers and employees of the society 
with power to sanction leave and to impose any punishment upon, 
or to suspend, any member thereof in terms of clause (h) of sub- 
rule (2) of rule 51 and clause (i) of sub-rule (2) of rule 51 
respectively; 


(ii) institute, defend and conduct legal proceedings in Law Courts and 
other places and enter into compromise or arbitration with creditors 
and debtors of the society.

perform or cause to perform the following duties, namely:— 


(069) receive all moneys on behalf of the society and issue receipts, other 
than receipts likely to create fresh obligations on the part of the 
society, in effectual discharge of the moneys stated to have been 
received therein,

49. Procedure in case of difference of opinion.—In the event of any differ- 
ence of opinion between the Executive Officer and the Managing Committee 
of the society with regard to any matter concerning the affairs of the society, 
not expressly covered by the Act, the Rules and the bye-laws, the Executive 
Officer may refer the matter to the Registrar for his decision, and the decision 
of the Registrar shall be final. 


50. Indemnification of Executive Officer—(1) The Executive Officer shall 
be indemnified out of the funds of the co-operative society for all costs, charges, 
travelling and other expenses incurred by him in the conduct of the society’s 
business or in the discharge of his duties. 


(2) The society shall make such contribution towards the cost of the deputa- 
tion of the officer as the State Government may direct.

(e) from time to time, place before the Chairman, the Managing Com- 
mittee or any other committee of such bank, as the Managing 
Committee may direct, statement of up-to-date receipts and disburse- 
ments, for examination, 


(f) do all other acts that are necessary for carrying on generally the day- 
to-day administration of such bank, and 


(g) perform any other duty which the Managing Committee may assign 
to him from time to time. 


(5) The powers conferred and the duties imposed on the Chief Executive 
Officer under sub-rule (2), sub-rule (3) and sub-rule (4) may be conferred ana 
imposed by the Managing Committee upon any other officer of such bank— 


(a) during the period of absence of the manager from duty, and 
(b) with the prior approval of the Registrar, during any other period. 


(6) When a Government Officer is deputed, under section 24 of the West 
Bengal Co-operative Societies Act, 1973, to the service of such society or bank 
referred to in sub-rule (1), the Manager or any officer of such society or bank, 
during the period of the aforesaid deputation of such Government servant, 
shall not, notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (2), sub-rule (3), sub- 
rule (4) and sub-rule (5), exercise any power or perform any duty which may 
be exercised or performed by such Government Officer under these rules.

or staff in the lower rank, as the case may be.

59, Additional Returns.—(1) In addition to the annual returns prescribed 
in rule 58, the apex societies, the Central Co-operative Banks and such other 
societies shall, if the Registrar so directs, furnish a quarterly return in the 
form set forth in the schedule, showing their working and transactions, and 
such other returns as the Registrar, may, from time to time, require. 


(2) The returns and statements required by sub-rule (1) shall be furnished 
within three months from the close of the period to which they relate or within 
such further time as may be allowed by the Registrar. 


60. Persons who will maintain accounts, books, etc.—The Managing Com- 
mittce shall specify which of the officers and employees of a society shall— 


(a) keep books of accounts; 
(b) keep other books and register; and 
(c) prepare returns and statements: 


Provided that a person charged with the keeping of accounts shall not be 
in charge of cash. 


61. Custody of accounts, books and records.—(1) The books and records 
of a society shall be kept in the custody of the Secretary or any other person 
exercising the powers or performing the duties of the Secretary. 


(2) No member or employee of a society shall, by any act or omission, 
prevent the Secretary or any other person exercising the powers or performing 


the duties of the Secretary from having custody of the books and records of 
the society. 


(3) Any member or employee of a society who commits a_ breach of 
sub-rule (2) shall, on conviction by a court, be punishable with fine which may 
extend to fifty rupees and, where the breach is a continuing one, with further 
fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day after the first during which 
the breach continues subsequent to such conviction. 


62. Preservation and destruction of books, records, etc.—The books and 
records of a society shall be preserved for such period as is set forth in the 
schedule or as may from time to time be directed by the Registrar. 


63. Preparation of statements, etc., at the expense of society and recovery 
of such cost.—{]) If a co-operative society fails to send to the Registrar within 
the time allowed any statement or return required by the Act or the rules, the 
Registrar may cause such statement or return to be prepared by employing 
such staff as he may deem to be necessary and may assess upon the society the 
cost of such staff. 


(2) The cost assessed under sub-rule (1) shall be recoverable from the 
society by the Collector as a public demand upon requisition by the Registrar, 
and the society may recover such cost from the person or persons responsible 
for the neglect. 


64. Documents to be kept open to inspection.—In addition to 016 
documents mentioned in sub-secticn (4) of section 29, every co-operative 
society shall keep open to inspection a copy of the latest audited balance sheet 
and the register of directors. 


65. Publication of balance sheet.—(1) Every co-operative society shall 
publish its audited balance sheet within one month from the date on which it is 
adopted by the general meeting by displaying it in any conspicuous place 17 
the registered office of the society and in every branch office where the business 
of the society is carried on. 


(2) Thé Managing Committee of a society shall in every co-operative year 
lay before a general meeting of the society a balance sheet made up to the 
date not more than three months prior to the date of the meeting or as on the 
last day of the quarter preceding. 


66. Borrowings.—(1) The maximum amount which a society may borrow 
shall be determined annually at a general meeting of the society, and no 


society shall borrow beyond the maximum amount so determined and in force 
for the time being: 


Provided that the Registrar may at any time revise the limit fixed by the 
general meeting.

67. Restriction on borrowings of primary agricultural credit society.—A 
primary agricultural credit society which is a member of a central bank shall 
not borrow by way of loans or deposits from any non-member without the 
sanction of the central bank, and where the society is not a member of any 
central bank, without the sanction of the Registrar. 


68. Restriction on borrowings of limited liability society—No society 
with limited liability shall, by accepting deposits or loans or in any other way, 
incur liabilities exceeding ten times the sum of the paid up share capital and 
the reserve fund for the time being separately invested outside the business of 
the society: 


Provided that— 


(a) the Central Co-operative Land Development Bank, or the _ State 
Co-operative Bank or a Central Co-operative Bank for the purpose 
of financing Land Development Banks, or a Land Development 
Bank for the purpose of financing its members, may incur liabilities 
by floating debentures, accepting deposits or in any other way to 
the extent of twenty times the value of paid up share capital and 
the reserve fund for the time being separately invested; 


(b) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, on agricultural society or a financing bank may incur 
liabilities for the purpose of advancing loans to members for 
production of crops and for financing the disposal of produce, 
repayable within a period of twelve months, irrespective of the 
amount of its paid-up share capital or reserve fund separately 
invested outside the business; 


(c) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, the Central Co-operative Land Development Bank or 
the State Co-operative Bank or a Central Co-operative Bank, or a 
Central or a Primary Society may incur liabilities, irrespective of 
the amount of its paid-up share capital and reserve fund separately 
invested outside the business, for the purpose of carrying on by 
itself or for the purposes of providing loans for carrying on by its 
members, the production, marketing and processing of any 
agricultural or industrial commodity; 


(d) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, a co-operative sOciety may incur liabilities by way of 
loan or deposits from another co-operative society, repayable 
within a period of twelve months irrespective of the amount of its 
paid-up share capital and reserve fund separately invested, if such 
liabilities are incurred on pledge or hypothecation of marketable 
security or goods or both, and the amount of such liabilities does 
not exceed 80 per cent. of the market value of such security or 
goods or both, offered for pledge or hypothecation; 


(e) only in such districts or part thereof, where Small Farmers Develop- 
ment Agency and Marginal Farmers and Agricultural Labourers 
Development Agency have been set up and with the permission 
of the Registrar and under such conditions as he may impose, a 
co-operative society may, for the purpose of financing its agricul- 
turist-members, incur liabilities to the extent of 20 times the sum 
of the paid-up share capital and the reserve fund, for the time being 
Separately invested outgide the business of the society; 


(f) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, a co-operative society composed solely of displaced 
persons and recommended by the Refugee Rehabilitation Com- 
missioner, West Bengal, may incur liabilities irrespective of its 
paid-up share capital and reserve fund separately invested.
