72. Application for loan.—({1) An application for loan shall be in such form 
as may be required by the Managing Committee and shall state the purpose 
for which the loan is required. 


(2) A member applying for a loan shall make such payment as may be 
required by the Managing Committee. 


(3) A member of a primary society applying for loan shall furnish a full 
statement of his— 


(i) property and debts; 
(ii) annual income; 


(iii) annual expenditure including instalment of principal and interest on 
prior debts; and 


(iv) surplus available for repayment of the loan applied for. 


73. Security for loan.—For every loan a member shall furnish such 
security as may be required under the bye-laws or by the Managing 
Committee. 


74. Period ef repayment.—(1) Subject to sub-rule (2), the period of repay- 
ment of loan shall be such as may be provided in the bye-laws. 


(2) Except on such condition as the Registrar may lay down, every loan 
which is granted to a member of a primary credit society other than 2 land 
development bank after the commencement of these rules shall be 19108890913 
within a period not exceeding five years. 


(3) The instalment for the repayment of a loan shall not be in excess of 
the annual surplus income of the applicant estimated by the Managing Com- 
mittee under clause (iv) or sub-rule (3) of rule 72. 


(4) No extension of the period for which a loan is advanced shall be 
granted except on sufficient cause shown and on the application of the borrower 
and with the consent of the sureties or guaranters, if any. 


75. Maximum and normal credit.—The Managing Committe of a co-opera- 
tive scciety shall determine the maximum or normal credit of its members in 
such manner as it thinks fit: 

Provided that— 


(a) in a primary non-agricultural credit society, the maximum or normal 
credit of a member shall be determined after taking into consiedra- 
tion his assets, liabilities and the surplus income over expenditure; 
in fixing the maximum credit regard shall be had to the provisions 
of sub-rule (3) of rule 74; and 


(b) unless otherwise directed by the Registrar, in a primary agricultural 
credit society other than a co-operative land development bank, the 
maximum credit limit of a member shall not exceed the amount 
required by him to cultivate the total lands to be cultivated by him 
according to his production plan and the amount required by him to 
maintain his family during the cultivation season.

ing production or disposal of crop, irrespective of the amount or 
the share capital paid up by such member; 


(f) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, the State Co-operative Bank or any other co-operative 
bank may grant loans to its members against pledge or hypotheca- 
tion of marketable security or goods or both up to a maximum 
limit of 80 per centum of the market value of such security or goods 
or both or against the guarantee of employer of the members of the 
society concerned, irrespective of the amount of share capital paid 
up by such member; 


(g) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, a co-operative society composed solely of displaced 
persons and recommended by the Refugee Relief and Rehabilitation 
Commissioner, West Bengal, may grant loans to its members irres- 
pective of the amount of share capital paid up by such members; 


(h) only in such districts or Pe thereof where small farmers’ development 
agency and marginal farmers’ and agricultural labourers’ develop- 
ment agency have been set up and with the permission of the 
Registrar and under such conditions as he may impose, a co-opera- 
tive society may grant loans to its agriculturist members up to 
twenty times the amount of share capital paid up by such members. 


77. Procedure for prohibiting transactions on mortgage of immovable 
property.—(1) When it appears to the State Government that the lending of 
money on the mortgage of immovable property by any society or class of 
societies should be prohibited or restricted, it shall publish a draft order in the 
“Calcutta Gazette”, prohibiting or restricting such transactions. 


(2) The copies of such draft order shall be sent to the society or class of 
societies concerned. 


(3) The order so published shall not take effect until thirty days have 
elapsed since the date of publication of the order in the “Calcutta Gazette” 
and until the State Government have considered the objections, if any, received 
within fifteen days from the date of publication of the order. 


(4) After consideration of the objections, if any, the State Government may 
withdraw the order or republish it with or without modifications as it thinks 
fit, and on such re-publication the order shall become final and binding on the 
society or class of societies mentioned in the order.

APPENDIX TO CHAPTER IV 
Conditions of Service 
{See rule 53] 


1. Conditions for appointment.—{a) No person shall be eligible for being 
appointed to any post under any co-operative society unless he possesses the 
qualifications prescribed in rule 53: 


Provided that this rule shall not apply to the employees who are already 
in the service or are deputed by the State Government. 


(b) If the Sites jap Committee of any society decides to enhance the 
qualifications or scale of pay of any post in the interest of the business of the 
society that shall, subject to the approval of the Registrar, prevail, but the 
present incumbent of the post concerned shall be absorbed in another post in 
the same scale of pay as was enjoyed by the incumbent concerned at the time 
of his absorption. 


(c) No person who has not attained the age of 18 years shall be eligible for 
appointment to any post under any co-operative society. 


No person over the age of 45 years shall be directly appointed to any post 
of grades I and II; and no person over the age of 30 years shall be appointed 
to any post of grade III and grade IV provided that in case of Scheduled Castes 
and Scheduled Tribes candidates the maximum ape for direct appointment to 
grade III or grade IV posts shall be 35 years and these restrictions regarding 
age shall not apply in ease of promotion or deputation or appointment from 
the service of one co-operative society by another. The following documents 
shall be accepted as proof of age of any person selected for appointment to 
any post under a co-operative society namely:— 


(i) Age recorded in the certificate of Matriculation or School Final or 
Higher Secondary or its equivalent Examination; and 


(ii) A certificate from the head of the Educational Institution last attended 


in the case of those who are not certificate-holders as mentioned in 
(i) above. 2 


(৫) No person shall be eligible for being appointed to any post under ae 


Co-operative Society without a Medical Certificate of fitness to be obtained 
from a registered medical practitioner as may be required by the Managing 
Committee which has 2150 have to be satisfied that he possesses good ء۰٣"‎ 
and antecedents. 


(e) The Managing Committee shall be the competent authority to prescribe 
scales and type of security deposit and/or personal sureties in respect of such 
Category of employees as considered necessary. The Managing Committee 
shall also be the competent authority to revise the same from time to time if 
circumstances so demand. The officers deputed by the State Government will 
not however be required to furnish any security. 


The Managing Committee shall be the appointing authority for various 
categories of posts under a co-operative society. The committee may, from 
rie ie time, delegate its powers in this regard to such authorities as it may 

eem fit: 


Provided that all appointments, including appointment by promotion, shall 
be made on the basis of a test, written or oral, as may be deemed proper by 
the appointing authority.

or special orders to the contrary, employees under the co-operative societies 
shall be graded as follows:

The Setvices of all the employees shall be classified as follows:— 
(i) Permanent, (ii) Probationer, (iii) Temporary. 


A “permanent” employee means an employee who shall be engaged on a 
permanent basis after satisfactory completion of probationary period. 


A “Probationer” means an employee appointed to fill a permanent vacancy 
of a post and has not completed the probationary period specified in the letter 
of appointment or the further extended period. 


A probationer shall ordinarily be on probation for one year. He may 
thereafter be confirmed in the post in his work and conduct are found 


satisfactory. The probationary (0۵ may be extended by another year at the 
discretion of the appointing authority. 


A “temporary” employee means an employee who has been engaged for a 
work which is essentially of a temporary character and likely to be finished 
within a limited period or who is temporarily employed in connection with a 
temporary increase in work of a permanent nature or who is temporarily 
appointed in a leave vacancy. 


3. Commencement of service and seniority.—({a) Service shall be deemed 
to commence from the working day on which a person reports for duty in the 
forenoon. If he reports in the afternoon the service shall be deemed to 
commence from the working day next following. 


Seniority in a particular post of the employees who are already in service 
of the Society on the date on which these rules come into force shall be deter- 
mined according to the date of joining the post. If in case of any two or 
more employees, the date of joining is the same their inter se seniority shall 
be determined according to the age, the older being the senior, and if in the 
case of such employees the date of birth of any two or more employees is also 


the same the inter se seniority shall be decided by the Managing Committee, 
whose decision shall be final. 


(b) Seniority of the employees appointed after the commencement of these 
rules in each category of posts shall be determined in the manner as follows:— 


(iy In case of employees appointed or promoted to a post in one batch, 
the seniority shall be determined in accordance with the orders of 
seniority specified by the appointing authority on the results of 
the test taken at the time of making the appointment or promotion. 


(ii) In other cases, seniority shall be determined with reference to date 
of appointment. But if one or more promotees and one or more 


direct recruits join on the same date the promotees shall be placed 
above the direct recruits. 


4. Pay, allowances and other concessions.—({a) The Managing Committee 
Shall be the competent authority to frame scales of pay, dearness and other 
allowances in respect of each category of employees of the society. The 
Managing Committee shall also be the competent authority to revise the same 
from time to time if circumstances so demand: 


Provided that where any co-operative society has incurred loss in the 
previous year, or has accumulated losses in its account the Managing 
Committee shall not increase the scale of pay or any allowances in respect of 
any category of its employees without the approval of the Registrar. 


(b) Unless anything is otherwise provided in the terms of the appointment 
a person on first appointment to any post under the society shall draw the 
initial pay of the post in the time-scale of pay. 


(c) If any employee is promoted from a post to a higher post or he is 
appointed to officiate in a higher post for a patie exceeding one month purely 
on a temporary measure, his initial pay in the higher post shall be fixed at the 


Stage in the new pay scale next above the stage in the pay scale of the lowe 
post from which he is promoted. 


(d) The annual increment in -the pay scale shall accrue normally to an 
employee after he has completed one year’s service at a stage in the pay scale, 


unless it has been previously withheld for reasons of unsatisfactory work, 
conduct or any other reason.

(6) The Managing Committee may, in special case, allow any employee to

5. Transfer and training——Every cmployee shall be liable to be transferred 
from one post to another in the same scale of pay and/or from one station to 
another in the interest of the business of a co-operative society. Every 
employee shall also be liable to join any training course as may be decided by 
the management and will be entitled to full pay and allowances during the 
training perjod including period of journeys to and from the training centre. 
Any delinquency on the part of an employee in carrying out such order of 
transfer or posting or training will be treated as an act of insubordination 
which may culminate in the dismissal of such an employee from the service 
of the society. 


On transfer from one station to another or for joining a training centre or 
return therefrom every employee shall be entitled to three days’ joining time, 
in addition to the time required for the journey. The Chief Executive Officer 
of the society, however, in special cases may not allow or extend the joining 
time. 


6. Leave.—(a) The following categories of leave shall be admissible to an 
employee of a co-operative society to the extent noted against each— 


(i) Casual Leave—15 days in a year. 


(ii) Compensatory Leave—An employee required to perform duties on 
any Bank holiday(s) shall be eligible for compensatory leave for a 
corresponding number of days. 


(iii) Earned Leave—15 days in a year. 
(iv) Medical Leave—15 days in a year. 


(v) Maternity Leave—6 weeks at a time and not more than three times 
during the entire period of service for a married female employee. 


Leave mentioned in clause (i), (ii) and (iii) shall be on _ full pay and that 
mentioned in clause (iv) and (v) on half pay plus full allowances in all cases. 


(vi) Extraordinary Leave—This may be ذدعئ‎ :)٥ to any employee in 
special circumstances when no other leave is, by rule, admissible. 
This kind of leave shall be sanctioned as leave without pay. It 
shall be at the discretion of the sanctioning authority to fix the 
amount of extraordinary leave to be granted in each case. If an 
employee fails to resume duty on the expiry of extraordinary leave, 
he shall automatically cease to be in the service of the society. 


(b) No leave of any kind can be claimed as of right and the grant of leave 
shall be subject to the exigencies of service and work and the circumstances 
of each case. 


(c) An employee shall be liable to be recalled from leave other than 
medical /maternity leave if the exigencies of work so require provided the 
society bears the actual travel fare of the employee recalled from leave if at 
the time of recall he is spending his leave at a place other than his 
headquarters, |

7. Conduct and discipline-—(a) Every employee of a co-operative society 
shall at all times: 


(i) maintain absolute integrity; 
(ii) maintain devotion to duty; 


(111) abide by and comply with the rules of the society and all orders and 
directions of the superior authorities; 


(iv) discharge his duty to the best of his ability in the interest of the 
society. 


(b) All employees shall so manage the private affairs to avoid habitual 
indebtedness or insolvency; and an employee against whom any legal proceed- 
ing is instituted for the recovery of any debt due from him or for adjudging 
him as an insolvent shall forthwith report the full facts of the legal proceedings 
to the society. 


(০) No employee shall join, or continue to be a member of association, the 
objects or activities of which are prejudicial to the interests of the sovereignty 
and integrity of India or public order or morality or to the interests of the 
society. 


(d) No employee shall, except in accordance with any general or _ special 
order of the Managing Committee or his superior officers or in the performance 
in good faith of the duties assigned to him communicate directly or indirectly 
the contents of any official document or any part thereof or other information 
to any other employee or any person to whom he is not authorised to commu- 
nicate such contents or information. 


(e) No employee shall accept or permit any member of his family or any 
person acting on his behalf to accept any illegal টি or pecuniary 
advantage or gifts, etc., from any person or agent having dealing with the 
society. 


(f) No employee shall engage himself or participate in any demonstration or 
strike which is prejudicial to the interests of the society, of the sovereignty 
and integrity of India, the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign 
States, public order, decency or morality, or which involve contempt of court, 
defamation or incitement to an offence. 


(g) No employee shall, in any radio broadcast or any document published 
in his own name or anonymously, pseudonymousty or in the name of any other 
person or in any communication to the ig or in any public utterance, make 
any statement of fact or opinion which has the effect of any adverse criticism 
of any policy or action of the society, or may embarrass the relations between 
the society, Central Government and the Government of West Bengal, or any 
other organisation related to the Society of which he is an employee: 


Provided that nothing in this rule shall apply to any statements made or 
views expressed by an employee in his official capacity or in the due 
performance of the duties assigned to him. 


(h) No employee shall, except for unavoidable reasons, absent himself from 
tts without taking prior sanction of leave or overstay the period of sanctioned 
eave: 


Provided that the period of authorised training, participation in seminars, 
conferences, with proper sanction, including the period of journeys undertaken 
for that purpose will not be treated as absence from duty.

8. Misconduct and disciplinary action.—{a) The following acts shall 
constitute misconduct of an employee, namely:—— 


(i) wilful insubordination or disobedience, whether in alliance with a 
co-employee or not, of any lawful and reasonable order of superior; 


(ii) wilfully avoiding work or abetment or instigation thereof; 


(iii) theft, fraud, misappropriation or dishonesty in connection with 
employer's business or property or otherwise; 


(iv) habitual absence without leave, overstaying the sanctioned leave 
without sufficient grounds or proper and satisfactory explanation of 
habitual late attendance; 

(v) commission of any act subversive of discipline or good behaviour in 
any public place such as drunkenness, riotous, disorderly or 
indecent behaviour, gambling or taking or giving bribes or any 
illegal gratification of any kind whatsoever; 

(vi) wilful damage to work or goods in process or to any property of the 
society; 

(vii) habitual neglect of work or gross or habitual negligence; 

(viii) disclosing to an unauthorised person any information with regard to 
the society which may come into the possession of the employee in 
the course of his work; 

(ix) indulging in scurrilous attacks against the management and other 
superiors of the employee in his official capacity; 

(x) delivering speeches or raising slogans tending to incite workers to 
violence; ۱ 

(xi) contempt of rules and disrespect of authority and general affront to 
the management; 

(xii) impertinent, rude and disrespectful language which is subversive to 
discipline. 

(b) Any of the following penalties may be imposed for such misconduct by 

the Disciplinary Authority on an employee, namely:— 


(i) dismissal from service which shall ordinarily be a disqualification for 
future employment under the society; 
(ii) 8 ۰۳ in rank to a lower grade in service or post on a lower time 
scale; 
(iii) withholding “of incremnets with cumulative effect; 
(iv) withholding of annual increment, without cumulative effect; 
(v) recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused 
to the society by negligence or breach of orders; 
(vi) censure; 
(vii) fine: 
Provided that the acts of misconduct enumerated in items (viii) and (xii) 
of clause (a) shall be deemed to be minor offences for which any of 


the penalties mentioned against items (iv) to (vii) of clause (b) may 
be imposed and not any of the other penalties. 


Explanation.—The following shall not amount to a_ penalty within the 
meaning of this rule, namely:— 


(i) stoppage of an employee at the efficiency bar in the time scale of pay 
if any, on the ground of his unfitness to cross the bar; 


(ii) reversion to a lower grade or post of an employee officiating in a 
higher grade or post for want of vacancy or on administrative 
grounds unconnected with his conduct; 


(111) reversion to his permanent service, grade or post of an employee 
appointed on probation to another service, grade or post during or 
at the end of the period of probation; 

(iv) termination of service— 


(a) of an employee appointed on probation during or at the end of the 
period of probation or; 


(b) of any employee employed temporarily or under an agreement, in 
accordance with the terms of such agreement or at one month's 
notice, for abolition of the post or otherwise;

(c) for the purpose of imposing any penalty under this rule the appoint- 
ing authority shall also be the ‘Disciplinary Authority’. Except 
where in accordance with rules 47 and 51 the Executive 
Officer, Managing Director, Secretary or Manager of the society, 
Shall be the disciplinary authority. But no penalty shall be imposed 
until the charges against an employee have been properly enquired 
into by an Enquiring Officer to be appointed by the Disciplinary 
Authority and the employee has been given an opportunity of 
explaining the charges personally and/or in writing: 


Provided that if any penalty is imposed by any authority other than the 
Managing Committee of the society an appeal against the order imposing the 
penalty shall lie to the Chairman. When the penalty is imposed or approved 
by the Managing Committee, an appeal shall lie to the general meeting. 


9. Suspension._a) An employee of the society whose conduct requires 
investigation on a charge of misconduct enumerated in clause (a) of paragraph 
8 may be placed under suspension by the Chief Executive Officer of the society, 
by whatever designation he may be called pending the result of enquiry into 
his alleged misconduct, if in the opinion of such authority, the attendance of 
such an employee on duty during the period of investigation of charges against 
him is likely to vitiate the proceedings. 


(9) No employee who has been suspended is entitled to absent himself 
from his station during the period of his suspension. 


(c) During the period of suspension, an employee shall be entitled to 
subsistence allowance equal to 50 per cent. of his salary with other usual 
allowances admissible to him in full or at such rate as will be fixed by the 
Managing Committee from time tu tims. 


No payment of any kind, other than the authorised subsistence allowance 
and other admissible allowance, is to be made to an employee during the period 
of suspension. 


An order of suspension shall continue to remain in force until it is modified 
or revoked by the authority who suspended him or by the Managing Committee. 


(d) When the charge against an employee is held to have been unjustifiable 
or not wholly justifiable, or when an employee who has been dismissed, 
removed or suspended is reinstated, the Managing Committee may grant 0০ 
him for the whole period of his suspension— 


(i) if he is honourably acquitted, the full pay and allowances, if any, to 
which he would have been entitled if he had not been dismissed, 
removed or suspended minus the subsistence, and other such 
allowances drawn by him. 


(ii) If otherwise, such portion of his pay and allowances, if any, as the 
Managing Committee may deuide. 


In any case falling under clause (i) above, the period of suspension will be 
treated as a period spent on duty. In any case falling under clause (ii) the 
period may be treated as on duty or on leave. But it will not be so treated 
unless the Managing Committee directs accordingly. 


(e) If any employee is absent from duty by reason of his being arrested or 
committed to prison either for debt or on criminal charge, he shall not be 
allowed to draw any pay, leave salary or allowances for the period of such 
absence until decision of the case against him, when an adjustment of his 
emoluments may be made according to the circumstances of the case, the full 
amount being given’ only in the event of the employee being acquitted of blame, 
or if the imprisonment was for debt, of its being proved that the employee's 
liability arose from circumstances beyond his control. When full amount is 
allowed, the period of such absence from duty will be treated as a period spent 
on duty. When less than full amount is allowed, the period may be treated 
as on duty or on leave as the Managing Committee may decide. 


10. Resignation, retirement and terminal benefits—{a) A permanent 
employee desirous of tendering resignation from the service of a society shall 
ive three months’ notice to the society in writing, failing which he shall be 
iable to pay an amount equal to three months’ salary and allowances.

Employees of co-operative society shall be eligible to ডিক of gratuity

him and a retiring gratuity at the rate of half of the monthly basic 
pay drawn by him at the time of his retirement for each completed

dies while in service, a death gratuity not exceeding half of the 
monthly basic pay for each completed year of continued service, 
subject to a minimum of three tinges and maximum of fifteen times 
the monthly basic pay drawn by him at the time of his death or 
Rs. 6,000 whichever is less, shall be paid to the person or persons 
on whom the right to receive the gratuity has n conferred by 
the deceased or if there be no such person to his legal heirs. 
Provided that in case of an i,:ex society the minimum should be 


six times of the monthly basic pay and the maximum should be 
Rs. 10,000. 


(3) When an employee after ten years’ of continued service becomes at any 

time physically or mentally incapable of rendering further service 

he shall be granted salary for the period of leave due to him and‏ ۔ 

a gratuity at the rate of half of the monthly basic pay for each 

completed year of service subject to a maximum of 15 times the 

monthly basic pay drawn by him at the time of termination of his 

Service subject to a maximum of Rs. 6,000, where his services are 
terminated for any one of the reasons set forth above: 


Provided that such an employee has to give a written undertaking before 
drawal of such gratuity to the effect that he would not accept any gainful 
employment under any organisation in course of next three years. 


(e) When an employee retires voluntarily or resigns before attaining 50 
years of age, he shall not be entitled to any gratuity.

the Collector by registered post with acknowledgement due and shall show the 
name, father’s name and full address of the member concerned with sufficient 
particulars of the property of, or revenue or loan or advance realisable from, 
such member so as to enable the Collector to identify the property or to find 
out the details of revenue or loan or advance, as the case may be. 


81. Form of declaration for creating charge on immovable property of 
members.—(1) A declaration to be made under section 48 shall be in the form 
set forth in the schedule. 


(2) A register of such declaration shall also be kept by the society in the 
form set forth in the schedule. 


(3) A charge on any immovable property created by a member in favour 
of a society for amounts borrowed or likely to be borrowed by him, from time 
to time, shall, subject to the provisions of clauses (b), (c), (d) and (e) of 


section 48, continue in force till the person creating the charge ceases to be 
a member of the society. 


82. Form of application for demarcation of irrigable area or protected 
area or co-Operative farming area.—A co-operative society shall submit an 
application for demarcation of the irrigable area, protected area or co-operative 
farming area under section 49 in the forms set forth in the schedule. 


83. Notice under sub-section (3) of section 49.—The notice under _ sub-

be published by hanging it on the land adjoining the source of irrigation or on

also by fixing copies of such notice on the notice board of the Collectorate, at

operative society.

85. Form of statement.—The statement referred to in sub-section (3), sub- 


section (7) or clause (c) of sub-section (10), of section 49, shall be in the form 
set forth in the schedule. 


86. Publication of map and statement.—The map and the statement

87. Levy of water and embankment rate.—A co-operative society may levy 
a water rate or embankment protection rate based on— 


(a) such percentage of the value of estimated produce of the land 
benefited; 
or, 


(b) such fixed rate per bigha calculated as to cover within 8 specified 
period all costs incurred together with the interest thereon for the 
provision of irrigation facilities or embankment protection; 


as the Managing Committee of the society, with the approval of the Registrar, 
may determine. 


88. Procedure for notifying non-members to join a co-operative farming 
society.—(1) The directions to be given to the non-members by a co-operative 
society under clause (d) of sub-section (10) of section 49 shall be by a written 
memorandum in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(2) The time within which a non-member shall join the co-operative society 
concerned under clause (d) of sub-section (10) of section 49 is forty-five days 
from the date of receipt of the memorandum referred to in sub-rule (1), and at 
the time of such joining, such non-member shall pay the requisite admission 
fee and the value of one or more shares as required by the bye-laws of the 
concerned society. 


(3) The memorandum referred to in sub-rule (1) shall be signed and dated 
by the Chief-Executive Officer of the society and shall be issued under the 
common seal of the society. 


89. Time within which, and the manner in which, mortgage deed referred 
to in sub-section (2) of section 52 to be sent to the Registeting Officer.— 
(1) The period within which a copy of the mortgage deed, referred to in sub- 
section (2) of section 52, shall be sent to the Registering Officer is thirty days 
from the date of its execution, and before such document is sent as aforesaid, 
it shall be 0৯৯ certified by the Manager, Branch Manager, or any officer of the 
Government deputed by the State Government or the Registrar under section 
24, as the case may be. 


(2) Such a documerit shall be sent to the Registering Officer concerned by 
a messenger or by registered post with acknowledgment due. 


90. Application for compromise between a_ co-operative society and 165 
creditors—(1) An application to the Registrar under section 54 shall contain 
the proposed terms and conditions of the compromise or arrangement and, 
where the applicant is a society, shall be accompanied by a resolution of the 
general meeting proposing the compromise or arrangement. 


(2) On receipt of such application, the Registrar may, if he is of opinion 
that the proposed terms and conditions of the compromise or arrangement 
Shall oe beneficial to the parties, give directions as to the following matters, 
namely:— 


(i) the date or dates when the scheme of compromise or arrangement 
shall be placed before the creditors; 


(11) the time and place where the meeting (or meetings) of the creditors 
Shall be held; 


(iii) the preparation by a person duly authorised by him of a statement 
containing the names of the creditors likely to be affected and the 
amount due by the society to each of them; and 


(iv) the time within which the Chairman of the meeting shall forward his 
report to the Registrar. 


(3) Together with the direction to be given under sub-rule (2), the Registrar 
may refer any question touching the compromise or arrangement for considera- 
tion and decision of the meeting, and the Chairman, of the meeting shall put 
such question to the mecting. 


91. Notice of creditors’ meeting —(1) On receipt of the order of the 
Registrar, the society or the liquidator (in case of a society in respect of whic 
an order of winding up has been passed) shall, before thirty clear davs nf the 
date fixed for the meeting, issue a notice— ۲ھ‎ 


(a) of the date, time and place of the meeting, and

(b) of the proposals for compromise, to every creditor who is likely to be 
attected thereby. 


(2) The notice shall be sent by registered post or through a messenger in 
which case the signature of the receiver shall be taken as proof of service. 


(3) Any creditor desirous of moving an amendment to the proposed 
compromise or arrangement shall send to the society or to the liquidator, if 
any, a copy of his amendment at least fifteen days before the date fixed for the 
meeting, and the secretary or the liquidator, as the case may be, shall send 
copies of such amendment by ordinary post to each creditor to whom the

(4) The proceedings of any meeting held under this rule shall not be 
invalid by reason only of the fact that the notice prescribed was not received 
by any person entitled to receive it where the proof of despatch is satisfactory. 


(5) Any Officer of the society or a liquidator or any person authorised 
in writing in this behalf by the Registrar may attend the meeting, and if so 
requested by the Chairman of the meeting, may take part in the discussion 
but shall not be entitled to vote. 


92. Appointment of proxy by creditor unable to attend meeting.—(1) A 
creditor, who is unable to be present in person in the meeting, may appoint 
another person as his proxy in writing in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(2) The appointment of proxy shal] not be valid unless the form, duly 
filled in, is deposited at the office from which the notice of the meeting 15 
issued at least forty-eight hours before the time fixed for holding the meeting. 


93. Procedure to be followed at meeting.—,1) On the date, time and place 
appointed for the meeting, the creditors present shall choose @ person to be 
Chairman of the meeting, 


(2) Immediately after the Chairman has been elected, he shall read out 
a statement, duly authenticated by an officer authorised in this behalf by the 
Registrar, containing the names of those creditors to whom notices under sub- 
rule (1) of rule 91 have been issued and the amount due by the society to each. 


(3) If as many creditors as are required by sub-section (2) of section 54 
are present, the Chairman shall read to the meeting the term of the proposed 
compromise or arrangement and shall put to the meeting the question whether 
the proposed compromise or arrangement is to be accepted. 


(4) Any creditor بات ا‎ may move an amendment to the compromise or 
arrangement proposed, if he has given notice of such amendment in accordance 
with sub-rule (3) of rule 91: 


Provided that the Chairman may put to the meeting any amendment 
proposed by a creditor of which such notice has not been given, if a majority 
of the creditors present agree that such amendment be considered by the 
meeting. 


(5) Every amendment shall be put to the meeting in such order as the 
Chairman may consider convenient for the purpose of discussion. 


(6) The persons present at the meeting may speak on the motion put by 
the Chairman or any amendment moved thereto in such order as the Chair- 
man may direct. The Chairman may fix a time limit for speeches. 


94. Minutes of meeting.—{1) The Chairman shall cause minutes to be 
prepared of the proceedings of the meeting and shall sign them before leaving 
the meeting. 


(2) The minutes shall contain the names of all creditors present at the 
meeting and if a poll is demanded, the number of creditors voting for or 
against the motion or any amendment moved thereto. 


(3) The Chairman shall forthwith forward to the Registrar a copy of the 
minutes of the proceedings of the meeting together with a copy of the terms 
of the compromise or arrangement, if any, duly signed by him. 


95. Dissolution of meeting, if required number of creditors are not present. 
--The Chairman shall dissolve the meeting if the number of creditors required 
under sub-section (2) of section 54 is not present and shall report to the 
Registrar.

CHAPTER VI 
Property and funds of Co-operative Societies 


97, Investment of funds.—In addition to the manner specified in section 55 
or in sub-section (5) of section 56, a co-operative society may invest or deposit 
its funds— 


(a) with the State Co-operative Bank; 


(b) with the Central Co-operative Bank of the area within which its 
registered address lies (including the branches of the said Central 
Co-operative Bank, if any), 


(c) in any other manner permitted by the Registrar. 


98. Creation of reserve fund in a society with unlimited liability—(1) In 
every co-operative society with shares and unlimited liability, not less than 
one-half of the net profits in any year shall be carried to the reserve fund until 
that fund is equal to one-half of the total borrowed capital; thereafter not 
less than one-third of the net profits in any year until the reserve fund equals 
the amount of borrowed capital, and thereafter not less than one-fourth of the 
net profits in any year shall be carried to the reserve fund: 


Provided that if by any increase in the borrowed capital, the proportion of 
the reserve fund to the borrowed capital is reduced in any year, the share of 
the net profits to be credited to the reserve fund shall be raised to the extent 
required until the proportion is restored. 


(3) In every co-operative society with unlimited liability and without shares, 
not less than three-fourths of the net profits in any year shall be carried to 
the reserve fund. 


99. Use of reserve and other funds in the business of a society—(1) A 
¢5-operative society may, subject to the approval of the Registrar and to such 
conditions as he may impose, use in its business— 


(i) up to one-fourth of its reserve fund, when the owned capital is less 
than the borrowed capital; 


(ii) up to one-half of its reserve fund, when the owned capital is equal to 
or exceeds, the borrowed capital; and 


(iii) the entire reserve fund, when there is no borrowed capital. 


(2) No part of the Bad Debt Fund, Agricultural Credit Stabilisation Fund 
or Inventory Loss Fund, maintained in terms of section 56, shall be used in the 
business of a co-operative society except in accordance with the rules, as may 
be framed by the State Government, for use of these funds. 


100. Provident fund of the employees.—(1) A co-operative society, comin 
within the purview of the Employees’ Provident Fund Act, 1952, shal 
establish, contribute to, and administer an Employees’ Provident Fund 
consistent with the provisions therein contained. 


(2) (a) Other co-operative societies may establish provident fund to be 
called the Employees’ Contributory Provident Fund. 


(b) A society creating such a fund shall, with the approval of the general 
body of members in a general meeting, formulate regulations for its manage- 
ment. Among other relevant matters, such regulations shall provide for the 
following, namelye— 


(i) authority to administer the Employees’ Contributory Provident Fun!;

101, Declaration of dividend, rebate, etc.—(1) In every co-operative 
society with shares, dividend may be declared up to a maximum of 12 per cent. 
per annum, op the amount paid up on shares. 


(2) (a) In any co-operative society dealing in goods, rebate may be allowed 
on the total amount of payments made by a member during a co-operative 
year towards his purchase of goods from the society during that year. 


(b) In case of credit societies, rebate 10 interest may be allowed to members 
making timely repayment. 


(3) No dividend shall be paid by a society with shares and unlimited 
liability without the previous sanction of the Registrar, 


(4) No dividend or rebate shall be paid in any co-operative society unless 
such dividend or rebate is recommended by the Managing Committee and 
approved hy the general meeting. 


(5) A society incurring loss or having accumulated losses on its account 
shall not, without the approval of the Registrar, pay bonus to its employees at 
more than the minimum rate prescribed under the Payment of Bonus Act or 
make any ex-gratia payment to them. 


102. Co-operative Development Fund.—(1) Every society shall, after the 
close of each co-operative year and after the audited balance-sheet is 
considered in a general meeting, while allocating the net profits, if any, make 
such contribution to the co-operative development fund as may be approved 
in the general meeting, subject to clause (a) of section 58. Such contribution 
shall, within two months from the date of the general meeting, be remitted to 
the West Bengal State Co-operative Bank Limited or to the Central Co-opera- 
tive Bank of the area concerned for credit to the fund. Where such 
contribution is remitted to the Central Co-operative Bank, such bank shall 
transfer the same to the West Bengal State Co-operative Bank within a period 
of thirty days, from the date of the receipt of the remittance. 


(2) (i) The funds shall be administered by a committee, called the Co-ope- 
rative Development Fund Committee, to be set up by the State Government, 
composed of the following persons, namely:— 


(a) Chairman of the State Co-operative Union—Chairman. 


(b) Three representatives of Agricultural Societies viz., one from societies 
dispensing short term credit, one from societies dispensing long 
term credit sector and one from marketing societies to be 
nominated by the State Government—Members. 


(c) Two representatives of non-agricultural societies, viz., one from non- 
agricultural credit societies and one from non-agricultural non- 
credit societies, both to be nominated by the State Government— 
Members. 

(d) One nominee of the Registrar—Member. 


(ii) The Executive Officer of the West Bengal State Co-operative Union, 
and in absence of such Executive Officer, the senior co-operation education 
Officer of the said union, shall be the Secretary of the committee. 


(ii1) The members of the committee shall hold office for a term of three 
years from the date of their appointment.

(3) Subject to such directions, if any, as the State Government may give

(a) the education of members, office-bearers, employees and general public 
in co-operative principles and practice; 


(b) the development of new types of co-operative societies; 

(c) the improvement of co-operative societies;

(f) the publication of books relating to co-operative movement;

co-operative movement; 


(h) the award of prizes or honorarium for rendering meritorious services 
to the cause of the co-operative movement of the State; 


(i) any other purpose as may be approved by the State Government. 


(4) The fund shall be audited by the Registrar or by an Audit Officer 
authorised by him in this behalf by an order in writing, annually within a 
period of six months from the close of each co-operative year, and the copies 
of the audit report shall be submitted to the coimmittee and to the State 
Government. 


103. Contribution for charitable and other purposes.—A co-operative | 


society may make contributions under sub-clause (iii) of clause (b) of section 58 
to the Co-operative Employees’ Benefit Fund, the West Bengal State Co-opera- 


tive Development Fund or any other fund which may be approved by the State | | 


Government by a general or special order made in this behalf. 


CHAPTER VII 
Privileges, liabilities and obligations of members of Co-operative Societies 


104. Appeal against refusal to admit any applicant as member of a 
society.—On receipt of an appeal under sub-section (4) of section 59, the 
Registrar shall issue clear seven days’ notice to the appellant and to the society 
concerned fixing the date, time and poe of hearing; and after affording the 
parties an opportunity of being heard, the Registrar shall make such order as 
he deems proper and the order shall be binding on the society with effect from 
the date of receipt of the same. No resolution of the Managing Committee 
admitting the appellant as member shall be necessary. 


105. Disqualification for voting.——No member of a primary or a central 
society Shall be eligible for appointment to vote in the affairs of another 
co-operative society, of which the firstmentioned society is a member— 


(a) if such member is disqualified under the provisions of the Act or the 
rules for voting in the affairs of the society of which he is a 
member or for being appointed or elected as a director: or 


(b) if, in the case of a primary society, the member is in payment of his 
dues and, the Managing Committee has not granted any extension 
of time for making such payment. 


106. Exercise of rights of membership.—(1) (a) Before a member may 
exercise rights of membership, he shall— 


(i) sign a declaration in such form, as may be required by the Managing 
Committee, undertaking that he shall be bound by the bye-laws of 
the society, 

() sign the register of members, and 


Gii) make payment of such amount to the society, as may be determined 


by the Managing Committee, within ninety days from the date of 
demand.

107. Nominal members.—Notwithstanding anything contained in the 
rules or the bye-laws in regard to membership, a_ co-operative society may 
admit in its own interest any person residing in the registered arca of operation 


of a society, as a nominal member, subject to the following conditions 
namely:— 


(a) Any person applying for nominal membership shall submit an 
2pplication to the society in the form prescribed by the Managing 
Committee and make such payment to 006 society as may be 
provided for in the bye-laws. The application shall be supported 
by at least two members of the society. 


(b) The Managing Committee shall, after due consideration, sanction or 
refuse an application for nominal membership, within 45 days from 
the date o receipt of the application: 


Provided that every application for nominal membership shall be dealt 
with in the manner provided for in sub-section (3) of section 59 
and the proviso thereto. 


(c) A nominal member shall be entitled to receive a special type of certifi- 
cate of membership from the society. A register of such members, 
kept by the society, shall be prima facie evidence of the following 
particulars entcred therein namely:— 


(i) the date on which the name of such person was entered in such 
register 25 a nominal member; and 


(ii) the date on which any such person ceased to be a nominal member. 


(d) A nominal member shall cease to be a member on his _ resignation, 
conviction in a criminal case, insolvency, lunacy, bankruptcy, or his 
leaving the area of operation without any intention to return: 


Provided that his obligation to the society as a nominal member shall 
subsist until he has discharged all his liabilities to the society. 


(e) The liability of such members for the debts of the society shall be 
limited to the payment made by them; and all fees paid by such 
members, which shall neither be transferable nor refundable, shall 
be credited direct to the Reserve Fund of the society. 


(f) A nominal member shall sign a declaration to the effect that he shall 
be bound by the bye-laws of the society. 

(g) For the purposes of section 86 and section 126, the word ‘member’ 
shall be deemed to include ‘nominal members’ also. 


108. Associate members.—Notwithstanding anything contained in the 
rules, or the bye-laws in regard to membership, a co-operative society may 
admit in its own interest, any person or an_ association or body of persons 
residing in the registered area of operation of the society, as associate member 
Subject to the following conditions namely:— 


(a) Any person or association or body of persons applying for associate 
membership shall submit an aprlication to the society in the form 
prescribed by the Managing Committee, supported by at least two 
members of the society, and make such payment to the society in 
respect af such membership as may be provided for in the bye-lava.

110. Manner of recalling a loan not utilised for the proper purpose.— 
Where the Managing Committee of a co-operative society has reasonable causé

within such time as may be specified in the notice, why the loan shall not be 
recalled, and where no cause is shown to the satisfaction of the society within 
the time specified, the society— 


(a) may recall the loan, and 


(b) if the loan is not refunded immediately on recall, shall apply to the 
5 for an award under section 126 in order to recover the 
oan. 


111. Restriction on interest of a member of a society with limited liability 
and shares.—Where the liability of the members of a co-operative society is 
limited by shares, no member other than a co-operative society shall hold more 
than one-seventh of the share capital of the society. 


112. Nomination of transferee—(1) A member of a co-operative society 
may, in accordance with section 69, nominate in writing any person to whom 
or to whose credit the share or interest or the value of aah share or interest 
shall, on his death be paid or transferred under the provisions of the Act: 


Provided that such member may, from time to time, revoke or vary such 
nomination in writing. 


(2) Every co-operative society shall keep a register of all persons so 
nominated. 


(3) In case the. nominee of a member dies, the member shall report the 
death to the society.

CHAPTER VIII 


Division, transfer of assets and liabilities, and amalgamation of co-operative 
societies 


114. Publication of preliminary order made under section 76 or secticn 77. 
(1) When the Registrar makes a preliminary order provijing for the— 


(a) amalgamation of two or more co-operative societies into one society 
under section 76, or 


(b) division of a co-operative society into two or more societies under 
section 77, or 


(c) transfer of assets and liabilities of one co-operative society to another 
society under section 77, 


he shall— 


(1) publish such order in the Official Gazette along with a notice calling 
upon the society or societies to be amalgamated or the society or 
societies to be divided or the transferor or the transferee societies, 
as the case may be, and every member or creditor of such society 
or societies to make objections or suggestions, if any, to the 
Registrar with respect to such order within two months from the 
date of publication of such crder in the Official Gazette, 


(ii) simultaneously send a copy of such order and notice, by registered 
post, to such society or societies, and 


(111) expeditiously send a copy of such order to the financing bank of 
which such society or societies may be member or members. 


(2) Every society, receiving copy of an order and notice referred to in 
sub-clause (11) of sub-rule (1), shall, within seven days of their receipt, com- 
municate, in writing, the substance therecf to its members and creditors either 
by delivery by hand after taking proper receipt or by registered post. 


CHAPTER IX 
Audit, inspection and inquiry 


415. Date of audit and audit fees—(1) The audit of a co-operative society 
shall be made and the audit report shall be submitted— 


(i) in case of a primary agricultural credit society, within nine months, 
from the date of the close of the co-operative year, and 


(81) in case of any other society, within six months, from the date of the 
close of the co-operative year: 


Provided that if the audit officer fails to submit the audit report within 
the time as aforesaid, the Registrar shall arrange for completion of 
audit in course of the next three months, in such manner, as he 
may deem fit: 


Provided further that if the Registrar cannot arrange completion of audit 
within the aforesaid period the society shall forthwith get its 
account audited by any of the auditors out of the panel of auditors 


maintained by the Registrar and with the authorisation of the 
Registrar. 


(2) A co-operative society, other than a society dealing in goods 1911 pa 
an audit fee calculated on the average working capital on the last day of eac 
month of the co-operative year, for which the audit fee wil! be due. 


(3) In the case of a society dealing in goods, the audit fee shall be calculated 
on the total value of the goods sold during the year: 


Provided that where a society, in addition to other business, deals in goods, 
the average working capital referred to in sub-rule (2) or the total value of 
the goods sold by the society during the year, whichever is higher, shall be 
taken into account in calculation of audit fee. 


4) The audit fee shall be calculated at the following rates, namely— 


(a) sixty-two paise for every one hundred rupees or part thereof subject 
to the maximum of one hundred and forty rupecs in the case of a 
primary society with unlimited liability; 

(b) sixty-two paise for every one hundred rupees or ‘gab thereof up ٥ 
Rs. 50,000, subject to a maximum of Rs. 250, thereafter Rs. 25 for 
every Rs. 25,000 or part thereof, up to one lakh of rupees, and 
thereafter Rs. 50 for every Rs. 50,000 or part thereof, subject to an

(2) The audit fee paid by a Central Co-operative Bank on behalf of a

118. Payment of Audit fee.—(1) Where the audit of the accounts of a 
co-operative society is conducted by a departmental officer, the audit fee shall 
be deposited, within a period of three months from the date of submission of 
the audit report, in the nearest treasury or the sub-treasury of the area, as 
the case my be, under the appropriate receipt head of the State Government. 


(2) Where the accounts of a society are audited by an audit officer, not 
being a departmental audit officer, the audit fee shall be paid, within a period 
of three months from the date of submission of the audit report, direct to such 
Audit Officer. 


119. Procedure of Audit.—(1) Unless the Registrar directs otherwise, the 
audit of a co-operative society shall be conducted in the registered Office of 
the society and at the branches and pay offices, if any. 

(2) Previous intimation shall be given to the society before the audit is 
commenced: 

Provided that the verification or examination required by clauses (a), (b), 
and (c) of sub-section (4) of section 79 may be carried out without any 
previous intimation to the society. 

(3) The officers and employees of the society shall give the audit officer 
all assistance necessary for the completion of the audit, and for this purpose, 
in particular, prepare such statements and take such action with regard to the 
verification or examination of its accounts, 25 he may require. 


120. Form of Audit statements.—The statements of accounts shall جا‎ 
prepared by the Managing Committee in the form set forth in the schedule 
Or in such other forms as the Registrar may approve. 


121. Scope of Audit—(l) The audit shall include annual audit, running 
audit or re-audit, where considered necessary, by the Registrar. The Managing 
Committee of a co-operative society may further arrange to have its accounts 
internally audited on a periodical or other basis, as deemed proper, by such 
person or persons and on such terms as may be decided by the Managing 
Committee: 

Provided that each apex society shall arrange to have its accounts inter- 
nally audited in such manner and on periodical or other basis as is deemed 
proper by the Managing Committee. 

Ezplanation.—(i) “Annual audit" means audit of the accounts of a co- 
operative society for every co-operative year, 

(ii) “running audit’ means audit of the accounts of a co-operative society 
within the co-operative year on monthly or quarterly basis, as is deemed 
necessary by the Registrar, ‘“re-audit” means audit of the accounts of the co- 
operative society to check up the quality of audit of the society conducted 
by any audit officer. 

(2) The audit officer shall examine the monetary transactions of a society 
in so far as may be necessary for the purpose of ascertaining whether there 
has becn material impropriety or irregularity in the expenditure or in the 
realisation of moneys due to the society and whether any transaction infringes 
any provisions of the Act, rules or bye-laws, or any directions of the Managin 
Committee. In case of difference of opinion between the audit officer an 
the society in regard to the propriety of any of its monetary transactions, the 
Registrar shall decide the matter and the decision shall be final. 


122. Audit objections and audit report—({1l) While conducting the statutory 
audit of a co-operative society the audit officer may issue, from time to time 
during audit, interim objections to the secretary of the society or to the officer 
performing the duties of the Secretary for compliance or explaining the effects 
and irregularities pointed out in such objections within a period not exceeding 
seven days. The secretary or the officer performing the duties of the 
secretary, as the case may be, shall return the interim objection sheets with 
the compliance” report to the audit officer within the time specified by the 
audit officer. The audit officer shall review the compliance report and waive 
such objections which, in his opinion, have been complied with satisfactorily 
and shall incorporate the remaining objections in the annual or running audit 
report, as the case may be. 

(2) In addition to what has_been stated in sub-section (1) of section ر80‎ 
the audit report shall state— 

(a) whether or not the audit officer has obtained all the information and 
explanations which he required;

123. Doubtful debt——If a member fails for three consecutive years 
without reasonable cause to pay at least 25 per cent. of each of the instalments 
of principal and interest fixed for repayment of a loan at the time of its issue, 
then, notwithstanding that on an examination of his assets and the assets of 
his sureties the debt appears to be covered by the value of such assets, the 
debt may be considered doubtful: 


Provided that notwithstanding the provisions of this rule the Registrar 
may, on the strength of advice issued from time to time by the Reserve Bank 
of India, direct any amount of principal and intercst thereon remaining due 
to a society from any of its members to be treated as doubtful debt. 


124. Bad debt.—(1) When the total amount due by a member to a_co- 
operative society by way of principal and interest exceeds the aggregate of his 
assets and the available assets of his sureties, and the amount due by way of 
arrear interest exceeds three years’ demand, such excess of his total dues over 
the total assets shall be considered bad debt. 


(2) A doubtful debt, if not recovered after action has been taken under 
Chapter X or section 126 to recover it or the recovery of which has become 
barred by limitation, shall be considered bad: 


Provided that notwithstanding the provisions of this rule the Registrar 
may, On the strength of advice issued from time to time by the Reserve Bank 
of India, direct any amount of principal and interest thereon. remaining due 
to a society from any of its members to be treated as bad debt. 


125. Writing off bad debts—{1) Any debt considered bad shall, if so 
کول تا‎ by the Registrar, be written off by the general meeting in the order 
below against— 

(a) the bad debt fund, or any fund created out of profits as provision for 
bad debts; 


(b) any other fund created out of profits but not earmarked for any 
Specific purpose; 
(c) the reserve fund constituted under section 56. 


__ (2) Where the society is a member of a financing bank and is indebted to 
it, the Registrar shall consult the financing bank before sanctioning the writing 
off of any debt. 


126. Rectification of defects.—A co-operative society shall remove ٥ 
defects pointed out in the audit report and shall submit to the Registrar a 
compliance report within sixty days from the date of receipt of an audit report 
by the society. In special circumstances, the period of sixty days may be 
extended by the Registrar on the request of the socicty. If the Registrar is 
not satisfied with the compliance report submitted by the society, he shall 
direct it to send further compliance report on the lines specified by him within 
such time as he may specify, and the society shall make further compliance 
report to the Registrar within the time specified by him. 


127. Inspection of societies by officers of financing bank.—An_ officer of 
a financing bank or a society who— 


(i) is a regular employee of the bank or ‘he society, as the case may be, 


and has received training, to the satisfaction of the Registrar, 
necessary [Or inspecting a society, and

(d) members of any local body; or 
(6) Chattered Accountants.

ce stamps.

(4) The Registrar or the Assistant Registrar, as the case may be, shall 


cause proper account of all receipts and payments under this rule to be 
maintained in a separate register at his office.

(2) When an award in a monetary dispute has been obtained against a

ing amounts due to the society by its members. 


Ezplanation.—For the purposes of rules 132 to 135, the expression “0০

(2) Any document or record tendered by a party may, on application, be

(2) Such copies shall be furnished within three weeks from the date of

copyists for the work, where necessary, on payment of remuneration not 
exceeding twenty-five paise for each foolscap page or part thereof, typed in the 
manner as indicated above.

CHAPTER XI 


Winding up and dissolution of co-operative societies 


1686(58) 


138. Winding up Obligatory on the Registrar—Where the Registrar has 
cause to believe that a co-operative society— 
(i) has not commenced working within a period of twelve months from 
the date of registration, or 
(ii) has not carried on business during the previous eighteen months, 
he shall, after giving the society a notice in such manner as he thinks fit, by 
an order in writing, direct that the society be wound up. 


139. Order for winding up of a co-operative society—When the Registrar 
passes an order under section 89 directing the winding up of a co-operative 
society, he shall— 


(a) publish the order— 
(i) if the liability of the society exceeds ten thousand rupees, in the 
Official Gazette; and 
(ii) in any other case, in such manner in the locality as he may think 


(b) communicate the order to the society by registered post, and 


(০) send, by registered post, a copy ot the order to the financing bank, if 
any, of which the society is a member. 


a 


140. Appointment and removal of liquidator.—(1) The liquidator shall be 
appointed— 
(a) in case of the societies having annual transactions of rupees five lakhs 
or above, from amongst the Chartered Accountants or the depart- 
mental officers, serving or retired, and 


(b) in any other case, from amongst the departmental officers, serving or 
retired. 


(2) The appointment and removal of a liquidator shall be published— 


(a) if the liability of the society exceeds ten thousand rupees, in the Official 
Gazette; and 


(b) in any other case, in the locality in such manner as the Registrar may 
think fit. 


141. Remuneration of liquidators.—The liquidator may be allowed such 
remuneration not exceeding two and half per cent. of the assets of the society, 
as the Registrar may decide. Such remuneration may be fixed to cover all 
costs incidental to the liquidation and shall be met out of the assets of the 
society. 


142. Publication of notice—Immediately after the date on which the order 
directing the winding up of the society takes effect, the liquidator shall publish, 
in such manner as the Registrar may direct, a notice in the form set forth in 
the schedule requiring all claims against the society to be forwarded to him 
within one month of the publication of the notice. 


143. Submission of accounts by the liquidator before the Registrar.— 
(1) The liquidator shall submit to the Reyistrar an account of the receipts and 
payments, in the form prescribed for cash account under rule 120 for audit,— 


(a) within three months after the close of every co-operative year, 


(b) where an order under section 89 is set aside on appeal, within fifteen 
days from the date of such setting aside and before handing over 
of charge in terms of sub-section £3) of section 91, and 


(c) fifteen days before making a final report to the Registrar in terms of 
sub-section (9) of section 91, when the affairs of the co-operative 
society concerned have been wound up. 


(2) In addition, the liquidator shall also submit to the Registrar such 
accounts, reports and returns, in such form and in such manner, as the 
Registrar may require, from time to time.

144. Meetings of members and creditors.—The liquidator may at any time 
call meetings of the members, or of the creditors, or joint meetings of the 
members and creditors; and such meetings shall be called, held and conducted 
at such time and place and in such manner as the liquidator thinks fit. 


145. Issue of summons, notice, etc., by a liquidator.—(1)'The liquidator 
may issue summons to persons whose attendance is required either 6০ give 
evidence or to produce documents. 


(2) The liquidator shall himself arrange for service of summons and shall 
send warrants, if any, for execution to the District or Subdivisional Magistrate 
concerned. 


146. Liquidator to keep notes of deposition——The liquidator shall keep 
short notes of the depositions of persons whose evidence he may have taken. 


147. Recovery by certificates.—lf the liquidator fails to recover the assets 
of the society amicably and decides to proceed under the Bengal Public Demands 
Recovery Act, 1913, he shall submit to the Collector in the form prescribed 
under the said Act (printed in the Bengal Certificate Manual) a requisition for 
a certificate against each contributor for the amount of his contribution and 
Shall "0 proceed according to the instructions in the Bengal Certificate 
Manual. 


148. Banking accounts of liquidator—(l) The liquidator shall open an 
account with such bank, as the Registrar may approve, in the name of the 
“Liguidator ءء‎ 0007770 Society”. 

(2) All moneys received in course of the winding up of the society shall 
be paid into such account at the bank immediately after receipt thereof. 


(3) All payments out of the aforesaid banking account shall be made by 
the liquidator by cheques or withdrawal order signed by him and shall be 
নিলা for in the record maintained for the purpose in the office of the 
iquidator. 


149. Distribution of assets.—({1) The audit fees due and payable in terms 
of sub-section (7) of section 91, if any, and all costs, charges and expenses 
incurred in the winding up of the scciety, including the remuneration of the 
liquidator, shall be payable in priority to all other claims. 


(2) After the liabilities other than owned capital as they stood on the date 
of order of winding up are paid off, the assets, if any, left with the liquidator 
may be employed, subject to the approval of the Registrar, for the following 
purposes in the order of priority— 


(1) رسود خی‎ refund to members of any contributions realised from 
them ا(‎ addition to their own personal debts; 


(ii) pro rata refund of share capital; and 


(ili) Pro rata payment of dividend on the shares, if any, at a rate not 
exceeding six per cent. per annum for the period of liquidation. 


150. Meetings of members at the conclusion of liquidation proceedings.— 
(1) At the conclusion of the liquidation proceedings the liquidator shall call 
a general meeting of the members at such time and place and in such manner 
as he thinks fit and place before such meeting— 


(1) a summary of his proceedings; 
(ii) a report of the causes of the failure of the society. 


(2) The members at such meeting, after due consideration of the report 
placed by the liquidator, may, by a resolution, request the Registrar to cancel 
ae registration or the order for the winding up of the society, as they think 

t. 


If there be a quorum at such meeting and the resolution is carried by three- 
fourths of the members present, it shall be binding upon the Registrar. 


(3) When no general meeting of members can be held, the liquidator shall 
report the fact to the Registrar, and the Registrar may, for reasons to be 
recorded in writing, dispense with the provisions of sub-rule (1) and 
sub-rule (2),

151. Final report of liquidator and termination of proceedings.—(1) After 
the liquidation proceedings of a society have been closed, the liquidator shall 
submit a final report to the Registrar together with a copy of his report and 
the resolution, if any, referred to in rule 150. 


(2) On receipt of the final report from the liquidator, the Registrar shall 
terminate the liquidation proceedings by cancelling either the régistration or 
the order for the winding up of the society. 


152. Termination of liquidation procecdings within a specified time 
obligatory on Registrar.—The liquidation proceedings of a society shall be 
closed within a period of two years from the date of the order of winding up: 


Provided that such period can be extended, from time 00 time, by the 
Registrar, for reasons to be recorded in writing, by an aggregate period of not 
more than three years. 


E.cplanatiOn.—In the case of a society which is under liquidation at the 
commencement of these rules, the order for the winding up of the society shall 
be deemed to have been passed on the date on which these rules come into 


operation. 


153. Disposal of books, etc., by the liquidator.—Upon the termination of 
liquidation proceedings, all books, registers and accounts belonging to the 
society and all books, accounts and papers relating to the liquidation proceed- 
ings, which are in possession of the liquidator, shall be deposited with the 
Registrar or such person as the Registrar may direct. 


154. Period after which the responsibility of the Liquidator, Registrar, 
etc., to cease for custody of documents.—After the expiry of three years from 
the date of the order passed under rule 151, no responsibility shall rest on the 
liquidator, or the Registrar or any person to whom the custody of the docu- 
ments may have been committed, by reason of the same not being forthcoming 
to any person claiming to be interested therein.

158. Procedure for appointment of distrainer—On receipt of an 
application from a co-operative land development bank, a central co-operative 
bank or a primary cu-operative credit society, as the case may be, signed and 
verified by the Secretary and the Manager or any other person duly authorised 
by the Managing Committee in this behalf setting forth full particulars of the 
property required to be 01511017060. the Registrar shall, if satisfied that the 
particulars set forth in the application are correct, appoint a distrainer: 


Provided that no distrainer shall be appointed unless the applicant deposits 
such security for cost of the distraint and 9810) as the Registrar may direct. 


159. Powers and functions of the distrainer.— (1) The distrainer on appoint- 
ment shall serve upon the defaulter a written demand specifying the amount 
for which the distraint is made. The demand shall be dated and signed by 
the distrainer and shall be served on the defaulter by delivering a copy to him 
or some adult male member of his famity at his usual place of abode; or when 
such service cannot be effected, by affixing a copy of the demand on some 
conspicuous part of the abode and of his land. 


(2) Simultaneously with the service of notice the distrainer shall cause 
the property specified in the application to be attached by affixing an order of 
attachment in the form set forth in the schedule— 


(a) where such produce is a growing crop on the land on which such crop 
has grown; or 


(b) where such produce has been cut or gathered on the thrashing floor 
or place for treading out grain or the like or fodder stack on or in 
which it is deposited; 

and another copy in a conspicuous manner on the outer door of the premises 
where he resides or works or is known to have last resided. 


(3) Where agricultural produce is attached, the distrainer shall make such 
arrangement fdr the custody thereof, as he may deem sufficient. 


(4) Subject to such condition as may be imposed by the distrainer, the 
defaulter may tend, cut, gather and store the produce and do any other act 
necessary for maturing or preserving it; if the defaulter fails to do all or any 
of such acts, the distrainer may do all or any of them, either by himself or by 
any person appointed by him in this behalf, and the costs incurred by the 
distrainer shall be recoverable from the defaulter, as if they were included, in, 
or formed part of, the order of attachment. 


(5) Agricultural produce, attached as a growing crop, shall not be deemed 
to have ceased to be under attachment or to require re-attachment, merely 
because it has been severed from the soil. ms 


(6) Crops, which are perishable and do not admit of being stored, may be 
sold before they are cut, or gathered. 


(7) No distraint shall be made before sunrise and after sunset. 


160. Sale of distraincd property. —(1) If within seven days from the date 
of the service of the demand the defaulter does not pay the amount for which 
a distraint has been effected, the distrainer may sell, in auction, the distrained 
property or such part thereof in one or more Jots as may, in his opinion, be 
necessary to satisfy the demand together with the expenses of the ٤۶ 
and the costs of the sale. 


(2) Before a Sale is actually made, the distrainer shall cause proclamation 
of the time and place of the intended sale by beat of drum in the village 
in which the defaulter resides or the produce is kept and in such 


other place or places as the distrainer may consider necessary to give due 
publicity to the sale: 


Provided that the sale may be made in the nearest bazar or other place of 
public resort, if the distrainer is of opinion that a better price is likely to be 
obtained there.

161. Investigation of claims, etc.—({1) Where any written claim is preferred

Provided that if the property distrained is of a perishable nature, he shall

(2) The Registrar, on receipt of a claim to a_ distrained property, shall

he thinks proper, and communicate his orders to the distrainer who shall act

Provided that the Registrar may, 11 he thinks fit, refer the claim to the 
civil court: 


Provided further that if the claim is not substantiated, the deposit of 
rupees ten mentioned in sub-rule (1) shall be forfeited and paid to the bank. 


(4) If no application is made to the Registrar within seven days of the 
date of the claim made under sub-rule (1), if any, the distrainer shall, without 
further delay, proceed with the sale. 


162. Private alicnation of property after attachment to be void.—When an 
attachment has been made under these rules, any private transfer or delivery 
of the property attached, or of interest therein, and any payment to the 
defaulter of any debt or other money contrary to such attachment shall be 
void as against all claims enforceable under attachment.

166. Abandonment of sale.—(1) Where prior to the actual sale the 
mortgagor or any person acting on his behalf or any person having interest 
in the mortgaged property tenders payment of the full amount due including 
interest and cost incurred in connection with the sale of the property, the Sale 
Officer shall not proceed with the sale: 


Provided that the sale cannot be abandoned at the instance of the bank 
concerned unless the entire overdue demand is satisfied in full. 


(2) If the Sale Officer considers that the price offered for the property is 
not fair, he may, upon the application of the owner of the property or some 
person authorising to act on his behalf, or the land development bank, central. 
co-operative bank or apex housing society concerned, postpone the sale to 
some other date not later than fifteen days from the date originally fixed, and 
on such date the sale shall be completed unless the price offered is, in the 
opinion of the Sale Officer, grossly inadequate. 


(3) If the price offered is, in the opinion of the Sale Officer, grossly inade- 
quate, the sale shall be postponed to another date, and it shall be sufficient 
proclamation if the time and place of the postponed sale mentioned in sub-rule 
(2) and sub-rule (3) and the nature of the property to be sold are announced 
by beat of drum at some place on or near such property: 


Provided that the Sale Officer shall not postpone the sale more than two 
times on the ground of inadequacy of price: 


Provided further that the Sale Officer shall complete the sale during the 
period of ninety days from the date of receipt of the case. The Registrar may, 
however, extend the date, if considered necessary, by not more than another 
ninety days.

incidental to the sale of the property: 


8 that the Registrar may review the case so determined by the Sale 
Officer. 


. 168. Procedure for the receipt, deposit, etc.—({l1) On every sale of property,
