money to the Sale Officer who shall issue a temporary receipt for such deposit, 
and in default of such deposit, the property shall forthwith be re-sold. 


(2) The balance of purchase money shall be paid by the purchaser to the 
Sale Officer on or before the fifteenth day after the date of sale. 


(3) On payment of the balance of the purchase money, the Sale Officer 
shall grant a final receipt for the entire sale price. 


(4) All money received by the Sale Officer on the sale of mortgaged 
property shall, as soon as possible but not later than seven days after such 
receipt, be deposited in the co-operative land development bank, the central 
co-operative bank or the apex housing society, as the case may be. 


169. Procedure in default of payment of full amount of purchase moncy.— 
(1) If the balance of the purchase money, referred to in sub-rule (2) of rule 168, 
is not paid within the specified period, the deposit shall be forfeited 1০ the 
bank or the society, and the property shall be re-sold. 


(2) The defaulting purchaser shail forfeit all claims to the property or to 


ay oe of the deposit of the sum for which the property may subsequently 
e sold. 


(3) Every re-sale, in default of payment of the purchase money within the 
period allowed for such payment, shall be made after the issue of a fresh 
proclamation- and in the manner hereinbefore prescribed for the sale. 


(4) Any deficiency of price which may ensue from a re-sale by reason of 
the purchaser’s default and all expenses attending such re-sale shall be 
certified by the Sale Officer, and shall be met out of the forfeited deposit 
referred to in sub-rule (1). The amount, which cannot be so met, shall be 
recoverable from the defaulting purchaser, on application before a civil court 
having jurisdiction: 


Provided that no such application shall be entertained unless made within 
thirty days of the date of re-sale.

170. Application to sct aside a sale.x—An application under section 105 to 
have a Sale set aside shalt be made within thirty days of the date of the sale: 


Provided that the Registrar may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, 
entertain an application beyond the period of thirty days. 


171. Return of purchase money and compensation.—(1) Where a sale 15 
set aside on an application under section 106, the Registrar shall intimate to 
the land development bank or the saciety concerned his order setting aside 
the sale, and on receipt of such order the managing committee of the bank 
or the society concerned shall issue a notice to the purchaser to appear on a 
date specified in the notice at the office of the bank or the society concerned 
and receive repayment of the purchase money and such compensation as may 
be due to him. 


(2) In the event of a dispute regarding the claim to the purchase money 
and compensation, the bank or the society concerned shall withhold payment 
and refer the disputants to the proper court for adjudication of their claim. 


(3) The purchase money and compensation shall remain with the bank or 
the society concerned till the dispute is decided by a court. 


172. Form and method of submission of a report.—The report to the 
Registrar under sub-section (1) of section 106 shall contain the following 
particulars:— 

(1) Name of Sale Officer. 

(2) Date of sale. 

(3) Place of sale. 

(4) Description of property sold. 

(5) Name of purchaser ard address. 

(6) Value realised. 

(7) Amount of claim of the bank including interest. 

(8) Cost of sale. 


(9) Application, if any, under section 105 and manner of disposal of such 
application. 


173. Form of notice to be served on landlord by purchaser shall be in the 
form annexed in the schedule.—(1) The Registrar shall grant a sale certificate 
to the purchaser in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(2) A purchaser of any mortgaged property shall supply to the Registrar 
a notice, in the form set forth in the schedule, for service on the State of West 
Bengal through the Collector of the district concerned. 


(3) The purchaser shall pay a ‘ee of two rupees for service of notice 
referred to in sub-rule (2). 


(4) The notice shall be served on the State of West Bengal through the 
Collector of the district concerned, as the case may be. 


174. Delivery of possession by Registrar to purchaser.—(1) Where the 
mortgagea property sold is in the occupancy of the mortgagor or of some 
person on his behalf or of some person claiming under a title created by the 
mortgagor subsequent to the mortgage in favour of the land development bank, 
the central bank or the apex housing society and a certificate in respect thereof 
has been granted under section 108, the Registrar shall, on the application of 
the purchaser, order delivery to be made by putting such purchaser, or any 


person whom he may appoint to reccive delivery on his behalf, in possession 
of the property. 


(2) Where the property sold is in the occupancy of a tenant or other person 
entitled to occupy the same and a certificate in respect thereof has been 
granted under section 108, the Registrar shall, on the application of the 
purchaser, and after notice to such tenant or other person, order delivery to 
be made by affixing এ copy of the certificate of sale in some conspicucus place 
on the property and proclaiming to the occupant by beat of drum at seme 


convenient place that the interest of the mortgagor has been transferred to the 
purchaser. 


(3) In regard to the cases dealt with in sub-rules (1) and (2) the rovisions 
of rules 97 to 103 of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil 
Procedure, 1907, shall, mutatis mutandis and so far as may be, apply.

175. Procedure for the disposal of property purchased by land development 
bank.—(1) Unless otherwise directed by the trustee, a purchasing bank or 
society concerned shall dispose of the property, purchased by it, by public 
auction, on a specified date not later than one year from the date of purchase. 


(2) The sale shall be previously advertised by— 
(a) advertising the property with full details in the local newspaper; 
(b) proclamation by beat of drum in the village where it is situate; and 


(c) publication of the sale notice in the office of— 
(1) Junior Land Reforms Officer concerned, 
(11) the Collector of the district, 
(111) the Block Development Officer of the area concerned, and 
(iv) Panchayat of the area in which the property is situate. 


176. Appointment of receiver and his duties, powers, functions and remu- 
neration.—(1) On an application by a land development bank, a_ central co- 
operative bank or the apex housing society, the Registrar may, by an order in 
writing, appoint a receiver. The receiver so appointed shall be entitled either 
to take possession of the property ur collect its produce and income as_ the 
case may be, to retain, out of the money realised by him, his expenses of 
management including his remuneration, if any, as may be fixed by the Registrar 
in consultation with the bank or the society, and to apply the balance in 
accordance with the provisions of sub-section (8) of section 69A of the Transfer 
of Property Act, 1882. 


(2) The receiver shall open an account with the nearest central co-operative 
bank or the unit of the State co-operative bank. 


(3) All moneys received shall be paid immediately into such account. 
(4) The receiver shall duly— 


(a) account for all sums of money which he may receive in respect of 
the property; and 


(b) submit his accounts at the end of every month to the land develop- 
ment bank, the central co-operative bank or the apex housing 
scciety and at the same time forward a copy thercof to the 
Registrar. 


(5) A receiver appointed under this rule may, for just and sufficient cause 
or on application made by the co-operative land development bank, the central 
co-operative bank or the apex housing society, be removed by the Registrar. 


(6) A vacancy in the office of the receiver may be filled up by the Registrar. 


177. Procedure, if value of property rendered insufficient—(1) When a 
member fails to give further security required by a land development bank, a 
central co-operative bank or the apex housing society, as the case may be, 
under section 114, the bank or the society may, and-if directed by the Registrar 
Shall, proceed to take action for the recovery of the loan outstanding in the 
manner provided in Chapter XII of the Act and the rules framed thereunder. 


(2) The value of the security to be furnished for obtaining any loan from 
any co-operative land development bank shal! be equal to the total value ০01 
the land to be mortgaged and the cost of the improvement to be effected. 
The amount of loan to be advanced as aforesaid shall not exceed fifty per cent. 
of the said total value of the land and the cost of improvement. 


(3) A security shall be deemed to be insufficient, if the value of the residue 
of the property docs not exceed the loan outstanding by one-third of such 
loan or by such other greater proportion, as may be provided in the bye-laws 
of the bank or the society, as the case may be. 


178. Action to be taken, if bank fails to proceed under section 99 or 101 
or 114.—If on a report of the Registrar or any officer authorised to inspect 
such banks it appears to the trustee of the central land development bank 
that a land development bank has neglected or failed to take action against a 
mortgagor under section 99, 101 or 114, as the case may be, the trustee of 
the central land development bank shall be entitled, after giving both the 
mortgagor and the land development bank an opportunity to file any objection, 
to take action against the ৮৮০৮1170017 for the recovery of the loan.

179. Fees payable to Collector for notifying encumbrances.—{1)} The fee 
payable to the Collector under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 117 shall 
not exceed half per cent. of the value of the notified property, subject to a 
maximum of two rupees. 


(2) The fee shall be accompanied by a statement containing material 
particulars in respect of the mortgage deed executed in favour of the bank or 
the society, as the case may be. : 


CHAPTER XIII 
Enforcement of obligations and recovery of sums due 


180. Restriction on issue of warrants.—No warrant for enforcing attend- 
ance of witnesses shall be issued, without the previous. sanction of the 
Registrar, by an audit officer, an arbitrator, a liquidator or any other person 
conducting an enquiry or inspection under Chapter IX of the Act. 


181. Procedure for conditional attachment of property—(1) An _ applica- 
tion to the Registrar for a conditional order of attachment shall contain— 


(a) full details of the property to be attached, its estimated value and the 
claim of the society; and 


(b) evidence in support of the contention that the pe:son or the co-opera- 
tive socicty concerned is about to remove or dispose of the 


property. 


(2) Order of attachment, if any, passed by the Registrar shall be served by 
such person as the Registrar may empower. The person so empowered shall 
follow, as far as possible, the procedure laid down in Order XXI of the First 
Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. 


182. Power under section 126.—District Auditor of Co-operative Societies 
and Co-operative Development Officers may exercise the power under 
section 126, when the claim does not exceed Rs. 2,000, and Inspectors of 
Co-operative Societies may exercise the said power, when the claim does not 
exceed Rs. 1) 


183, Procedure of disposal of proceedings drawn up by the Registrar 
under section 127.—When the Registrar holds an enquiry under section 127, 
he shall draw up proceedings against the officer concerned, showing the 
charges against him and shall— 


(i) supply the officer concerned with a copy of the proceedings and a 
summary of the evidence which, prima facie, appears; 


(01) call on the officer to furnish his explanation within a fortnight; 
(111) receive and record such evidence as may be adduced; and 


(iv) record a decision as early as possible but not later than three months 
from the date of drawing up proceedings. 


184. Culpable negligence.—Negligence in the following matters shall be 
deemed culpable within the meaning of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of 
section 127, namely— 


(i) investment, custody and employment of funds and use or disposal 
of stores or other assets or properties contrary to the provisions 
of the Act, rules or bye-laws or any written direction of the 
Registrar given in accordance therewith; 


(ii) failure to remedy audit defects and irregularities, when directed by 
the Registrar under section 80; and 


(111) failure to file disputes against defaulters and to execute any decree 
Or award within the period of limitation. 


185. Penalty for certain misdemeanour under section 128.—If no cause is 
shown within a specified time or the cause shown is not considered satisfac- 
tory, the Registrar may order a penalty for every contravention referred to 
in— 


(1) clauses (a) and (b) of section 128—a sum not exceeding fifty rupecs;

186. Officer responsible for carrying out the direction of Registrar.—(1) 
In deciding under section 129 which officer is to be held responsible for the 
carrying out of his directions, the Registrar shall always consider the secretary 
or the Chief Executive Officer of the society, by whatever designation he may 
be called, to be responsible unless there is anything in the bye-laws, or in any 
resolution of the general meeting or the managing committee by which a 
particular duty is entrusted to any officer other than the secretary or the 
Chief Executive Officer. 


(2) In accordance with sub-rule (1), the Registrar may call on such person. 
as he may hold responsible, to carry out any of his directions within such time 
as a کت‎ specify, and on his failure, may take action against him under

CHAPTER XIV 
Jurisdiction, Appeal and Revision 


187. Co-operative Tribunal.—({1) The co-operative tribunal, referred to 
in Section 133, shall consist of not more than three members of whom there 
shall be a President, when such tribunal shall consist of more than one 
member; and the President shall be either a serving or retired High Court 
quate or a Serving or retired member of the West Bengal Higher Judicial 

ervice. 


(2) A person shall not be qualified for appointment as a member of the 
co-operative tribunal unless— 


(a) he a a serving or retired member of the West Bengal Higher Judicial 
rvice, 


(b) he has served as Registrar of Co-operative Societies or Additional 
Registrar of Co-operative Societies in any State, or 


(c) for at least ten years he has been a practising lawyer in any court in 
West Bengal, and since the last five years actively associated with 
the co-operative movement in the State. 


(3) The tribunal shall have a Secretary to be appointed زا‎ the State 
Government by notification in the Official Gazette. Such Secretary shall 
perform such functions as shall be assigned to him by the tribunal or by 
regulations made under sub-section (7) of section 133. 


(4) The method of disposal of its business by the co-operative tribunal 
(hereinaiter referred to as the tribunal) shall, til it makes regulations under 
sub-section (7) of section 133, with the previous approval of the State Govern- 
ment, for regulating its procedure and disposal of its business, be as follows:— 


(a) every memorandum of appeal, application for review shall be 
presented in person by the appellant or the applicant, as the case 
may be, or by his pleader or duly appointed agent to the Secretary, 
West Bengal Co-operative Tribunal within office hours of the 
tribunal or sent to such secretary by registered post. 


Explanation: ‘pleader’ means a pleader as defined in clause (15) of 
section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. 


(b) Where a memorandum of appeal or application for review is signed 
and presented by a pleader or an agent, it shall be accompanied by 
a vokalatnama bearing a court fee stamp of Re. 1 or a letter of 
authority, as the case may be, appointing him as such and duly 
signed by the appellant or the applicant, as the case may be. 


(c) Every memorandum of appeal or application for review shall— 
(i) be either type-written or written in ink in legible handwriting; 


(ii) state the name and address of the appellant or applicant, as the case 
may be, and also those of the respondent or the Opposite party, 


as the case may be;

جب ———————————— 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, SEPTEMBER 2, 4 


(iii) state the date of the order complained of and the authority by 
which the order was passed; 

(iv) state clearly the grounds on which the memorandum of appeal or 
the application for review is made; 


(v) state precisely the relief that the appellant or the applicant claims; 


(vi) bear a court fee stamp of rupees two in case of memorandum of 
appeal and of rupees five in caSe of application for review. 


(d) Every memorandum of appeal or application for review shall be 
accompanied by a certified copy of the award or order complained 
of. The memorandum of appeal or the application for review, as 
the case may be, shall be further accompanied by as many copies 
of the memorandum or the application as there are respondents or 
opposite parties. 


(e) No memorandum of appeal or application for review shall be accepted 
by the secretary unless it conforms to the provisions of clause (b), 
clause (c) and clause (d) above. 


(f) On receipt of every memorandum of appeal or application for review, 
the secretary shall endorse on it the date of its receipt. The 
secretary Shall, as soon as practicable, examine— 


(i) whether the person presenting it has authority to do so; 

(ii) whether it is.made within the period of limitation (if any) laid 
down in the Act; and 

(iii) whether it conforms to the provisions of the Act and these rules. 


If the secretary is satisfied on these points, he shall cause the memoran- 
dum of appeal or the application to be registered in an appropriate 
register maintained under clause (g). 


If the secretary finds that the memorandum of appeal or application 

‘aaa tie to him does not conform to any of the aforesaid provisions, 

e shall make a note to that effect and call upon the party concerned 

or his pleader or agent, to remedy the defects within a _ period of 

seven days from the date of receipt of notice requiring him to do so. 

The secretary may, for sufficient cause extend the period for the 
purpose of remedying the defects: 


Provided that-if the extension of more than fifteen days is sought for, the 
Secretary shall place the matter before the tribunal and obtain its 
order in that behalf. 


If the defect in the memorandum of appeal or application is remedied the 
Secretary shall cause it to be registered in the appropriate register. 


(g) The secretary shall maintain separate registers for— 


(i) memoranda of appeal in Form A; 
(ii) applications for review in Form B; 
(iii) miscellaneous applications in Form C; 
(iv) unregistered memoranda of appeals and applications in Form D; 
(v) court fees received in Form E. 


These Forms are set out in the appendix to this Chapter. 


(h) When a memorandum of appeal or an application has been registered, 
the secretary shall, as soon as may be, send an intimation thereof 
to the Registrar of Co-operative Societies or other officer 
concerned, calling for the records and proceedings relating to such 
memorandum of appeal or application unless those records and 
proceedings are already in the office of the tribunal. 


(i) After the registration of the memorandum of appeal or application 
the tribunal shall fix a date of hearing of the same. After the date 
of hearing is fixed a notice in Form F (contained in the appendix 
to this Chapter) shall be served by the Secretary on-the parties 
concerned calling upon them to appear before the tribunal either 
in person or through their pleader or agent on the date specified in 
the notice or oh any subsequent date to which the hearing may be 
adjourned by the tribunal.

On the date fixed for hearing or any other date to which the hearing may 

be adjourned, the appellant or 2pplicant or his pleader or agent shall 

ordinarily be heard first in support of his appeal or application. The 

respondent or the opposite party or his pleader shall, if necessary, be 

heard next, and the appellant or the applicant or his pleader shall, in 

case where the respondent or the opposite party or his pleader 1s 

heard, be entitled to a right to reply. 


If on the date fixed for hearing or any other date to which the hearing 
may be adjourned, the appellant or the applicant does not appear 
either in person or through his pleader or agent when the appeal or 
application is called for hearing and if the tribunal finds no reason 
to adjourn the hearing of the appeal or application, as the case may 
be, the tribunal may dismiss the appeal or the application, as the 
case may be, or may decide it on merits after hearing the respondent 
or his pleader or agent. 


If on the date fixed for hearing or any other date to which the hearing 
may be adjourned, the respondent or the opposite party does not 
appear in person or through his pleader or agent when the appeal or 
application is called for hearing and if the tribunal finds no reason 
to adjourn the appeal or application, as the case may be, the tribunal 
may decide the same on merits after hearing the appellant or 
applicant, as the case may be, or his pleader or agent. 


(j) If any of the parties was absent on the date of hearing and the appeal 
or application was heard and decided in the absence of that party, 
such party may apply for restoration of the appeal or application, 
as the case may be, and if the party satisfies the tribunal that he 
had no notice of the hearing or that he was prevented by any 
sufficient cause from appearing when the appeal or application was 
heard and decided, the tribunal may restore the appeal or 
application, as the case may be, to its file: 


Provided that where the other party had appeared at the hearing, such 
party shall be given notice and an opportunity of being heard 
before the order for restoration is made. 


(k) When the hearing of an appeal or application concludes the tribunal 
may pronounce its judgement or order in open court forthwith or 
may fix a date for the same. The tribunal shall state at the end 
of its judgement or order whether the appeal or application is 
dismissed or allowed wholly or in part and mention the relief, if 
any, granted to the appellant or applicant, as the case may be. 


The costs of appeal or the application shall be in the discretion of the 
tribunal and in case where costs are awarded the tribunal shall 
State which party shall bear the costs and in what proportion, if 
any. 


0) A certified copy of every judgement or final order of the tribunal 
shall, as soon as practicable, be forwarded to the Registrar of Co- 
operative Societies or such other officer appointed to assist him as 
may be concerned with the appeal or application, as the case may 
be. Certified copies of the judgement or final order may also be 
supplied to the parties on application being made in that behalf 
and on payment of such fees as 276 prescribed in sub-rule (1) of 
rule 137. Sub-rule (2) of rule 137 shall mutatis mutandis apply in 
these cases. 


188. Court-fee stamp necessary on application for reference or appeal.— 
An application for reference or a memo of appeal to the prescribed authority, 
other than the co-operative tribunal referred to in section 133, shall bear a 
court-fee stamp of two rupees: 


Provided that no such court-fee stamp shall be necessary in the case of an 
appeal preferred against the decision of a society under section 59 refusing to 
admit as member any person applying for membership.

CHAPTER XV 
Offences, Penalties and Procedure 


* 189. Certified copies of entries in books.—A copy of any entry in a book 
of a co-operative society may be certified by a declaration written at the foot 
of such copy that it is a true copy of such entry, that such entry is contained 
in one of the ordinary books of the society (to be named) and was made in 
the usual and ordinary course of business, and that such book is still in the 
custody of the society; such certificate shall be dated and _ signed by the 
Secretary, Chairman, the Executive Officer or the Chief Executive Officer of 
the society by whatever designation he may be called. 


190, Procedure and condition for obtaining copies of documents.— 
Certified or uncertified copies of any document which a member of the public 
has a right to inspect under the Act, the rules or the bye-laws of a co-opera- 
tive society or which a member of such society may require. shall, on 
application, be supplied, within a month, from the date of such application on 
payment of a sum calculated at twenty-five paise for each hid red words or 
a part thereof. 


19], Fees for inspection of public documents filed in the office of the 
dad argh Any member of the public may, on payment of a fee of one 
rupee for each occasion Of inspection, with the permission of the Registrar, 
inspect, for an lawful purpose, any public documents (exclusive of documents 
privileged under sections وو ڑج‎ and TT or the Indian Evidence Act, 
1872), filed in the office of the Registrar and, in particular, the following 
documents namely;— টি 7272 


(a) certificate of registration of a co-operative society; 
/€6) bye-laws of a co-operative society and amendment effected in such 
bye-laws; 
(c) order directing the winding up of a co-operative society;- 
(d) order cancelling the registration of a co-operative society; 
(e) annual returns; 
(f) register of co-operative societies.

(2) (a) Certified copies of any document which a person has a right under 
sub-rule (1) to inspect may be obtained by him on application made to the 
Registrar and on payment of— 


(i) three rupees for certificate of registration; and

a part thereof of the copy or extract of any other document, 


(b) Such certified copies shall be furnished within such period and in such 
manner as provided for in sub-rule (2) of rule 137. 


192. Payment of fees—(1) Unless the State Government otherwise 
directs, all fees, payable to it under the Act or the rules except audit fees, 
Shall be paid in court-fee stamps. 


(2) Audit fees payable to Government or to an audit officer, not being a 
Government officer and, dues and fees payable to a co-operative society shall 
be paid in cash, by cheque or by bank draft under proper receipt. 


CHAPTER XVI 
Miscellaneous 


193. Penalty—Any person committing a breach of any of the rules of the 
West Bengal Co-operative Societies Rules, 1974, shall, at the instance of the 
Registrar or of any co-operative society with the approval of the Registrar, on 
conviction by a Magistrate having juriSdiction over the place where such 
person resides, be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred 
rupees, and where the breach is a continuing one, with further fine which ma 
extend to ten rupees for every day after the first during which the breac 
continues subsequent to such conviction.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
LEGISLATIVE DEPARTMENT 


NOTIFICATION 


No: 2102-L.—4th September, 1974.—The following Act of the West Bengal Legislature, having been 
assented to by the President, is hereby published for general information سے‎ 


West Bengal Act XXXIX of 1974 


THE WEST BENCAL COMPREHENSIVE AREA 
DEVELOPMENT AcT, 1974. 


[Passed by the West Bengal Legislature.] 


[Assent of the President was first published in the Calcutta 
Gazetie, Extraordinary, of the 4th September, 1974.] 


An Act to provide for development of the State of West Bengal 
through area based development programme with a view 
to increasing agricultural and allied production and 
ensuring mazimum benefits of such production to the 
cultivators. 


WHEREAS it is expedient in the public interest to provide 
for development of the State of West Bengal through area 
based development programme with a view to increasing 
agricultural and allied production and ensuring maximum 
benefits of such production to the cultivators and thereby to 
give efiect to the policy of the State towards securing the 
principles specified in টিন (৮) and clause (০) of article 39 
of the Constitution of India; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
re ublic of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 
follows :— 


Short title, 1. (1) This Act may be called the West Bengal Compre- 


16081۲٥ Area Development Act, 1974.‏ یں یت 
encement. (2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal.‏ 


(3) It shall come into force on such date or dates as the 
State Government may, by notification in the Oficial Gazette, 
appoint and different dates may be appointed for different 
provisions of this Act‘or for different areas. 


Defini- 2. In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in 
tions. the subject or context,— 

(a) “agricultural production’? includes production of 
agriculture, horticulture, pisciculture, forestry, 
sericulture, hee-keeping, dairy farming, piggery 
and pouliry farming and also includes such other 
types of production as are ancillary or incidental 
thereto and as the State Government may, by 
notification in the Oficial Gazette, specify as 
agricultural production ;

(c) ‘‘cultivator’’ means a person engaged in agricultural 
production either in the capacity of an owner or 
wn lessee or a bargadar or a labourer; 


(d) ‘‘notified area’’ means an area notified under sub-

3. (1) The State Government shall, as soon as may be 
after the commencement of this Act, by a notification in the 
Oficial Gazette, establish for the State of West Bengal a 
Corporation to be called the West Bengal Comprehensive 
Area Development Corporation. 


(2) The Corporation shall be a body corporate having 
perpetual succession and a common seal and may by the said 
name sue or be sued. 


4 (i) The Corporation shall consist of a Chairman, a 
Vice-Chairman, and such number of _other members not 
exceeding thirty as the State Government may think fit to 
appoint. 


(2) The terin of office of, and the manner of filling casual 
vacancies among, the members of the Corporation shall be 
such مد‎ may be prescribed. 


5. The State Government may remove from office any 
member of the Corporation who has, in the opinion of the 
State Government, so ubused his position as to render his 
continuance in office as a member of the Corporation 
detrimental to the interests of the Corporation. 


6. (J) The State Government shall, subject to such terms 
and conditions as may be prescribed, appoint a member of the 
Corporation to be the Executive Vice-Chairman of the 
Corporation who shall be ita Chief Executive Officer. 


(2) The Executive Vice-Chairman shall exercise such 
powers and perform such duties as may be provided by 
regulations. 


7. Subject to such terms and conditions as may be 
provided by regulations, the Corporation may appoint such 
officers and other employees ag it considers necessary for the 
purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act: 


Provided that no person whose honorarium or maximum 
salary exceeds fifteen hundred rupees per month shall be 
appointed by the Corporation except with the previous 
approval of the State Government. 


8. The Corporation shall be responsible for drawing up 
and implementation of projects for comprehensive develop- 
ment of selected areas in the State with a view to increasing 
agricultural production and ensuring maximum benefits of 
such production to the cultivators.

namely :—

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 
ORDERS 


No. 19686-F.S./FS/14R-14/71.—5th September 
1974.—In exercise of the powers conferred by 
section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 
(Act 10 of 1955), read with the Government of India, 
Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Food), 
order No. G.S.R.316(E), dated the 20th June 1972, 
the Governor is pleased hereby to rescind, with 
effect, from the 5th September 1974, the West Bengal 
Guests Control Order, 1968, published with this 
department order No. 1725-F.S./FS/14R-2/67, dated 
the 5th March 1968, in Part I of the “Calcutta 
Gazette, Extraordinary” of even date, except as 
respects any action taken or anything done or 
omitted to be done thereunder before the said date. 


By order of the Governor, 
S. L. BOSE, 
Jt. Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal. 


No. 19687-F.S./FS/14R-14/71]-Pt.—5th September 
1974.-Whereas the Governor is of opinion that it 
Is necessary so to do for the maintenance and 
increase of supplies essential to the life of community; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred 
by rule 114 of the Defence of India Rules, 1971, the 
Governor is pleased hereby to make the following 
order, namely: 


1. Short title, extent and commencement. 
(1) This order may be called the West Bengal 
Guests Control Order, 1974. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal. 
(3) It shall come into force at once. 


2. Definitions: In this order, unless the context 
otherwise requires, 


(a) “caterer” means the proprietor or other 
person in charge of a catering establishment 
and includes an agent or servant who acts 
on behalf of such caterer; 


(b) “catering establishment” means a_ hotel, 
restaurant, eating house, cafe, tea shop, 
coffee house, free feeding centre, club, 
canteen or railway refershment room and 
includes any other place of a like nature 
open to the public, where food is prepared, 
supplied or consumed; 


(c) “18950 means a person who either himself or 
through any other person undertakes to 
distribute, or provide چا‎ consumption, food 
in a party, entertainment or social or other 
function; 


(d) “institutional establishment” means a hospital, 
Sanatorium, convalescant home, nursing 
home, orphanage, workshouse, infirmary, 
asylum or school providing food and 
includes any other establishments of a like 
nature; 


(e) “prohibited foodstuffs” means cereals and 
their products and all preparations there- 
from and sweetmeats prepared from casein 
(Chhana) and Khoa (Kshir); 


1703 


1704 THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, SEPTEMBER 5, 1974 


#, 


ہے ES‏ نے 


(0 “residential establishment” means a boarding 
apartment house, residential hotel, or 
nurses’ home and includes’-any other 
establishment of a like nature but does 
not include a private household. 


3. Restriction on preparation, consumption and 
Distribution of prohibited foodstuffs: (1) No 
person, or body of persons, acting in concert either 
jointly or severally, other than a caterer at or i 
connection with one or more partiés, entertainments 
or functions, shall, on any one day, either himself 
or themselves, prepare, serve, distribute or provide 
for consumption, or accept or contribute for service 
or distribution for consumption, any prohibited 
foodstuff to more than twenty-five persons (includ- 
ing the host or hosts) at ordinary parties or 
entertainments or social or other functions or to 
more than fifty persons (including the host or hosts) 
in connection with weddings or funerals. 


(2) No caterer at the instance or for the benefit 
of himself or any person in connection with one or 
more of his own or such person’s parties, entertain- 
ments or functions, shall, on any one day, either 
himself or through any other caterer, serve, 
distribute or provide for consumption, or accept 
for service or distribution for consumption, any 
rrohibited foodstuff to more than twenty-five persons 
(including the host or hosts) at ordinary parties 
Or entertainments or social or other functions or to 
more then fifty persons (including the host or hosts) 
in connection with weddings or funerals. 


(3) No person shall accept or consume any 
rrohibited foodstuff at or in connection with any 
party, entertainment, social or other function, 
wedding or funeral where the number of participants 
(including the host or hosts) exceeds twenty-five 
in the case of ordinary parties, entertainments or 
social or other functions, or where such number 
exceeds fifty (including the host or hosts) in the 
case of weddings or funerals: 


] 


.ےہ .0ھ ؤسنسوددوھ 9 کک ص|عحإ٤عےَیر0تن-‏ 


Provided that nothing in this paragraph shall 
apply to; 


(i) parties, cntertainments ہ٣‎ social مہ‎ 
other functions in the premises serving as 
the headquarters of diplomatic or consular 
representatives or governmental missions of 
foreign countries; 


(ii) the proprietor, manger or other person in 
charge of a residental establishment, 
institutional establishment or _ catering 
establlishment serving food to consumers or 
residents in the course of regular business 
and not in connection with any party, 
entertainment or social or other function 
given at the instance of himself or of any 
other person; 


(iii) the distribution of food containing any 
prohibited foodstuff by way of “bhog” or 
“prasad’’ or as part of a recognised religious 
ceremony, in any temple, mosque, 
gurdwara, church or other place of 
religious worship. 


4. Powers of entry, search, seizure, etc: For the 
effective enforcement of the provisions of this order, 
any officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of 
Food and Supplies or a _ police officer of or 
above the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector may, 
when he has reasons to believe that a contravention 
of this order has been, is being or is about to be 
committed, enter and search any premises, interrogate 
any person and seize any article including their 
coverings or containers in respect of which he has 
reason to believe that the contravention has been, is 
being or is about to be committed. 


By order of the Governor, 
S. L. BOSE, 
Jt. Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

HOME DEPARTMENT

ORDER 


No. 7192-P.—2nd September 1974.—Whereas as respects the places 
described in serial Nos. (1) and (2) of the schedule below (hereinafter referred 
to as the said places), the Governor considers it necessary and expedient in 
the public interest as also in the intcrest of the safety and security of the 
suid places that special precautions should be taken to prevent the entry of 
unauthorised persons therein; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by sub-sections (1) and 
(2) of section 6 of the West Bengal Maintenance of Public Order Act, 1972 
(West Ben. Act 150 of 1972), the Governor is pleased hereby— 


(a) to declare the said places to be protected places, and 
(b) to authorise the officers specified in serial No. (3) of the said schedule 


to grant the permission referred to in sub-section (2) of the said 
section in respect of the said places. 


Schedule 


(1) Name of places—The factory premises of the Fertilizer Corporation of 
India Ltd., police-station Sutahata, Haldia, district Midnapore. 

(2) Particulars of the boundaries of the places—North—Calcutta Port 
Commissioners’ Road; east—Irrigation bundh/Approach Road 
towards Patikhali ramp; south—Irrigation bundh on the bank of 
river Hooghly; west—Indian Oil Corporations boundary area. 

(3১ Person authorised to grant permission—({i) General Manager, (ii) Deputy 
General Manager, (iii) Chief Engineer, (iv) Administrative Officer of 
the F.C.I., ডে) Officer-in-charge, C.I.S.F., Haldia site.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 
ORDER 


No. 19794F.S. / FS/14R-18/74.—7th Sctember 1974.—Whereas the Governor 
is of opinion that it is necessary and expedient so to do for maintaining supplies 
of toodgrains and securing their equitable distribution and availability at fair 
prices in the State of West Bengal; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by rule 114 of the 
Defence of India Rules, 1971, the Governor is pleased hereby to make, the 
following Order, namely— 


1. Short title, extent and commencement.—({1) This Order may be called 
the West Bengal Foodgrains (Requisitioning) Order, 1974. 

(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal. 

(3) It shall come into force at once. 


(4) It shall expire on such date not later than the 3150 December 1974 as 
may be notified by the State Government in the Oficial Gazette, but its expiry 
shall not affect its operation as respects things previously done or omitted to 
be done. 


2. Definitions.—In this order, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) “consumer” means a person who purchases foodgrains for consump- 
tion by himself and the members of his family and includes an 
institution or establishment which purchases foodgrains for consump- 
tion by its members, customers and staff; 


(b) “family” includes servants living in the same mess and, in the case of 
an institution or establishment, all its members, customers and staff; 


(০) “foodgrains” means rice or paddy;

(d) “institution” and “establishment” have the same meanings as in the 


West Bengal Rationing Order, 1964; 


(e) “paddy” means rice in the husk; 


({) “procurement agent” means a person who has entered into an agree- 


ment with the State Government for purchase, sale or storage of 
foodgrains on behalf of the State Government and includes the 
Food Corporation of India, established under the Food Corporations 
Act, 1964 (37 of 1964), acting through its officers and agents as an 
agent of the State Government for the purposes of this order; 


(g) “procurement price” has the same meaning as in the West Bengal 


Foodgrains Procurement (Levy) Order, 1973; 


¢h) “producer” means a person who in any capacity grows paddy or causes 


paddy to be grown on land; 


(i) “requiring authority” means the Block Development Officer, Joint Block 


Development Officer, District Controller of Food and Supplies, 
Assistant District Controller of Food and Supplies, Subdivisional 
Controller of Food and Supplies in their respective jurisdictions 
and includes such other officer not below the rank of Inspector in 
the Department of Food and Supplies of the State Government as 
may be appointed by the State Government, by notification in «he 
01000 Gazette, to perform the functions of the requiring authority 
under this order; 


(j) “৮809৮ means rice imported into, or produced out of paddy, in West 


Bengal and includes broken rice, but does not include chira, muri 


or khoi. Jn, : : 


3. Power of the requiring authority to call for accounts and information.— 


Every persgn holding in stock any foodgrains shall, when called upon to do so 
by the requiring authority by an order in writing, furnish— 


(a) a true account of such foodgrains, and 


(b) information regarding the production, storage, acquisition, use or con- 


sumption of such foodgrains in such manner and within such period 
as may be specified in the order and a person, when so called upon, 
shall not, unless permitted by the requiring authority, sell or other- 
wise dispose of such foodgrains or any part thereof. 


4. Power of the requiring authority to direct sale.—({1) Subject to the 


provisions of sub-paragraph (3), the requiring authority may, by an order in 
writing, direct any person, holding in stock any foodgrains, to sell at the pro- 
curement price such quantity of such foodgrains to such person or such pro- 
curement agent or such officer of the State Government and within such period, 
as may be specified in the order. 


(2) Every such order shall specify the following particulars, namely: — 


(a) the quantity, class and grade of foodgrains held in stock by such 
person ; 


(b) the quantity, in respect of which exemption is granted to such person, 


under the provisions of sub-paragraph (3); 


(c) the quantity, class and grade of foodgrains required to be sold by 
such person; and 


(d) the period within which the foodgrains, directed to be sold by such 


person, are to be delivered. 


(3) A producer or consumer ‘mentioned in column 1 of the Table below 


shall, for all or any of the purposes mentioned in column 2 of the Table, be 
entitled to hold in stock the guantity of foodgrains calculated according to the 
scale mentioned in the corresponding entries in column 3 or column 4, as the 
case may be, of the table and the requiring authority shall exempt such pro- 
ducer or cosumer from selling such quantity of foodgrains.

5. Powers of entry, search, seizure, etc.—The requiring authority or any 
officer of the Department of Food and Supplies, Government of West Bengal 
not below the rank of Sub-Inspector, or any police officer not below the rank of 
Assistant Sub-Inspector, or any other officer authorised by the State Govern- 
ment in this behalf, may, with a view to securing compliance with the provi- 
sions of this order or to satisfying himself that the provisions of this order 
have been complied with,— 


(a) inspect or cause to be inspected any book of account or accounts as 
well as any stock of foodgrains belonging to or under the control of 
any person, 


(9) require any person to give any information in his possession in respect 
to any foodgrains, 


(০) stop and search forthwith, with such aid or assistance as may be 
necessary, any person or vehicle or vessel or animal, used or sus- 
pected of being used for delivery of foodgrains from any premises 
where he has reason to believe that foodgrains are stored, 


(d) enter and search, with such aid or assistance as may be necessary, any 
such premiscs, 


(e) seize and remove, with such aid or assistance as may be necessary, 
any stock of foodgrains along with the packages, covering or recep- 
tacles in which such stock is found, and the animals, vehicles or

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


IRRIGATION AND WATERWAYS 
DEPARTMENT 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 16-I.—7th September 1974.—Whereas the Gov- 
emor is of opinion that lands in the area _ included 
within the boundaries specified in Part II of the 
Schedule below (hereinafter referred to as the said 
area) have been benefited or are likely to be benefited 
by irrigation during the Kharif season by the water 
supplied from the irrigation work, namely, the Sahara- 
jore Irrigation Scheme in the district of Purulia, the 
full description whereof is stated in Part I of the 
Schedule below; 


And whereas an Ordinance, namely. the West 
Bengal Irrigation (Imposition of Water Rate) Ordi- 
nance, 1974 (West Ben. Ord. No. VII of 1974) (here- 
[08100 referred to as the said Ordinance), providing 
for a simplified procedure for imposition, assessment 
and collection of water rates in respect of lands 
benefited or likely to be benefited by irrigation ۳۶۰ 
different cultivation seasons by water supplied from 
any irrigation work has since been promulgated by 
the Governor; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by section 4 read with sub-section (1) of section 5 of 
the said Ordinance, and in supersession of all orders 
made under the Bengal Irrigation Act, 1876 (Ben. 
Act III of 1876), determining the rates to be 64 
lor canal water supplied for purposes of irrigation of 
any land in the said area, the Governor is pleased 
1616০ to declare its intention to impose with effect 
tom Ist day of July 1974 in the said area a water 
‘ate for Kharif season every year.

lime to time and that he never acquired any 
permanency. The Company stated in their

him with effect from 11th September 1973 is 
8. 01060 2 To what relief, if anv, is he 
entitled £ 

On that very day notices were issued under 

Rule 20D of the West Bengal Industrial Dispuies 

Rules, 1958, requiring the parties to appear before 

this Tribuaa!l on 21st June 1974 and submit their 

written staiement. iif appears that the said 
nolices were sent under registered cover with

11168 parties. On 21st June 1974, the concerned

but none appesred on belialf of the Company nor

fling the written statement by the workman.

to file wrilten statement on behalf of the 
workman. On 26th July 1974 Shri Biswas filed 

the written sfatement, but as the management did 

not entered cppearance, the matter was placed [01 

ex parte hearing today.

In order lb) substantiate the issue Shri Biswas 
examined Shri Manilal Kundu as P. W. ‘lag coms

PART.V —Acts of the Parliament of India assented to by the President and Acts enacted and Ordinances 
promulgated by the President 


GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS 


(Legislative Department) 


The following Act of Parliament received the assent of 
the President on the 13th March, 1974, and is hereby pub- 
lished for general information: — 


THE ESSO (ACQUISITION OF UNDERTAKINGS IN INDIA) 
ACT, 1974 


No. 4 oF 1974 
: [73th March, 1974.] 


An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the 
right, title and interest of Esso Eastern. Inc. in relation 
to its undertakings in India with a view to ensuring co- 
ordinated distrtbutton and utilisation of petroleum 
products distributed and marketed in India by Esso 
Eastern Inc. and for matters connected therewith or 
incidental thereto. 


WHEREAS Esso Eastern Inc., a foreign company, is carry- 
ing on, in India the business of distributing and marketing 
petroleum products manutactured by Esso Standard Refining 
Company of India Limited and Lube India Limited, and has, 
for that purpose, established places of business at Bombay 
and other places in India; 


AND WHEREAS it is expedient in the public interest that 
the undertakings, tn India, of Esso Eastern Inc. should be 
acquired in order (0 ensure that the ownership and control 
of the petroleum products distributed and marketed in India 
by the said company are vested in the State and thereby so 
distributed as best to subserve the common good ;

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fifth Year of 
the Republic of India as follows ;— 


CHAPTER 1آ‎ 
PRELIMINARY 


Short title. 1. This Act may be called the Esso (Acquisition of 
Undertakings in India) Act, 1974. 


Definition. 2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) “appointed day” means the date of commencement 
of this Act; 


(b) ‘‘Esso”’ means Esso Eastern Inc., a foreign company 
within the meaning of section 59! of the Companies 
Act, 1956, incorporated under the laws of the 
State of Delaware in the United States of America, 
and having its principal office at 2401 South 
Gessner, City of Houston, State of Texas, in the 
United States of America ; 


(c) “Esso Standard’’ means’ Esso Standard Refining 
Company of India Limited, being a company as 
defined in the Companies Act, 1956, and having its 
registered office at Administration Building, Mahul, 
Bombay 400074 ; 


(d) “Government company’’ means a company as defined 
in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956 ; 


(6) “Lube India” means Lube India Limited, being a 
company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956, 
and having its registered office at Administration 
Building, Corridor Road, Mahul, Bombay 400074 ; 


(/) “notification” means a notification published in the 
Official Gazette ; 


(g) “prescribed” means prescribed by rules made under 
this Act. 


a CHAPTER 1

and vest- Esso, in relation to its undertakings in India, shall stand

CHAPTER 1 


PROVISIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYEES OF 550 


8. (7) Every whole-time officer or other employee )مہ‎ 
Esso who was, immediately before the appointed day, em- 
ployed by Esso in connection with its undertakings in India, 
and every whole-time officer or other employee of Esso who 
wao was, immediately before the appointed day, temporarily 
holding any assignment outside India, shall, on the appointed 
day, become an officer or other employee, as the case may be, 
of the Central Government or, as the case may be, the Govern-. 
ment company in which the right, title and interest of Esso 
in relation to its undertakings in India have vested under this 
Act and shall hold office or service under the Central Govern- 
ment or the Government company, as the case may be, on 
the same terms and conditions and with the same rights to 
pension, gratuity and other matters as would have been 
admissible to him if there had been no such vesting and shall 
continue to do so unless and until his employment under the 
Central Government or the Government company, as the 
case may be, is duly terminated or until his remuneration and 
conditions of service are duly altered by the Central Govern- 
ment or the Government company, as the case may be.

15. (/) Where an offence under this Act has been com- 
mitted by a company, every person who at the time the 
offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible 
to, the company for the conduct of the business of the com- 
pany, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty’ 
of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and 
punished accordingly: 


Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall 
render any such person liable to any punishment, if he proves 
that the offence was committed without his knowledge or 
that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the com- 
mission of such offence. 


(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (J), 
where any offence under this Act has been committed by a 
company and it is proved that the offence has been com- 
mitted with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable 
to, any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary 
or other oflicer of the company, such director, manager, 
secretary or other officer shall be deemed to be guilty of that 
offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and 
punished accordingly. 


E.rplanation.—-For the purposes of this section— 


(a) “company” means any body corporate and includes 
a firm or other association of individuals; and 


(b) ‘‘director’’, in relation to a firm, means a partner in 
the firm.

pany or any of its officers or other employees for anything 


which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this 
Act. 


17. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1898, no court shall take cognizance of 
any Offence against this Act except on a complaint, in writing, 
made by the Central Government or any officer authorised in 
this behalf by that Government. 


18, Every officer of the Central Government and every 
officer or other employee of the Government company shall 
be indemnified by the Central Government or the Govern- 
ment company, as the case may be, against all losses and 
expenses incurred by him in, or in relation to, the discharge 
of his duties under this Act except such as have been caused 
by his own wilful act or default.

‘ferred by section 4 of the Departmental Proceed- 
ings (Enforcement of Attendance of Witnesses 
and Production of Documents) Act, 1973, the

Banerjee,, WBHJS, Commissioner for Depart-

said Act in relating to any person within such. 
class or category of persons.

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 


Treasury, etc. 
GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 


ORDER 


No. 19960-F.S./FS/14R-17/74.—17th September 1974.—Whereas _ the 
Governor is of opinion that it is necessary and expedient so to do for maintain- 
ing supplies of rice and securing its equitable distribution and availability at 
fair prices in West Bengal; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by rule 114 of the 
Defence of India Rules, 1971, the Governor is pleased hereby to make, with 
the prio concurrences of the Central Government, the following Order, 
namely: — 


1. Short title, extent and commencement.—(1) This Order may be called 
the West Bengal Rice (Restrictions on Movement) Order, 1974. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal, except the areas in which the 
West Bengal Rationing Order, 1964, is in force. 


(3) It shall come into force at once. 


(4) It shall expire on such date as may be notified by the State Government 
in the Official Gazette, but its expiry shall not affect its operation as respects 
things previously done or omitted to be done. 


2. Definitions.—In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) ‘‘Controller” means, in respect of any area, the Subdivisional Controller 
of Food and Supplies in the Department of Food and Supplies, 
Government of West Bengal, having jurisdiction in such area, and 
includes such other Officer of the State Government not below the 
rank of Inspector in the Department of Food and Supplies as may 
be authorised by the State Government by notification in the 
Official Gazette to perform the functions of the Controller under 
015 01061 in respect of such area as may be specified in the noti- 
fication; 


(b) “rice” includes broken rice but does not include chira, muri and khot; 
(c) “transport” means to move or Cause to be moved by any motor vehicle 
or inland vessel or by rail. 


17998 


1732 THE CAICUTA GAZETTE, EXTRA ORDINARY, SEPTEMBER 17 1974 [Parr | 


Lid

3, Restrictions on transport of rice.—No person shall transport any rice 
from any place within a district to any place outside it except under and in 
accordance with a permit granted by the Controller; 


Provided that nothing in this paragraph shall apply to transport of rice not 
exceeding 2 kilogfams in weight by a bona fide traveller for his personal 
consumption. 


4. Savings.—Nothing in this Order shall apply to transport of any rice— 


(i) by, or on account of, or on behalf of, or on the authority of, the State 
Government or the Central Government or the Food Corporation of 
ee established under the Food Corporations Act, 1964 (Act 37 of 
1964(۰ 


(ii) Covered by a permit or a written authority or an order of exemption 
issued by a competent authority under any order made under 
section 3 of the Essential Commodities#Act, 1955 (Act 10 of 1955); 


(iii) under and in accordance with military credit notes or certificates: 


ny river in West Bengal, 
quired for their, bona fide

(iv) by the crew of any inland vessel plying i 
not exceeding such quantity as may be 
consumption calculated at the scale of 
grams of paddy per head per day for a 


5. Powers of entry, search, seizure, etc.—The Controller or any Officer of 
the Department of Food and Supplies, not below the rank of Sub-Inspector or 
any Police Officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector or such other 
Officer of the State Government as may be authorised by the State Government 
in this behalf, may, with a view to securing compliance with this Order, or to 
satisfying himself that this Order has been complied with, with such aid or 
assistance as he thinks fit,— 


(a) stop and search any vessel found in inland waterways, or any motor 
vehicle used or capable of being used for the transport of rice; 


(b) inspect any document relating to transport of rice; 
(c) enter and search any premises or place; 


(৫) seize and remove any article i) respect of which he has reason to 
believe that any provision of this Order has been, is being or is 
about to be contravened, along with the packages, coverings or 
receptacles in which such article is found and the vehicles or vessels 
used in carrying such articles and thereafter take or authorise the 
taking of all measures necessary for securing the production of the 
article, packages, coverings, receptacles, vehicles or vessels so seized, 
before a Magistrate without delay and for their safe custody 
pending such production. 


By order of the Governor, 
S. B. RAY, 
Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

THE WEST BENGAL PRIMARY EDUCATION 
ACT, 1973. 


[Passed by the West Bengal Legislature. | 


{Assent of the President was first published in the Calcutta 
Gazette, 20420721122, of the 20th September, 1974.] 


An Act to make better provision for the development, expan- 
sion, management and control of primary education with 
a view to making it universal, free and compulsory. 


WHEREAS it is expedient to make better provision for the 
development, expansion, management and control of primary 
education with a view to making it universal, free and com- 
pulsory ; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fourth Year of the 
না of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 
ollows:— 


PART I 


CHAPTER I 


Preliminary 


1. (1) This Act may be called the West Bengal Primary 
Education Act, 1973. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal. 


(3) It shall come into force in such arcas and oa such dates 
as the State Government may, by notification, appoint and 
different dates may be appointed for different areas or for 
different provisions of this Act. 


2. In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the 
subject or context,— 


(i) ‘‘attendance” at a school means présence for instruc- 
tion at a primary school for so many days ia a 
school year and at such time or times on each day 
of attendance as may be required by the prescribed 
educational! authority ; 


(ii) “Board” means the West Bengal Board of Primary 
Education established under this Act; 


(iit) ‘‘Calcutta” means Ca!cutta as defined in the Calcutta 
Municipal Act, 1951; 


(10) “Chairman’’ means the Chairman of a_ Primary 
School Council ; 


(v) “child” means a boy or girl who has completed six 
but not eleven years of age at the beginning of a 
school year: 


Provided that a boy or girl who completes six years of 
age within ninety days from the beginning of a 
school year shall be deemed to be a child; 


(vi) “Director” means the Director of Public Instruction, 
Government of West Bengal ;

The West Bengal Primary Education Act, 1973. 
(Part 1f.—Chapter I1.—The Board.—Sections 3, 4.) 


PART Il 
CHAPTER II 


The Board 


3. (1) The State Government shall, by notificat.on, 
establish, with effect from such date as may be specified in 
the notification, a Board to be called the West Bengal Board 
of Primary Education. 


(2) The Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual 
succession and a common Seal, shall be entitled to acquire, 
hold and dispose of property, to enter into contracts ana to 
do all other things necessary for the purposes of this Act, and 
shall by its corporate name sue and be sued. 


4. The Board shall consist of the following members, 
namely: — 
(2) an officer not below the rank of a Deputy Director of 
Public Instruction, Government of West Bengal, to 
be nominated by the State Government; 


(b) two teachers of Junior Basic Training Institutions, of 
whom one shall be the head of one such Institu- 
tion, elected in the prescribed manner by the 
teachers of Junior Basic Training Institutions from 
amongst themselves ; 


(c) eight teachers of primary schools of whom at least 
two shall be women, elected in the prescribed 
manner in accordance with the system of propor- 
tional representation by means of the single 
transferable vote by the members of the Primary 
school Councils who are representatives of teachers 
of primary schools in Primary School Councils; 


(9) one person elected in the prescribed manner by the 
Councillors of the Calcutta Corporation ; 


(৫) four persons elected in the prescribed manner in 
accordance with the system of proportional repre- 
sentation by means of the single transferable vote 
by the Commissioners of municipalities ; 


(f) three persons clected in the prescribed manner in 
accordance with the system of proportional repre- 
sentation by means of the single transferable vote 
by the members of the Zula Parishads ; 


(g) two members from each of the districts of Midnapore 
and 24-Parganas and one member from each of the 
other districts, from among the members of the 
West Bengal Legislative Assembly elected in the 
prescribed manner by the members of the 
Assembly from that district and one member from 
Calcutta elected by the members of the Assembly 
from Calcutta ; 


(hk) twelve persons interested in education nominated by 
the State Government of whom at least— 


(1) one shall be a woman; 


(ii) one shall be a member of the Anglo-Indian 
Community; 


(iti) one shall be a member of a Scheduled Caste; 


(8৮) one shall be a member of a Scheduled Tribe;

44. (1) There shall be a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman of 
a Primary School Council. 


(2) The Chairman and the Vice-Chairman shall be 
elected by the members of the Primary School Council from 
among themselves in such manner as may be prescribed and 
shall, subject to the provisions of section 45, hold office for 
a term of four years mentioned in section 42: 


Provided that until a Chairman is elected by the members 
of the Primary School Council for the first time the State 
Government may appoint a person to be the Chairman of 
the Primary School Council and the person so appointed shall 
hold office until a Chairman is elected by the members of the 
Primary School Council and assumes office. 


(3) The Chairman and the Vice-Chairman shall receive 
such pay or allowances or both as may be fixed by the State 
Government. 


(4) The Chairman may resign his office by giving notice 
in writing to the Primary School Council and when such 
resignation is accepted by the Primary School Council the 
Chairman shall be deemed to have vacated his office. 


(5) The Vice-Chairman may resign his office by giving 
notice in writing to the Chairman and when such resignation 
15 accepted by the Chairman the Vice-Chairman shall be 
deemed to have vacated his office, 


45. If at a meeting of the Primary School Council specially, 
convened for the purpose a resolution is passed against the 
Chairman or the Vice-Chairman by a majority of the then 
members of the Primary School Council and by a majority of 
not less than two-thirds of the members of the Primary 
School Council present and voting such resolution shall have 
the effect of reinoving the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman, 
as the case may be, from his office as from the date on which 
the resolution is so passed. 


46. (1) (a) In the event of the occurrence of any vacancy 
in the office of the Chairman by reason of his death, resigna- 
tion or removal, or otherwise, or, 


(b) when the Chairman is unable to discharge his func- 
tions owing to absence, illness or any other cause, 
the Vice-Chairman shall exercise the powers, perform the 
functions and discharge the duties of the Chairman until a 
new Chairman is elected and assumes office or until the 
Chairman resumes his duties, as the case may be. 


(2) In the event of the occurrence of vacancies in the 
offices of both the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman the State 
Government may appoint a member of the Primary School 
Council to exercise the powers, perform the functions and 
discharge the duties of the Chairman until a Chairman or a 
Vice-Chairman is elected and assumes office.

CHAPTER VII 
Committees of the Primary School Council 


67. (1) As soon as may be after a Primary School Council 
is established it shall constitute the following Committees; 
namely :— 

(a) the Recognition Committee; 

(b) the Staff Selection Committee; 

(c) the Finance Committee; 

(d) the Discipline Committee; , 

(e) the Appeal Committee; 

(f) the Development Committee. 


(2) The constitution, powers and functions of a Committee 
shall be such as may be prescribed, 


68, (1) A Primary School Council may, with the approval 
of the State Government and subject to such directions as 
the State Government may issue in this behalf, constitute such 
other Committee or Committees as it may think fit and any 
such Committee may be composed wholly or in part of mem- 
bers of the Primary School Council. 


(2) A Primary School Counci] may, with the approval of 
the State Government, delegate to any such Committee any 
of its powers and functions and may in like manner withdraw 
from it any such power or function. 


(3) A Primary School Council may, with the approval of 
the State Government, dissolve any of the Committees referred 
to in sub-section (J) of section 67 or constituted under sub- 
section (4) of this section. 


CHAPTER VIII 
Fimance and audit 


68. (1) Every Primary School 0000] shall in each year 
prepare in the prescribed form a budget estimate of income 
and expenditure of the Primary School Council for the ensu- 
ing financial year, and shall submit the budget estimate to the 
State Government through the Director on or before the 
thirtieth day of November. 


(2) The State Government may either approve of the 
budget estimate as it stands, or approve of it after making 
such alterations, if any, as it may think fit or may cause it 
to be returned to the Primary School Council for such modi- 
fications as the State Government may think necessary, and 
when such modifications have been made, the budget estimate 
shall be re-submitted for approval to the State Government.

CHAPTER XIV 


Miscellaneous 


99. (J) The State Government may, by an order in 
writing specifying the reasons therefor, temporarily suspend 
the execution of any resolution or order of the Board or a 
Primary School Council or of any Committee of the Board 
or the Primary School Council or temporarily prohibit the 
doing of any act by it which 1s purported or intended to be 
done under this Act, if the State Government is of opinion 
that such resolution, order or act is in excess of the powers 
conferred by or under this Act upon the Board, the Primary 
School Council or the Committee, as the case may be. 


(2) When any order is made under sub-section (J), the 
State Government shall give the Board, the Primary School 
Council or the Committee of the Board or the Primary! 
School Council an opportunity to express its views on such 
order and after considering the views of the Board, the 
Primary School Council or the Committee, as the case may 
be, revoke or confirm such order. 


100. (J) The State Government may, from time to 
time, cause enquiry to be made by any person in regard to the 
Board or a Primary School Council on matters connected with 
primary education or any matter with respect to which the 
sanction, approval, consent or order of the State Government 
is required by or under this Act. 


(2) The person holding such enquiry shall have the powers 
of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, 
to take evidence and to compel the attendance of witnesses, 
and the production of documents for the purpose of enquiry. 


(3) The State Government may make orders as to the cost 
of enquiry made under sub-section (1) and as to the party by 
whom and the funds out of which such costs shall be paid 
and such orders may on the application of the State Govern- 
ment or the person named therein be executed as if it were 
a decree of a Civil Court. 


101. The members of the Board, the Primary School 
Councils, or the Committees of the Board or the Primary 
School Councils, persons in the service of the Board, the 
Primary School Councils or such Committees and any person, 
appointed under this Act to audit the accounts of the Board 
or of a Primary School Council or to perform any other 
duties under this Act or the rules and regulations made there- 
under shall be deemed, when acting or purporting to act in 
the discharge of their duties o1 the exercise of their powers 
under this Act or under the rules and regulations made there- 
under, to be public servants within the meaning of section 2] 
of the Indian Penal Code. 


102. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding 
whatsoever shall lie against any person for anything in good 
faith done or intended to be done under this Act.

district.

Urban Primary Education Act, 1963, shall be deemed to have 
been recognised under this Act until the expiration of the 
period of recognition subject, however, to the power of the 
Primary School Council having jurisdiction to withdraw 
recognition in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

to him under this Act shall be deemed to be salary paid to 
him in arrears and the provisions of sub-section (J) of section 
89 of that Act shall apply accordingly. 


Erplanation.—In this section, ‘‘previous year’ and “total 
income’’ have the meanings respectively assigned to them in 
the Income-tax Act, 1961.

offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punish- 
ed accordingly.

RULES 

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These rules may be called the West 

Prevention and Control of Water Pollution (Conduct of Business) Rules,‏ ا 


(2) They shall come into force on 20th September 1974.

2. Definitions —In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the 
subject or context,— 


(a) “the Act” means the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 
, 


(b) “Board” means the We:i Bengal Prevention and Control of Water 
Pollution Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 4; 


(০) “Chairman” means the Chairman of the Board; 

(d) ‘‘member” means a member of the Board; 

(e) ‘““Member-Secretary” means a Member-Secretary of the Board; 
(f) “section” means a section of the Act. 


3. Meetings.—{1) The place, date and time of a meeting shall be fixed by 
the Member-Secretary with the approval of the Chairman. 


(2) A notice of each meeting indicating place, date and time of the meet- 
ing shall be sent by tne Member-Secretary to each member at least ten days 
before the date of the meeting: 


Provided that the Chairman may at any time call a meeting at forty-eight 
hours’ notice to transact any business which in his opinion is of an urgent 
nature 


(3) A copy of the agenda of the meeting and where necesssry 2 copy of 
the explanatory note on the items of discussion shall be sent to each member 
before the meeting: 


Provided that in case of a meeting for the consideration of the Budget 
Estimate for the ensuing financial year and the Revised Estimate for the current 
financial year the notice shall be accompanied by a copy of the draft estimate 
and by a note sufficient to explain the estimates. 


(4) No resolution of the Board shall be invalid only on the ground that 
insufficient notice of the meeting or agenda has been given. 


(5) If at any meeting one-third cf the members present object to the deter- 
mination of any question on the ground of insufficiency of notice, the Chairman 
shall postpone the discussion of that question to the next meeting, and if any 
objection is made by any member before the proceedings are confirmed at the 
next meeting, the Chairman shall lay the objection before the Board for deci- 
sion when the proceedings are placed on the table for confirmation. 


4, Quorum.—The quorum of any meeting of the Board shall be one-third 
of the total number of the members for the time being of the Board. 


5. President of the meeting.—The Chairman shall preside over every meet- 
ing and in his absence the members present shall elect one from among them- 
selves to preside over the meeting. 


6. Adjourned meeting.—If at any meeting no quorum is present, the Chair- 
man or the member who presides over the meeting shall, subject to the provi- 
sion of sub-rule (2) of rule 7, adjourned the mceting to such date and time as 
he thinks fit and at such adjourned meeting any number of members present 
shall form the quorum. 


7. Business to be transacted at an adjourned mecting.—(1) At an adjourned 
meeting no business shall be transacted other than that which was fixed for 
the meeting originally convened. 


(2) Not less than seven days’ notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given 
to all members of the Board including those who were absent from the 
meeting. 


8, Casting vote.—In the event of an equality of votes the Chairman or the 
member presiding cver the meeting shall have a second or casting vote. 


9, Consideration of additional [নাজ in this rule shall prevent 
any subject being considered at the meeting although no notice of such subject 
has been circulated, provided the members present unanimously agree to 
consider that subject.

10. Decisions to be taken by majority of votes.—All questions which come 
before the members at a meeting shall be decided by the majority of votes of 
the members present and each member shall have one vote. Voting by proxy 
shall not be permitted. 


11. Minutes of meetings.—{1) The minutes of every meeting and the resolu- 
tion passed thereat shall be recorded by the President of the meeting who may 
be assisted in this regard by the Member-Secretary. 


(2) Copies of the minutes shall be circulated to all members before the next 
meeting. 

12. Confirmation of minutes of the meeting—(1) The minutes of every 
meeting shall be laid before the next succeeding meeting for confirmation. 


(2) The Board may refuse to confirm the minutes or any part thereof of 
any meeting on any of the following grounds, namely: 


(a) that the notice prescribed was not sent to every member; 
(b) that the minutes have not been correctly recorded; 


(c) that any resolution recorded at an adjourned meeting did not relate 
to any part of the business to be transacted at the original meeting. 


(3) If any objection is raised by a member to the confirmation of the 
minutes or any part thereof on any of the grounds specified in sub-rule (2), 
the President of the meeting shall in any case of doubt put the matter to vote, 


By order of the Governor,
